The resulting infection, called cysticercosis, can cause disease in various organs including the muscles, skin, eyes and brain, which can lead to serious health consequences. When the cysts are in the brain, this condition is called neurocysticercosis. Symptoms: Taeniasis is often characterized by non-specific symptoms that are difficult to associate with the infection (abdominal pain, nausea, diarrhoea, etc.). These symptoms can persist until the parasite dies following treatment, or they can last for several years.

translations.source: Game da cutar cushewar ciki, lokacin yin ƙyanƙyansa kan bambanta, sannan kuma masu fama da matsalar za su ci gaba da kasancewa ba tare da wata alama ba tsawon shekaru. A wasu wuraren da suka fama da annoba, waɗanda suka kamu ka iya siffantuwa da wasu abubuwa da za a iya gani (abun da za iya taɓawa) a ƙasan fata. Kumburin ƙwaƙwalwa na bayyan ne da alamomi iri-iri, ya danganta ga da adadi da girma da mataki da kuma wurin da cutar ta fito da kuma yadda garkuwar jiki ta bayar da kariya da ƙwayar halittar mai cutar, sai dai za ta iya kasancewa ba ta nuna wata alama ba. Alamomin wannan cuta za su iya kasncewa matsanancin ciwo kai da makanta da farfaɗiya da taruwar ruwa a ƙwaƙwalwa da zazzaɓi da cutar mantuwa da kum sauran alamomin da raunin ya fito a ƙwaƙwalwa ya haifar. Magani: Maganin dauɗar ciki na da muhimmanci wajen hana aukuwar cutar kumburi da jan ruwan ƙwaƙwalwa a matasayin wata hanya ta hana ko tsakayar da hana yaɗuwar ƙwayoyin cuta. Za a iya yin magani dangane da yanayin mutane daban-daban ko ta yawan shan magani bisa ga yanayi wuri da kuma hanyar dakatar da yaɗuwar cutar da ka yi amfani da ita. za a iya maganin cutar dauɗar ciki ta hanyar amfani da maganin macijin ciki. Game da matsalar kumburi da jan ruwan ƙwaƙwalwa, fashewar ruwan kan iya yi zafi, ana buƙatar magani cuta na musamman, wanda ka iya ɗaukar matakai masu tsayi da kuma shan maganin macijin ciki ko allura mai yawa da kuma sauran magungunan farfaɗiya da kuma yuwuwar yin aiki. Yawan magani da tsawon lokacin da za a ɗauka ana sha ya danganta da adadi da girma da wuri da kuma matakin kumburin da zafin kumburin da tsininsa da tsananinsa da kuma alamominsa.
translations.reference: For cysticercosis, the incubation period is variable, and infected people may remain asymptomatic for years. In some endemic regions, infected people may develop visible or palpable nodules (a small solid bump or node which is solid that can be detected by touch) beneath the skin. Neurocysticercosis is associated with a variety of signs and symptoms depending on the number, size, stage and location of the pathological changes as well as the host’s immune response and the parasite’s genotype, but it can also be clinically asymptomatic. Symptoms may include chronic headaches, blindness, seizures (epilepsy if they are recurrent), hydrocephalus, meningitis, dementia and symptoms caused by lesions occupying spaces of the central nervous system. Treatment: The treatment of taeniasis by Taenia solium is important to prevent neurocysticercosis and as a tool to assist in controlling or stopping the parasite transmission cycle. The treatment can be done on an individual bases, or as Mass Drug Administration depending on the local circumstances and the control approaches being implemented. Taeniasis can be treated using anthelmintics (Praziquantel, Niclosamide, Albendazole). In neurocysticercosis, since the destruction of cysts may lead to an inflammatory response, specialised treatment of active disease is required and may include long courses with high doses of anthelmintic, as well as supporting therapy with corticosteroids and/or anti-epileptic drugs, and possibly surgery. The dosage and the duration of treatment can vary greatly and depend mainly on the number, size, location and developmental stage of the cysts, their surrounding inflammatory edema, acuteness and severity of clinical symptoms or signs.
translations.hypothesis: For cystic echinococcosis, the incubation period is variable and asymptomatic cases are frequent, with the majority of patients remaining unaffected for several years. In endemic areas, infected individuals may also exhibit various skin lesions (nodules, maculae, papules) that are sometimes confused with other skin conditions. Lesions can be asymptomatic or cause a range of symptoms, depending on the number, size, location and stage of the cysts, and the immune response and virulence of the parasite, but may also be totally asymptomatic. Symptoms can include severe headaches, neck stiffness, fever, altered consciousness, seizures, and neurological signs that reflect the part of the brain affected. Treatment: Anticonvulsant drugs are useful in preventing or limiting seizures and are an important part of the treatment to control the spread of infection. Treatment can be empirical, based on the patient’s clinical condition, or targeted according to the causative agent and the means of transmission used. Cystic echinococcosis can be treated with anti-infective drugs. For cerebral echinococcosis, the cysts can cause severe morbidity and require specific treatment, which can be long and complex, involving anti-infective drugs, percutaneous treatment of the hydatid cysts with the PAIR (Puncture, Aspiration, Injection, Re-aspiration) technique, and various surgical options. The drug dosage and duration of treatment depend on the number, size, location and stage of the cysts, the severity of the clinical condition and the drug’s adverse effects.

translations.source: Cutar tetanos ƙarin bayan: Ttetanos babbar cuta ce da ake ɗauka daga wasu ƙwayoyin halitta da ke rayuwa a cikin ƙasa da yawu da kuma taki. ƙwayar halittar na shiga jikin mutum ne ta hanyar wani yanka mai zurfi ko ciwo ko ƙonuwa da yake shafar ƙwaƙwalwa. Cutar kan haifar da ciwo a jiki, musamman muƙamuƙi da wuya, wanda aka fi sani da lockjaw. Kowane rukuni na mutane ka iya kamuwa da cutar tetanos, to amma cutar ta fi yawa da tsanani ga jariari da iyayensu, a yayin da uwar ba ta samu kari daga cutar ba ta hanyar allura,. Cutar tetanos da ta kama mai juna biya ko kuma mako 6 kafin haihuwa ana kiran ta da cutar tetano ta uwa, yayin da wadda yaro ya kamu da ita a lokacin da yake da kawana 28 ana kiran ta da tetanos ta lokacin haihuwa. Cutar tetanos na ɗaya daga cikin manyan cututtuka da ke addabar sassa daban-daban na duniya, musamman ƙasashe mara arziki, inda ba a samun wadatar kulawa da garkuwr jiki da yawan al'adun rashin zabta a yayin haihuwa. Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya ta yi sashe a 2018 cewa (wadda ita ce shekara mafi ƙaranci da aka yi hasashen), kimanin jarirai 25,000 ne ke mutuwa bayan haihuwarsu sakamakon cutar tetanos, inda aka samu raguwar kaso 88% a 2000. Alamomi: Kusan dukkan matsalar cutar tetabos na furuwa ne ga mutanen da ba taɓa yi musu allura ko manyan da ba su sake yin allura bayan wadda suka yi a baya. Alamomin cutar tetanos kan iya bayyana kowane lokaci daga kwana 3 zuwa 21 da shigar ƙwayar cutar jikin mutum ta hanyar rauni da ya ji .
translations.reference: Tetanus Overview: Tetanus is a serious illness contracted through exposure to the spores of the bacterium, Clostridium tetani, which live in soil, saliva, dust and manure. The bacteria can enter the body through a deep cuts, wounds or burns affecting the nervous system. The infection leads to painful muscle contractions, particularly of the jaw and neck muscle, and is commonly known as “lockjaw”. People of all ages can get tetanus but the disease is particularly common and serious in newborn babies and their mothers when the mother is unprotected from tetanus by the vaccine, tetanus toxoid. Tetanus occurring during pregnancy or within 6 weeks of the end of pregnancy is called maternal tetanus, while tetanus occurring within the first 28 days of life is called neonatal tetanus. The disease remains an important public health problem in many parts of the world, but especially in low-income countries or districts, where immunization coverage is low and unclean birth practices are common. WHO estimates that in 2018 (the latest year for which estimates are available), 25 000 newborns died from neonatal tetanus, 88% reduction from the situation in 2000. Symptoms: Nearly all cases of tetanus occur in people who have never been vaccinated or in adults who have not kept up to date on their booster shots. Signs and symptoms of tetanus appear anytime from 3 to 21 days after tetanus bacteria enter the body through a wound.
translations.hypothesis: Tetanus Overview: Tetanus is a serious infection that is caused by bacteria living in soil and animal waste. The bacteria enter the body through deep wounds, injuries or even small skin breaks and affect the nervous system. The disease causes stiffness in the body, especially the neck and jaw muscles, which is why it is also known as lockjaw. Anyone can get tetanus, but it is most common and severe in newborns and their mothers, when the mother is not immune from vaccination. Tetanus that occurs in the 2 to 6 weeks before birth is called maternal tetanus, while tetanus that occurs in a newborn is called neonatal tetanus. Tetanus is one of the most common diseases affecting different parts of the world, particularly low- and middle-income countries, where there is often a lack of access to quality health care and high rates of unsafe births. WHO estimates that in 2018 (the latest year for which data are available), about 25 000 newborns died from neonatal tetanus, a reduction of 88% since 2000. Symptoms: All cases of tetanus occur in people who are unvaccinated or in adults who have not received a booster dose of the vaccine. Symptoms of tetanus may appear anywhere from 3 to 21 days after the bacteria enter the body through a wound.

translations.source: Yawancin cutar na bayyana ne cikin kwana 21. Alamomin sun ƙunshi: ƙagewar muƙamuƙi da kasa buɗe baki ƙagewar jiki, musamman baya da ciki da tafin hannu da na ƙafa ƙagewar jiki da kuma jin zafi na faruwa ne sakamakon ƙara wahala wajen yin haɗiya suma ciwon kai zazzaɓi da zufa Sauyawar hawan jini ko kuma saurin bugawar zuciya.
translations.reference: Most cases occur within 14 days. Symptoms can include: jaw cramping or the inability to open the mouth muscle spasms often in the back, abdomen and extremities sudden painful muscle spasms often triggered by sudden noises trouble swallowing seizures headache fever and sweating changes in blood pressure or fast heart rate.
translations.hypothesis: Onset of symptoms usually occurs within 21 days. Symptoms include: stiffness of the neck and difficulty opening the mouth stiffness in the back, shoulders, arms and legs; muscle aches and pains, which increase with movement; headache; fever; chills; nausea; vomiting; constipation; difficulty breathing; swelling of the face, neck, chest and extremities; rapid heart rate; low blood pressure; and seizures.

translations.source: A tetanos ɗin lokacin haihuwa, alamomin kan haɗa da ƙagewar jiki, wanda yawanci ke gabatar kasa tsotsar nonon jariri da kuma yawan kuka. Ana tabbatar da cutar tetanos dangane da alamu ba tare da buƙatar yin gwaji ba. Cutar tetanos na buƙatar kulawar asibiti, musamman tura zuwa wani asibitin. Mutanen da suka samu sauƙi daga cutar tetanos ba su da garkuwar jiki ta halicci, sannan kuma za su iya sake kamuwa, don haka suna buƙatar riga-kafi. Kariya: Za a iya samun kariya daga cutar tetanos ta hanyar yin riga-kafi da alluaran da ke kashe ta, waɗanda ake amfani da su a lokacin shirin zagayen riga-kafi na duniya da yin ta a yayin da ake zuwa duba lafiyar juna-biyu. Idan mutum ba ya so ya kamu da cutar har abada, hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya ta bayar da shawarar cewa, mutum ya riƙa yin allura da ke kashe tetanos sau 6 (na fari 3 da kuma riga-kafi) na alluran da kashe tetanos,. Alluran farko 3 a jere ya kamata a yi su, mako 6 da haihuwa, inda daga bisani bayan yin allurar da mako 4. An fi son yin riga-kafin ta 3 a shekara ta biyu bayan haihuwa (wata 12 zuwa 23) a shekara 4 zuwa 7 da kuma shekara 9 zuwa 15. An fi son a yi aƙalla shekara 4 a tsakanin alluran riga-kafin. Akwai allurai iri daban-daban da za a iya amfani da su wajen samun kariya daga cutar tetanos: allurar kashe tetatnos a lokacin yarinta da ta hana kawuwa da cutar tetanos da alluran hana tari.
translations.reference: In neonatal tetanus, symptoms include muscle spasms, which are often preceded by the newborn’s inability to suck or breastfeed, and excessive crying. Tetanus is diagnosed on the basis of clinical features and does not require laboratory confirmation. Tetanus requires treatment in a medical facility, often in a referral hospital. People who recover from tetanus do not have natural immunity and can be infected again and therefore need to be immunized. Prevention: Tetanus can be prevented through immunization with tetanus-toxoid-containing vaccines (TTCV), which are included in routine immunization programmes globally and administered during antenatal care contacts. To be protected throughout life, WHO recommends that an individual receives 6 doses (3 primary plus 3 booster doses) of TTCV. The 3-dose primary series should begin as early as 6 weeks of age, with subsequent doses given with a minimum interval of 4 weeks between doses. The 3 booster doses should preferably be given during the second year of life (12–23 months), at 4–7 years of age, and at 9–15 years of age. Ideally, there should be at least 4 years between booster doses. There are many kinds of vaccines used to protect against tetanus: diphtheria and tetanus (DT) vaccinesdiphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis (whooping cough) (DTaP) vaccinestetanus and diphtheria (Td) vaccinestetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis (Tdap) vaccines.
translations.hypothesis: In neonatal tetanus, symptoms include stiffness of the body, which is often preceded by difficulty in feeding and irritability. Tetanus is diagnosed based on clinical signs and does not require any specific test. Tetanus requires medical care, and in severe cases, hospitalization. People who have recovered from tetanus remain susceptible to the toxin and can contract the disease again, so they need to be vaccinated. Prevention: Tetanus can be prevented through vaccination with a toxoid, which is included in all WHO-recommended childhood immunization programmes and is also given during pregnancy. If lifelong protection is desired, WHO recommends a 6-dose primary vaccination series with tetanus toxoid-containing vaccine. The first 3 doses should be given as a series, starting at 6 weeks of age, with subsequent doses given 4 weeks apart. The diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis (DTP) vaccines are preferred for the 3 primary doses, given at 6 weeks, 10 weeks and 14 weeks of age. A booster dose is recommended at age 12–23 months, 4–7 years and 9–15 years. At least 4 years should ideally separate booster doses. There are several different vaccines that can be used to prevent tetanus: tetanus toxoid-containing childhood vaccines, diphtheria-tetanus vaccines and booster vaccines.

translations.source: Za a iya kauce wa kamuwa da cutar tetanos ta lokacin haihuwa, ta hanyar yi wa mata da suka kai shekarun haihuwa riga-kafi da alluran kashe cutar tetanos kodai a lokacin da suke da juna biyu ko bayan haihuwa. Haka kuma, yawan kula da lafiya a-kai-a-kai ka iya hana kamuwa da cutar tetanos, wanda ya haɗa tsafta lokacin haihuwa da kula da lafiyar jariri yayin haihuwa da kula da rauni wajen yin tiyata da kuma aikin haƙori.
translations.reference: Neonatal tetanus can be prevented by immunizing women of reproductive age with TTCV, either during pregnancy or outside of pregnancy. Additionally, robust medical practices can also prevent tetanus disease including clean delivery and cord care during childbirth, and proper wound care for surgical and dental procedures.
translations.hypothesis: Neonatal tetanus can be prevented by vaccinating women of reproductive age with tetanus-containing vaccines during pregnancy or just after birth. Additionally, good hygiene practices can prevent tetanus, including clean delivery practices, good neonatal care, and proper wound and dental care.

translations.source: Cutar kumburin ƙwaƙwalwa ƙarin bayani: Cutar ƙwaƙwalwa na ɗaya daga cikin muhimman abubuwan da suke haifar da cuta a ƙwaƙwalwa a gabashi da tsakiya da arewaci kuma yake ci gaba ƙaruwa yammacin ƙasashen Turai, sannan kuma a arwacin China da Mongolia da Ttarayyar Rasha. Nau'in ƙwayar wannan cuta na cikin dangin ƙwayoyin cuta na Filabibiraidi. Kimanin mutane 10,000 zuwa 12,000 ke kamuwa da cutar ƙwaƙwalwa a duk shekara, amma an yi imanin wannan adadi bai kai ainihin adadin da ake samu ba. Mafi yawan wannan cuta da ƙwayar cutar na samuwa ne sakamakon ticks da ya kamu da cuta, wanda yawanci yake kasancewa a jikin fata tsawon kwanaki. A wasu lokutan, ana kamuwa da cutar ta hanyar shan nonon akuya ko tunkiya ko saniya mai cuta da aka sha ba tare da an dafa ba. Mutane kan kamu da cutar kumburin ƙwaƙwalwa a yayin mu'amala a wuraren da suke da daji da nisansa ya kai kimanin mita 2000. Mutane ba su yaɗa cutar a junansu. Alamomi: Yawanci kamuwa da cutar ba ya nuna alama. cutar kumburin ƙwaƙwalwa na ɗaukar kwana 2 zuwa 28 kafin ta fara (Yawanci kwana 7 zuwa 14) sannan kuma da kwana 1 zuwa 8 wanda shi ne alama ta bai-ɗaya, inda alamomi irin su yawan gajiya da ciwon kai da rashin jin daɗin jiki, wanda ya wanci ya haɗa da zazzaɓi wanda zafinsa ya kai 38C.
translations.reference: Tick-borne encephalitis Overview: Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is an important cause of viral infections of the central nervous system in eastern, central, northern and increasingly western European countries, and in northern China, Mongolia, and the Russian Federation. Tick-borne encephalitis virus is a member of the family Flaviviridae. Approximately 10 000–12 000 clinical cases of tick-borne encephalitis are reported each year, but this figure is believed to be significantly lower than the actual total number of clinical cases. The vast majority of infections with the virus result from infected ticks, which often remain firmly attached to the skin for days. On rare occasions, infection can result from consumption of unpasteurized milk from infect goats, sheep or cows. People come in contact with the ticks during outdoor activities in forested areas up to an altitude of about 2000 meters. There is no direct person-to-person transmission. Symptoms: Most infections remain asymptomatic. In case of clinical illness, the incubation period for tick-borne encephalitis lasts 2–28 days (most commonly 7–14 days) and is followed by 1–8 days of general cold symptoms, such as fatigue, headache and general malaise, usually combined with fever of ≥38 °C.
translations.hypothesis: Encephalitis Overview: Encephalitis is an acute infectious disease that is common in South-East Asia and Africa, and less common in the Eastern Mediterranean and the Western Pacific Regions, and in Europe, China, Mongolia and the Russian Federation. The virus belongs to the flavivirus family. An estimated 10 000 to 12 000 people contract encephalitis each year, but this number is likely an underestimate of the true number of cases. Most cases are caused by a mosquito-borne virus, which is usually transmitted after the mosquito has bitten an infected animal. In some cases, the virus is transmitted through the consumption of raw milk or products made from raw milk, or the consumption of raw meat from infected animals. People usually develop encephalitis after a short period of viral infection (3–7 days) during which they may experience fever, headache, and malaise. The incubation period is from 2 to 28 days (usually 7–14 days) and the febrile stage lasts 1 to 8 days with symptoms including lassitude, headache, and general malaise, sometimes with a fever of up to 38 °C.

translations.source: Bayan rashin nuna alama na kwana 1 zuwa 20, kusan kaso 15% na marasa lafiyar sukan fuskanci mataki na biyu na cutar, wanda ake yawan yin zazzaɓi da zafinsa ya wuce 40C da kuma nuna alamun cutar, kamar rashin jin ɗin jiki (da ya haɗa da zazzaɓi da ciwon kai ƙagewar wuya) da sakwarkwacewar ƙwaƙwalwa (kamar yawan bacci da rikicewa da rikicewar hanyoyin hankali) da zafin laka. Zafin ƙwaƙwalwa ka iya haifar da shanyewar ɓarin jiki da wata cutar ko ma mutuwa. Kimanin kaso 1% na matsalar da shafi ƙwaƙwalwa na iya gushewa, inda aka samu rahoton yawan mutuwa a Tarayyar Rasha, wanda za a iya dangantawa da ƙwayoyin cuta iri-iri. Ttsananin cutar na ƙaruwa, amma an samu rahoton samun mace-mace a kowane rukunin shekara. Babu wani takamaiman maganin kumburin ƙwaƙwalwa. Kariya: Mutane za iya samun kariya daga cutar tufafin ƙwaƙwalwa ta hanyar saka tufafin da ya dace, wanda ya haɗa da wando da safa, a yayin zuwa ko zama a ƙasashe ko wuraren da ke fuskantar barazana. Ya kamata a riƙa duba jiki kullum sannan a cire kumburin nan da nan. Ya kamata a guji shan madarar dabbar da ta kamu ba tare da an dafa a waɗannan wwuraren. Riga-kafi ya fi komai saurin yin maganin cutar. A yanzu akwai allurai 4 da suke da inganci yin maganin cutar:
translations.reference: After an asymptomatic interval of 1–20 days up to 15% of patients experience a second phase of the disease characterized by fever frequently exceeding 40 °C and signs of central nervous system involvement, such as meningitis (e.g. fever, headache, and a stiff neck), encephalitis (e.g., drowsiness, confusion, and sensory disturbances), myelitis or radiculitis. Encephalitis developing during this second phase may result in paralysis, permanent sequelae or death. About 1% of cases with neurological pathologies may die; higher fatality rates have been reported from the Russian federation, which may be related to a different virus subtype. Severity of illness increases with age of the patient, but fatalities have been reported from all age groups. There is no specific treatment for tick-borne encephalitis. Prevention: People can protect themselves from ticks by wearing appropriate clothing, including long trousers and closed footwear, when hiking or camping in countries or areas at risk. The whole body should be inspected daily and attached ticks removed as soon as possible. The consumption of unpasteurized dairy products should also be avoided in those areas. Immunization offers the most effective protection. Currently, there are 4 widely used vaccines of assured quality:
translations.hypothesis: After a symptom-free period of 1 to 20 days, approximately 15% of patients progress to a second stage, which is characterized by high fever (above 40 °C) and neurological signs, such as myalgia (muscle ache), dizziness, and altered consciousness (ranging from drowsiness to coma), seizures and tremor. Encephalitis can cause permanent brain damage, disability or death. Up to 1% of cases can result in fatal encephalitis, with higher mortality rates reported in Russia, possibly related to specific viral strains. Severe cases of encephalitis have been reported in all age groups. There is no specific treatment for encephalitis. Prevention: People can protect themselves from Japanese encephalitis by using appropriate clothing, including long-sleeved shirts and trousers, when in or around potentially affected areas. Bites should be cleaned with soap and water immediately. Consumption of raw milk and products made from raw milk should be avoided in endemic areas. Vaccination is the most effective means of prevention. There are currently 4 vaccines that are effective against Japanese encephalitis:

translations.source: Sun haɗa da allurar FSME-Immun da Encepu, waɗanda ake yi a Austria da Germany, sannan kuma dangane da ƙarfin ƙwayar cutar a Turai da TBE-Moscow da kuma EnceVir, waɗanda da ake yin su a Tarayyar Rasha, sannan dangane da ƙarfinta a can gabashi. Ana ganin allurai 4 sun fi inganci da aminci. Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya ta bayar da shawarar yin alluran ga kowane rukuni na shekara, da ya haɗa da yara a wuraren da cutar ta zama annoba. Cutar kumburin ƙwaƙwalwa na haifar da cutar Borreliosis, wadda ƙwayar cuta ke haifarwa. Allurar TBE ba ta maganin wannan cuta, wacce za a iya maganinta da maganin da ke kashe ƙwayoyin cuta.
translations.reference: FSME-Immun and Encepur, manufactured in Austria and Germany respectively, and based on European strains of the virus; and TBE-Moscow and EnceVir, manufactured in the Russian Federation and based on Far-Eastern strains. The 4 vaccines are considered to be safe and effective. In areas where the disease is highly endemic, WHO recommends that vaccination be offered to all age groups, including children. Ticks also transmit Borreliosis (Lyme disease), which is a bacterial infection. TBE vaccination is not effective against this disease, which however is treatable with antimicrobials.
translations.hypothesis: They include FSME-Immun and Encepu, used in Austria and Germany, and TBE-Moscow and EnceVir, used in the Russian Federation, depending on the circulating tick-borne encephalitis virus variants in Europe and Asia, respectively. All 4 vaccines are considered safe and effective. WHO recommends vaccination for all age groups, including children, in endemic areas. TBE is caused by the bacterium Borrelia burgdorferi. TBE vaccine does not protect against Lyme disease, which can be treated with antibiotics.

translations.source: Taba sigari Ƙarin bayani: Sinadarin nikotin da ke cikin taba sigari na kama mutane, sannan shan sigari na ɗaya daga cikin manyan matsalolin da ke haifar da shanyewar ɓarin jiki da matsalolin numfashi, inda take haifar fiye da kaso 20% na ire-iren cutar kansa da sauran manyan cututtuka. A kowace shekara, mutane miliyan 8 ne suke mutuwa sakamakon shan taba sigari. Yawan mace-macen da ke da nasaba da taba sigari na faruwa ne a ƙaranci da matsakaicin tattalin arziki, waɗanda su kamfanonin taba sigari suka fin yin tallace-tallace. Haka kuma taba sigari na kashe waɗanda ba sa sha. Masu shaƙar hayaƙin taba sigari na fuskantar barazanar lafiya, inda kimanin mutane miliyan 1,2 ke mutuwa duk shekara. Kusan rabin yara ƙanana na sheƙar iskar da taba sigari ta gurɓata, sannan kuma kimanin yara dubu 65,000 ke mutuwa duk shekara sakamakon cututtuka masu nasaba da shaƙar taba sigari. Shan taba yayin da ake ɗauke da ciki na iya haifar da matsalolin lafiya na har abada ga jarirai. Kayayyakin taba da aka gasa (HTPs) sun ƙunshi taba, kuma suna jefa masu shau haɗuwa da hayaƙi mai guba, waɗanda da yawa daga cikin su ke haifar da cutar kansa kuma suna da illa ga lafiya. Tsarin isar da nicotine na lantarki (ENDS) da tsarin ba da abubuwan da ba na nicotine ba na lantarki (ENNDS), wanda akafi sani da e-cigarettes, basa ƙunshe da taba kuma ƙila su ƙunshi nicotine ko ba su ƙunshi nicotine ba, amma suna da illa ga lafiya kuma babu shakka amfani da su yana da haɗari.
translations.reference: Tobacco Overview: Nicotine contained in tobacco is highly addictive and tobacco use is a major risk factor for cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, over 20 different types or subtypes of cancer, and many other debilitating health conditions. Every year, more than 8 million people die from tobacco use. Most tobacco-related deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries, which are often targets of intensive tobacco industry interference and marketing. Tobacco can also be deadly for non-smokers. Second-hand smoke exposure has also been implicated in adverse health outcomes, causing 1.2 million deaths annually. Nearly half of all children breathe air polluted by tobacco smoke and 65 000 children die each year due to illnesses related to second-hand smoke. Smoking while pregnant can lead to several life-long health conditions for babies. Heated tobacco products (HTPs) contain tobacco and expose users to toxic emissions, many of which cause cancer and are harmful to health. Electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) and electronic non-nicotine delivery systems (ENNDS), commonly known as e-cigarettes, do not contain tobacco and may or may not contain nicotine, but are harmful to health and undoubtedly unsafe.
translations.hypothesis: Tobacco Overview: Nicotine, the addictive substance in tobacco, causes people to continue using tobacco even though they know it is harmful. Tobacco use is one of the major causes of stroke and respiratory diseases, and is a risk factor for at least 20 different types of cancer and other major diseases. About 8 million people die each year from tobacco-related causes. The vast majority of tobacco-related deaths occur prematurely, with low- and middle-income countries disproportionately affected by tobacco-related deaths and illnesses due to aggressive targeting by the tobacco industry. Tobacco also kills those who don’t smoke. Smokeless tobacco use also carries health risks, with about 1.2 million deaths annually. Nearly half of all children breathe smoke-filled air, and about 65 000 children die each year from illnesses attributable to second-hand smoke. Smoking during pregnancy causes harm to the developing fetus and increases the risk of health problems for the newborn. Heated tobacco products (HTPs) still involve tobacco and expose users to nicotine and to harmful chemicals, some of which cause cancer and have other long-term health effects. Electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) and electronic non-nicotine delivery systems (ENNDS), also known as e-cigarettes, do not contain tobacco but may contain nicotine and have been shown to be harmful and are highly addictive.

translations.source: Sai dai, ya yi wuri a ba da cikakkiyar amsa kan tasirin HTPs da/ko amfani da sigari na dogon lokaci. Tasiri: Kimanin mutane biliyan 1.3 a faɗin duniya suna amfani da kayan sigari, kashi 80% daga cikinsu suna cikin ƙasashe masu ƙarami ko matsakaicin karfi. Yin amfani da taba yana taimakawa wajen ƙaruwar talauci ta hanyar karkatar da kuɗaɗen amfanin gida daga buƙatun dole, kamar abinci da matsuguni, zuwa taba. Wannan halin kashe kuɗi yana da wahala a hana shi saboda taba tana da shiga rai sosai. Haka nan yana haifar da mutuwa da wuri da naƙasa ga manya masu tasowa a gidaje, wanda hakan ke haifar da raguwar kuɗin shiga na gida da ƙarin kashe kuɗi kan kiwon lafiya. Baya ga illar da taba ke yi kan lafiya, an ƙiyasta cewa jimillar kudin da ake kashewa kan shan sigari (daga kuɗaɗen da ake kashewa kan kiwon lafiya da asarar yawan aiki) ya kai dalar Amurka tiriliyan 1.4 a kowace shekara, kwatankwacin kashi 1.8% na ma’aunin GDP na shekara-shekara na duniya. Kusan kashi 40% na wannan kuɗi ya faru ne a ƙasashe masu tasowa, wanda ke nuna babban nauyin da waɗannan ƙasashe ke fama da shi. Ana amfani da wani ɓangare na harajin taba don yaƙar wannan tasirin, kuma ana kallon hakan a matsayin hanya mafi inganci wajen hana shan taba, musamman tsakanin matasa da masu ƙaramin ƙarfi. Ƙarin harajin da ya ƙara farashin taba da kashi 10 cikin 100 yana rage yawan shan taba da kusan kashi 4 cikin 100 a ƙasashe masu ƙarfin tattalin arziƙi da kuma kusan kashi 5 cikin 100 a ƙasashe masu ƙaramin ƙarfi da matsakaicin kuɗin shiga. Martanin ƙuniyar WHO: Girman wannan bala'i ga ɗan adam da na tattalin arziƙi yana da ban tsoro, amma kuma ana iya hana shi.
translations.reference: However, it is too early to provide a clear answer on the long-term impact of HTPs and/or e-cigarette use. Impact: An estimated 1.3 billion people worldwide use tobacco products, 80% of whom are in low- and middle-income countries. Tobacco use contributes to poverty by diverting household spending from basic needs, such as food and shelter, to tobacco. This spending behaviour is difficult to curb because tobacco is so addictive. It also causes premature death and disability of productive age adults in households thus leading to reduced household income and increased healthcare costs. In addition to the detrimental impact of tobacco on health, the total economic cost of smoking (from health expenditures and productivity losses together) are estimated to be around US$ 1.4 trillion per year, equivalent in magnitude to 1.8% of the world's annual gross domestic product (GDP). Almost 40% of this cost occurred in developing countries, highlighting the substantial burden these countries suffer. Tobacco taxes are applied in part to combat this effect and are seen as the most cost-effective way of curbing tobacco use, particularly among youth and low-income populations. A tax increase that increases tobacco prices by 10% decreases tobacco consumption by about 4% in high-income countries and about 5% in low- and middle-income countries. WHO response: The scale of this human and economic tragedy is shocking, but it’s also preventable.
translations.hypothesis: However, it is too early to give a definitive answer on the long-term health effects of HTPs and/or their role in long-term smoking cessation. Impact: About 1.3 billion people worldwide consume tobacco products, 80% of whom live in low- and middle-income countries. Tobacco use contributes to household poverty by reallocating household resources away from necessities such as food and shelter, to tobacco. This pattern of spending is hard to break as tobacco is highly addictive. It also causes early death and disability in adults, which results in lost income and increased health care costs. In addition to the health costs, the economic cost of tobacco consumption (including health care costs and lost productivity) is estimated at US$ 1.4 trillion annually, or 1.8% of the global gross domestic product. About 40% of this cost is in low- and middle-income countries, reflecting the large burden these countries face. A portion of tobacco tax revenues is used to offset these costs and is considered a best practice in tobacco control, particularly among young people and other vulnerable groups. A 10% increase in tobacco product prices results in a 4% decrease in consumption in high-income countries and about a 5% decrease in low- and middle-income countries. WHO response: The scale of the human and economic costs is staggering, but the damage is preventable.

translations.source: Big Tobacco - tare da duk masu haɗa kayan sigari - suna yaƙi don tabbatar da cewa sun ɓoye haɗarin hajarsu, amma muma muna yaƙarsu: A shekarar 2003, Ƙasashe Mambobin WHO a jimlace sun amince da Yarjejeniyar Tsarin Taimako ta WHO kan Kula da Taba (WHO FCTC), yarjejeniya kan lafiyar jama'a ɗaya tilo a ƙarƙashin ƙungiyar WHO. Yarjejeniyar da ke aiki tun 2005, a halin yanzu tana da mambobi 181. Don taimaka wa ƙasashe wajen aiwatar da WHO FCTC, WHO ta gabatar da MPOWER, wani ƙunshin matakan da kayayyaki na ƙwarewa, wanda kowanne ya dace da a ƙalla tanadin WHO FCTC guda ɗaya. MPOWER yana haɓaka ƙarfin ƙasashe na aiwatar da matakai 6 don rage amfani da kayan sigari: sa ido kan tsare-tsaren amfani da taba da daƙile wa, kare mutane daga shan taba, ba da taimako kan daina shan taba, gargaɗi game da haɗarin taba, tilasta hana tallan taba, tallatawa da ɗaukar nauyi, da ƙara haraji akan taba.
translations.reference: Big Tobacco — along with all manufacturers of tobacco products — is fighting to ensure the dangers of their products are concealed, but we are fighting back: In 2003, WHO Member States unanimously adopted the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (WHO FCTC), the only public health treaty under the auspices of WHO. In force since 2005, it has currently 181 Parties. To help countries implement the WHO FCTC, WHO introduced MPOWER, a package of technical measures and resources, each of which corresponds to at least one provision of the WHO FCTC. MPOWER builds the capacity of countries to implement 6 measures to reduce the demand for tobacco products: monitor tobacco use and prevention policies, protect people from tobacco use, offer help to quit tobacco use, warn about the dangers of tobacco, enforce bans on tobacco advertising, promotion and sponsorship and raise taxes on tobacco.
translations.hypothesis: Big Tobacco – along with all other parties to the tobacco control treaty – is fighting to ensure that the true risks of their products are hidden, but we will fight back: In 2003, WHO Member States adopted the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (WHO FCTC), the first international public health treaty under WHO’s aegis. The Convention, which came into force in 2005, now has 181 Parties. To help countries implement the WHO FCTC, WHO introduced MPOWER, a package of effective measures and technical specifications, each corresponding to at least one WHO FCTC article. MPOWER promotes 6 cost-effective tobacco control measures: monitor tobacco use and prevention policies, protect people from second-hand smoke, offer help to quit, warn about the dangers of tobacco, enforce restrictions on tobacco advertising, promotion and sponsorship, and increase taxes on tobacco.

translations.source: Trachoma Bayani: Trachoma cuta ce ta ido kuma cutar da ke kan gaba wajen jawo makanta a duniya. Ɗaurarrun ƙananan ƙwayoyin cuta da ake kira Chlamydia trachomatis ne ke haifar da ita. Cutar na yaɗuwa ne daga mutum zuwa mutum ta hanyar haɗuwa da ruwan da ke fita daga ido ko hancin mai ɗauke da cutar kai-tsaye ko ba kai-tsaye ba; yaɗuwar da ba ta kai-tsaye ba ta haɗa da ɗaukar cutar a jikin wasu nau’ika na ƙuda. Yaran da ba su kai matakin shiga makaranta ba suna kamuwa da cutar sosaa. Samfuran tsare-tsare sun nuna cewa mutum na buƙatar cututtuka sama da 150 masu haɗari kafin ya haɗu da rikice-rikicen makanta na trachoma. Cutar ta Trachoma na yaɗuwa sosai a wasu daga cikin matalautan duniya, waɗanda ke zaune a yankunan karkara da lunguna, kuma ba su da isasshen ruwa da tsaftar muhalli da tsarin kiwon lafiya. Afirka ce nahiyar da cutar ta fi shafa, amma kuma tafi ko ina ƙoƙarin shawo kan matsalar. Haka nan ana samun cutar a Amurka ta Tsakiya da Amurka ta Kudu da Asiya da Ostiraliya da Gabas ta Tsakiya. Ya zuwa2 ga Janairun 2020, ƙasashe 13 sun ba da rahoton daƙile cutar.
translations.reference: Trachoma Overview: Trachoma is a disease of the eye and the leading infectious cause of blindness worldwide. It is caused by an obligate intracellular bacterium called Chlamydia trachomatis. Infection is transmitted from person to person by direct or indirect transfer of ocular and nasal discharges of infected people; indirect transfer includes carriage on the body of species of flies. Preschool-age children harbour the principal reservoir of infection. Models suggest that an individual requires more than 150 lifetime infections to develop the blinding complications of trachoma. Trachoma is endemic in some of the world’s poorest populations, who live in rural and remote areas and have highly inadequate access to water, sanitation and healthcare. Africa is the most affected continent, but it also has the most widespread control efforts. The disease is also found in Central and South America, Asia, Australia, and the Middle East. As of 2 January 2020, 13 countries had reported achieving elimination goals.
translations.hypothesis: Trachoma Overview: Trachoma is a bacterial eye infection and a leading cause of preventable blindness worldwide. It is caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis. The disease is transmitted by direct or indirect contact with the discharge from the eyes or nose of an infected person; indirect transmission involves flies and contaminated surfaces. Preschool children are the main group affected. Mathematical models show that a person needs to be infected with more than 150 strains of the bacteria to develop the chronic condition of trachomatous blindness. Trachoma is mainly found in impoverished communities in rural and remote areas lacking adequate water and sanitation systems and health services. Africa is the most affected continent, but the disease is also found in Central and South America, Asia, Australia and the Middle East. As of January 2020, 13 countries had been certified as having eliminated the disease.

translations.source: A shekarar 2019 kaɗai, an yi wa mutane 92 622 aikin tiyata don babbar cutar ta trachoma, kuma an yi wa mutum miliyan 95.2 maganin da magungunan kashe ƙwayoyin cuta. Duk da waɗannan nasarorin, cutar ta ci gaba da zama babbar damuwa ga lafiyar jama'a, tare da asarar kusan dalar Amurka biliyan 8 a kowace shekara wurin yin aiki saboda makanta da matsalar gani. Alamomi: Kamuwa da cutar na haɗe da canje-canje na kumburi a cikin conjunctiva da ake kira "trachoma mai aiki". Garkuwar jikin mutum na iya kawar da dunƙulen cutar guda ɗaya, amma a cikin al'ummomin da cutar tayi yawa, sake haɗuwa da ƙwayoyin cutar yana faruwa akai-akai. Bayan shekaru da yawa ana maimaita cutar ta trachoma mai aiki, cikin fatar ido zai iya zama mai tabo mai tsanani (trachomatous conjunctival scarring) har ta juya zuwa ciki tana saka gashin ido yana gogar ƙwayar ido (trachomatous trichiasis), wanda ke haifar da ciwo na kullum da rashin iya kallon haske sosai; wannan da kuma sauran canje-canjen ido na iya haifar da tabon cornea. Idan ba a yi maganin sa ba, yana iya haifar da haɗuwar dusashewar da ba za a iya gyarawa ba, tare da haifar da naƙasar gani ko makanta. Shekarun da wannan ke faruwa ya dogara da abubuwa da yawa, waɗanda suka haɗa da ƙarfin yaɗuwa na cikin gida. A cikin al'ummomin da masu cutar ke da yawa sosai, tana iya faruwa a lokacin yarinta, ko da yake farkon nakasar gani ya fi faruwa tsakanin shekaru 30 zuwa 40. Mata sun fi makanta sau huɗu fiye da maza, mai yiwuwa saboda yawan saduwa da yara masu ɗauke da cutar. Mutanen da ke zaune a cikin mafi talauci kuma mafi nisan al'ummomin Afirka da Asiya da Ostiraliya da Gabas ta Tsakiya da Amurka ta Tsakiya da Amurka ta Kudu da Tsibiran Pacific suna cikin haɗari.
translations.reference: In 2019 alone, 92 622 people received surgical treatment for advanced trachoma and 95.2 million were treated with antibiotics. Despite these successes, the disease remains a serious public health concern, with an estimated US$ 8 billion annual loss in productivity due to blindness and visual impairment. Symptoms: Infection is associated with inflammatory changes in the conjunctiva known as “active trachoma”. An individual’s immune system can clear a single episode of infection, but in endemic communities, re-acquisition of the organism occurs frequently. After years of repeated episodes of active trachoma, the inside of the eyelid can become so severely scarred (trachomatous conjunctival scarring) that it turns inwards and causes the eyelashes to rub against the eyeball (trachomatous trichiasis), resulting in constant pain and light intolerance; this and other alterations of the eye can lead to scarring of the cornea. Left untreated, this condition leads to the formation of irreversible opacities, with resulting visual impairment or blindness. The age at which this occurs depends on several factors including local transmission intensity. In very highly endemic communities, it can occur in childhood, though onset of visual impairment between the ages of 30 and 40 years is more typical. Women are blinded up to four times as often as men, probably due to more frequent contact with infected children. Individuals living in the poorest and most remote communities of Africa, Asia, Australia, the Middle East, Central and South America and the Pacific Islands are at risk.
translations.hypothesis: In 2019 alone, 92 622 people had surgery for advanced trichiasis and a further 95.2 million people were treated with antibiotics. Despite this progress, the disease remains a major public health problem, with an estimated 8.4 million years lost to disability and vision impairment every year. Symptoms: Infection is associated with a range of symptoms in the conjunctiva called “trachoma spectrum”. The body can sometimes overcome the infection, but in endemic communities, re-infection is frequent. After years of repeated infection by Chlamydia trachomatis, the inner surface of the eyelids can become severely scarred (trachomatous conjunctival scarring) and eventually turned inwards so that the eyelashes rub on the eyeball (trachomatous trichiasis), causing constant pain and irritation and making it difficult to see; this and other eye changes can cause corneal opacities. If left untreated, it can cause irreversible vision loss, leading to blindness. The age at which this occurs depends on several factors, including the level of domestic transmission. In communities where the disease is highly endemic, it may occur in childhood, although the greatest impact on vision usually occurs between the ages of 30 and 40 years. Women are four times more likely than men to be blind, possibly because they have more contact with young children who carry the infection. People living in impoverished communities in Africa, Asia, Australia, the Middle East, Central America and South America, and the Pacific Islands are most at risk.

translations.source: Magancewa: Ana iya kare cutar ta trachoma ta hanyar rage haɗurran da ke da alaƙa da muhalli. Waɗannan sun haɗa da rashin isasshiyar tsafta, da cunkoso a gidaje, da rashin samun isasshen ruwa, da rashin isassu kayan tsaftar muhalli da damar amfani da su. Yawanci cutar na farawa a ƙananan shekaru, kuma tana ƙaranci kuma mafi gaharta idan ana ƙara yawan shekaru. An fi kamuwa da cutar ta hanyar iyali da hulɗa da masu fama da cutar. Maimaita cutar na haifar da mafi girman alamun cutar. Ana iya daƙile cutar ta trachoma a matsayin matsalar lafiyar jama'a ta hanyar amfani da dabarun SAFE, wanda ya ƙunshi: Tiyata don magance trachomatous trichiasis, matakin makanta na cutar; Magungunan kashe ƙwayoyin cuta don kawar da cutar, musamman bayar da maganin nan mai suna azithromycin mai kashe ƙwayoyin cuta da yawa, wanda masana'anta ke bayarwa kyauta ga shirye-shiryen ƙasa ta hanyar International Trachoma Initiative; Tsaftar fuska; da kuma Inganta muhalli, musamman samun damar amfani da ruwa da tsafta mafiya kyawu.
translations.reference: Treatment: Trachoma can be prevented by limiting environmental risk factors. These include inadequate hygiene, crowded households, inadequate access to water and inadequate access to and use of sanitation. Infections usually begin at an early age and grow less frequent and shorter in duration with increasing age. Infections are most often acquired through family and contact with others with active disease. Repeated infections cause the most serious symptoms of the disease. Trachoma can be eliminated as a public health problem using the SAFE strategy, comprising: Surgery to treat trachomatous trichiasis, the blinding stage of the disease; Antibiotics to clear infection, particularly mass drug administration of the antibiotic azithromycin, which is donated by the manufacturer to national programmes through the International Trachoma Initiative; Facial cleanliness; and Environmental improvement, particularly better access to water and sanitation.
translations.hypothesis: Prevention: Trachoma can be prevented by reducing the risk factors associated with the disease. These include poor hygiene, crowded living conditions, insufficient water supplies, and inadequate environmental sanitation and access to washing facilities. The disease usually starts in childhood, and becomes less severe and less frequent with increasing age. It is mainly transmitted within families and close communities. Repeated infection leads to more severe disease. Trachoma can be controlled as a public health problem by applying the SAFE strategy, which stands for: Surgery to correct trachomatous trichiasis, the blinding stage of the disease; Antibiotics to treat the infection, mainly azithromycin, which is donated by several pharmaceutical companies to national programmes through the International Trachoma Initiative; Facial cleanliness; and Environmental improvements, mainly providing access to safe water and improved sanitation.

translations.source: WHO ta yi amfani da dabarun SAFE a shekarar 1993, kuma tana ci gaba da aikinta na yin jagoranci da daidaita ayyukan ƙasa-da-ƙasa don kawar da cutar ta trachoma a matsayin matsalar lafiyar jama'a.
translations.reference: WHO adopted the SAFE strategy in 1993 and continues in its mandate to provide leadership and coordination of international efforts to eliminate trachoma as a public health problem.
translations.hypothesis: WHO adopted the SAFE strategy in 1993, and continues to lead and coordinate global efforts to eliminate trachoma as a public health problem.

translations.source: Magungunan Gargajiya da na Ƙari da Haɗaɗɗun Magunguna Bayani: Maganin gargajiya Maganin gargajiya yana da dogon tarihi. Shi ne jimillar ilimi da ƙwarewa da ayyuka bisa ƙa'idoji da imani da gogewa na cikin gida ga mutane masu al’adu daban-daban, wanda za a iya bayaninsa da wanda ba za a iya ba, wanda ake amfani da su wajen kula da lafiya da kuma rigakafi da gano cuta da ingantawa ko magance rashin lafiyar jiki da ta ƙwaƙwalwa. Maganin Ƙari "Maganin ƙari " ko "maganin madadi " na nufin wani jerin tsarin ayyukan kula da lafiya waɗanda ba sa cikin al'adar ƙasar na kanta ko magungunan gargajiya kuma ba sa cikin gamammen tsarin kula da lafiya. Ana amfani da su a madadin magungunan gargajiya a wasu ƙasashe. Magungunan ganye Magungunan ganye sun haɗa da ganyayyaki da kayan ganyayyaki da gyara ganyayyayki da kuma kayan ganye da aka sarrafa, waɗanda ke ƙunshe da sassan tsirrai ko wasu kayan shuka ko duka. Tasiri: An ƙirƙira kuma an ƙaddamar da Dabarun Magungunan Gargajiya na WHO 2014-2023 don mayar da martani ga ƙudurin Majalisar Lafiya ta Duniya kan magungunan gargajiya (WHA62.13).
translations.reference: Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine Overview: Traditional medicine Traditional medicine has a long history. It is the sum total of the knowledge, skill, and practices based on the theories, beliefs, and experiences indigenous to different cultures, whether explicable or not, used in the maintenance of health as well as in the prevention, diagnosis, improvement or treatment of physical and mental illness. Complementary medicine The terms “complementary medicine” or “alternative medicine” refer to a broad set of health care practices that are not part of that country’s own tradition or conventional medicine and are not fully integrated into the dominant health-care system. They are used interchangeably with traditional medicine in some countries. Herbal medicines Herbal medicines include herbs, herbal materials, herbal preparations and finished herbal products, that contain as active ingredients parts of plants, or other plant materials, or combinations. Impact: The WHO Traditional Medicine Strategy 2014–2023 was developed and launched in response to the World Health Assembly resolution on traditional medicine (WHA62.13).
translations.hypothesis: Traditional, complementary, and integrative medicine Overview: Traditional medicine refers to the sum total of the knowledge, skills, and practices based on the theories, beliefs and experiences of indigenous peoples, whether biological, physical, chemical, psychological, or spiritual, used in the maintenance of health and in the prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care of physical and mental illnesses. Complementary medicine “Complementary medicine” or “alternative medicine” refers to a set of health care practices that are not part of the dominant or conventional medical system in a particular country or region, but which are used in conjunction with conventional medicine in some countries. Herbal medicines Herbal medicines are preparations made from plant parts or other plant products, including leaves, roots, stems, flowers, seeds, and fruits. Impact: The WHO traditional medicine strategy 2014–2023 was developed in response to the World Health Assembly resolution on traditional medicine (WHA62.13).

translations.source: Dabarun na da nufin tallafawa ƙasashe mambobin ƙungiyar wuein samar da tsare-tsare na gaske da aiwatar da tsare-tsaren ayyuka waɗanda za su ƙarfafa rawar da magungunan gargajiya ke takawa wajen kiyaye lafiyar al'umma. Magance ƙalubalen, mayar da martani ga buƙatun da ƙasashe mambobi suka gano, da kuma haɓaka aikin da aka yi a ƙarƙashin dabarun maganin gargajiya na WHO: 2002-2005, dabarun da aka sabunta a lokacin 2014-2023 ya ba da ƙaimi fiye da wanda ya gabace shi don ba da fifiko ga ayyuka da tsare-tsaren kiwon lafiya, waɗanda suka haɗa magungunan gargajiya da na ƙari, da ayyuka masu aiki. Manufofin dabarun su ne: Don gina fage na ilimi don gudanar da aikin T&CM ta hanyar tsare-tsare na ƙasa waɗanda suka dace; Don ƙarfafa tabbatar da inganci da aminci da amfani da T & CM yadda ya dace kuma cikin tasiri ta hanyar kula da magunguna da ayyuka da masu aiki; Don haɓaka shiga ko ina a duniya ta hanyar haɗe ayyukan T&CM cikin gudanar da ayyukan kiwon lafiya da kula da lafiyar kai. Martanin WHO: an samar da rahoton na WHO na duniya game da maganin gargajiya da na ƙari na 2019 don cike giɓin bayanai abin dogaro, sahihi, kuma na hukuma daga Ƙasashe Mambobi na yankin T&CM. Wannan rahoto ya yi duba kan ci gaban duniya a T&CM cikin shekaru ashirin da suka gabata, kuma ya dogara ne kan gudummawar ƙasashe mambobin WHO guda 179. Ya ba da bayanai masu mahimmanci ga masu tsara manufofi, da ƙwararru kan kiwon lafiya, da jama'a don yin amfani da yiwuwar gudummawar T&CM ga lafiya da walwala.
translations.reference: The strategy aims to support Member States in developing proactive policies and implementing action plans that will strengthen the role traditional medicine plays in keeping populations healthy. Addressing the challenges, responding to the needs identified by Member States and building on the work done under the WHO traditional medicine strategy: 2002–2005, the updated strategy for the period 2014–2023 devotes more attention than its predecessor to prioritizing health services and systems, including traditional and complementary medicine products, practices and practitioners. The strategic objectives are: To build the knowledge base for active management of T&CM through appropriate national policies; To strengthen the quality assurance, safety, proper use and effectiveness of T&CM by regulating products, practices and practitioners; To promote universal health coverage by integrating T&CM services into health care service delivery and self-health care. WHO response: The WHO global report on traditional and complementary medicine 2019 was developed to address the gap in reliable, credible and official data from Member States in the area of T&CM. This report reviews global progress in T&CM over the past two decades and is based on contributions from 179 WHO Member States. It provides valuable information for policy-makers, health professionals and the public for capitalizing on the potential contribution of T&CM to health and well-being.
translations.hypothesis: The strategy aims to support Member States in developing national policies and action plans that strengthen the role of traditional medicine in people-centred health care. Building on the challenges, opportunities and lessons learned during the implementation of the WHO traditional medicine strategy: 2002–2005, the updated strategy for 2014-2023 provides a more focused direction for actions and health policies, including traditional, complementary, and integrative medicine services. The objectives of the strategy are to: 1. build the knowledge base for active management of T&CM through national policies and action plans; 2. strengthen national capacity and quality assurance mechanisms for the appropriate and effective use of T&CM, including regulation of T&CM products, services and practitioners; and 3. promote access to T&CM services through integration of T&CM into health systems governance and delivery of personal health care. WHO response: The 2019 WHO Global report on traditional and complementary medicine was developed to fill gaps in reliable, accurate, and comprehensive information on the state of T&CM in WHO’s Member States. The report reviewed the global development of T&CM over the last two decades and was based on the contributions of 179 WHO Member States. It provides key information for policy-makers, health and research professionals, and the public to better understand the potential contribution of T&CM to health and well-being.

translations.source: Dashe Bayani: Dasa tantanin halitta da tishu da gaɓoɓin mutane Dashentantanin halitta ko tishu ko gaɓoɓin jikin mutum na ceton rayuka da yawa kuma yana dawo da ayyuka masu mahimmanci inda babu tasiri madadin su. Cikin shekaru 50, dashe yayi nasara a faɗin duniya. Sai dai akwai babban bambanci tsakanin ƙasashe wajen samun damar dashen da ya dace da kuma matakin aminci da inganci da samun gudummawa da dashen tantanin halitta na ɗan adam da tishu da gaɓoɓi. Abubuwan da suka dace na dashe su ne kan gaba. Musamman, rashin biyan buƙatun marasa lafiya da ƙarancin abin dashe na haifar da yiwuwar fataucin sassan jikin ɗan adam don dasawa. Dashen mutum Tantanin halitta na ɗan adam da tishu don dasawa na iya ceton rayuka ko dawo da ayyuka masu mahimmanci. Misali corneal graft zai iya dawo da gani a makantar corneal;
translations.reference: Transplantation Overview: Transplantation of human cells, tissues and organs Transplantation of human cells, tissues or organs saves many lives and restores essential functions where no alternatives of comparable effectiveness exist. In 50 years, transplantation has become a successful worldwide practice. However, there are large differences between countries in access to suitable transplantation and in the level of safety, quality, efficacy of donation and transplantation of human cells, tissues and organs. The ethical aspects of transplantation are at the forefront. In particular, the unmet patients’ needs and the shortage of transplants lead to the temptation of trafficking in human body components for transplantation. Human transplantation Human cells and tissues for transplantation can save lives or restore essential functions. For examplea corneal graft can restore sight in corneal blindness;
translations.hypothesis: Overview: Human organ, tissue and cell transplantation Life-saving and health-restoring, transplantation is an essential health service with no therapeutic alternatives in many cases. Over the past 50 years, transplantation has been achieved on a global scale. However, there remain huge disparities between countries in access to transplantation, and in the safety and quality of donated organs, tissues and cells. Ethical issues in transplantation are complex. In particular, the mismatch between organ supply and demand leads to illegal organ trafficking. Human transplantation Human cells, tissues and organs for transplantation can save lives or restore vital functions. For example, a corneal graft can restore sight in a patient with corneal blindness;

translations.source: dashen tantanin halitta na hematopoietic na iya warkar da cututtukan da aka haifi mutum da su ko waɗanda suka samu, waɗanda suka haɗa da wasu daga cikin cutar sankarar bargo. Duba ƙarin bayani akan Tantanin Halitta na Haematopoeitic Sau da yawa dashen bawul na zuciyar ɗan adam yakan zama mafi kyawun yanayin maye gurbi kuma marasa lafiya masu karɓa ba sa buƙatar dogon lokaci na maganin cututtukan sarƙewar jini. Xenotransplantation Xenotransplantation, wato daga dabba zuwa mutum, shi ne rayayyen tantanin halitta ko tishu ko gaɓoɓin asali na dabba da ruwan jikin mutum da tantanin halitta ko tishu ko gaɓoɓin da ke da ex vivo da waɗannan masu ran, da kayan xenogeneic, suna da yiwuwar zama madadin kayan asali na jikin ɗan adam da kuma cike giɓin da ke cikin kayan jikin ɗan adam don dasawa. Gudunmawa: Ya kamata a haɓaka gudummawa daga matattu zuwa iyakar ƙarfinsu don gujewa haɗarin da ke tattare da masu ba da gudummawa gwargwadon iko, kamar yadda aka bayyana a cikin Ƙa’idodin Jagora na 3. Akwai buƙata ga al'ummomi da ƙwararru kan kiwon lafiya ta samun ilimi mai zurfi game da gudummawa da dashe, kuma wannan shi ne mabuɗin samun nasarar shirye-shiryen bayar da gudummawa daga waɗanda da suka mutu. Duk da haka, duk da yawan amfani da kayan da aka ba da gudummawa daga matattu, gudummawar da ake bayarwa daga masu ba da gudummawar rayuwa ya zama dole don wasu nau'ikan dashe ko don rama ƙarancin kayan da ake samu daga masu ba da gudummawar da suka mutu don biyan buƙatun majiyyata. Don haka, ana ba da gudummawar rayuwa duk da cewa tana ƙunshe da haɗari ga mai ba da gudummawa wanda ba za a yi sakaci da shi ba. Yayin da sayan kayan ɗan adam na dashe daga masu bayarwa ga matattu ko masu rai, kuma dashen allogeneic na gaba na iya haifar da haɗari na ɗabi'a da aminci ga duka masu karɓa da mai ba da gudummawa da tsauraran kula da ingantaccen sa ido ya kamata hukumomin lafiya su aiwatar da su don kare su.
translations.reference: the transplantation of haematopoietic stem cells can cure congenital or acquired diseases including some leukaemias See further information on Haematopoeitic Stem Cells the transplantation of a human heart valve often constitutes the best replacement situation and recipient patients do not require long term anti-coagulation therapy. Xenotransplantation Xenotransplantation, animal to human, defined as living cells, tissues or organs of animal origin and human body fluids, cells, tissues or organs that have ex vivo with these living, xenogeneic materials, has the potential to constitute an alternative to material of human origin and bridge the shortfall in human material for transplantation. Donation: Donations from deceased persons should be developed to their maximum therapeutic potential avoiding, whenever possible, the inherent risks to live donors, as stated in WHO Guiding Principle 3. There is a recognized need for communities, and health professionals, to become better educated about donation and transplantation and that is the key to the success of deceased donation programmes. However, despite the frequent use of materials donated from deceased donors, the donations from living donors are necessary for some types of transplants or to compensate for the limited supply of material available from deceased donors in order to meet patient needs. Living donation is thus practised despite the fact that it involves risks for the donor that may not be negligible. As the procurement of human material for transplantation from deceased or living donors and the subsequent allogeneic transplantation may entail ethical and safety risks for both the recipient and the donor, strict controls and effective oversight should be carried out by the health authorities to protect them.
translations.hypothesis: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation can cure many inherited disorders and acquired conditions, including some cancers. See more about Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation Often, a matched unrelated donor is the best option and patients do not require long-term immunosuppression. Xenotransplantation Xenotransplantation, which is the transplantation of living cells, tissues or organs from one species to another, is the transfer of living cells, tissues or organs from one animal to another or from an animal to a human, or vice versa, where the donor and recipient are of different species. It is possible that xenotransplantation may one day provide an unlimited source of organs to replace those lost through disease or injury. Donation: Donation from deceased donors should be encouraged to the maximum extent possible in order to avoid any risk to the living donor, as described in Guideline 3. There is a need for communities and health-care professionals to have accurate information about donation and transplantation, and this is key to the success of any deceased donor transplantation programme. However, despite the many benefits of deceased organ donation, living donation is required in specific cases or to compensate for a shortage of deceased donor organs in order to meet the needs of patients. Therefore, living donation is only offered after the potential donor has been fully informed of the risks involved and has made an autonomous decision to proceed. Given the current limited supply of human organs for transplantation, and the ethical issues associated with the commercialization of human tissues, living related or unrelated altruistic donation carries some risk for the donor that should be carefully weighed against the potential benefit to the recipient, with appropriate medical, psychological and social support provided to both.

translations.source: Ƙa'idodin Jagora sun ba da umarni mai kyakkyawar kulawa ga masu bayarwa da masu karɓa. Sa ido a fili na hukumomin lafiya kan ayyukan bayar da agaji da ayyukan dashe yana da matuƙar muhimmanci wajen ƙara amincewar jama'a kan tsarin. Bugu da ƙari, sau da dama yanke shawarar zama mai bayarwa ya dogara ne kan fahimtar cewa gudummawar da aka samu don samar da dashen zai iya amfanar da buƙatun lafiyar iyalin mai bayarwa. Idan mun shirya karɓar dasshe idan muna da buƙatar hakan, to ya kamata mu kasance a shirye don bayarwa Ɗa'a: Ƙa'idodin Jagora na WHO kan Dashen Tantanin halitta da Tishu da Gaɓoɓin Jiki A 1987, Majalisar Kiwon Lafiya ta Duniya ta arba'in, ta damu da kasuwanci don riba kan sassan jikin mutum, ta fara shirye-shiryen Ƙa'idodin Jagora na farko na WHO game da dashe, wanda Majalisar ta amince da shi a 1991 a ƙuduri na WHA44.25. Waɗannan Ƙa'idodin Jagora sun yi tasiri sosai ga ƙa'idodin ƙwararru da ayyuka da kuma dokoki a duk duniya cikin kusan shekaru ashirin. Bayan tuntuɓa wadda ta ɗauki shekaru da yawa, Majalisar Kiwon Lafiya ta Duniya ta Sittin da Uku ta amince da ƙuduri na WHA63.22 a ranar 21 ga Mayu 2010, tare da amincewa da sabunta Ƙa'idodin Jagororanci na WHO da gano wuraren ci gaba don inganta ayyukan ba da gudummawa da dasawa. Sanarwar Istanbul Ƙwararru na ba da gudummawa da dasawa daga dukan yankuna, ta hanyar ƙungiyoyi da cibiyoyi da yawa, suna goyon bayan Sanarwar Istanbul game da fataucin sassan jiki da yawon shaƙatawa da aka bunƙasa a ƙarƙashin jagorancin ƙungiyar dashe da kuma Ƙungiya Nephrology ta Ƙasa-da-ƙasa a watan Mayun 2008.
translations.reference: The Guiding Principles mandate optimal care for donors and recipients. The transparent oversight of the health authorities over donation and transplantation activities is also essential to increase the trust of the public in the system. In addition, the decision to be a donor is often based on the understanding that a contribution to the availability of transplant resources may someday benefit the health needs of the donor’s family. If we are prepared to receive a transplant should we need one, then we should be ready to give Ethics: WHO Guiding Principles on Human Cell, Tissue and Organ Transplantation In 1987 the fortieth World Health Assembly, concerned at the trade for profit in human organs, initiated the preparation of the first WHO Guiding Principles on Transplantation, endorsed by the Assembly in 1991 in resolution WHA44.25. These Guiding Principles have greatly influenced professional codes and practices as well as legislation around the world during almost two decades. After a consultation process that took several years, the Sixty-third World Health Assembly adopted resolution WHA63.22 on 21 May 2010, endorsing the updated WHO Guiding Principles and identifying areas of progress to optimize donation and transplantation practices. The Declaration of Istanbul Professionals of donation and transplantation from all regions, through many of their organizations and institutions, are endorsing the Declaration of Istanbul on organ trafficking and transplant tourism developed under the leadership of the Transplantation Society and the International Society of Nephrology in May 2008.
translations.hypothesis: The Code of Practice provides valuable guidance to both providers and recipients. External oversight of public health response activities and post-disaster reconstruction is critical to increasing public confidence in the system. Moreover, the decision to donate is often based on the understanding that the support provided through transplantation can address critical health needs of family members. If we plan to receive organs when needed, we should be willing to donate WHO’s Code of Practice on the Procurement, Storage, and Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues In 1987, the Thirty-ninth World Health Assembly, concerned by the growing commercialization of organ transplantation, initiated the development of the first WHO Code of Practice on the transplantation of organs and tissues, which was adopted by the Assembly in 1991 in resolution WHA44.25. The Code of Practice has served as a model for professional standards, policies and legislation around the world for nearly two decades. After years of consultations, the Sixty-third World Health Assembly adopted the resolution WHA63.22 on 21 May 2010, approving the revised WHO Code of Practice and identifying areas for improvement in the performance of transplantation activities. Istanbul Declaration Professionals from all regions, through many organizations and institutions, supported the Istanbul Declaration on the Procurement and Transplantation of Human Organs, Tissues and Cells, developed under the aegis of the Transplantation Society and the International Society of Nephrology, in May 2008.

translations.source: Tafiya da lafiya Taƙaitaccen Bayani: Tafiya tsakanin ƙasashe na iya barazana na haɗari daban-daban ga lafiya, wanda ya danganta da yanayin matafiyin da ita tafiyar. Matafiya na iya haɗuwa da mahimman canje-canje a lokaci guda a cikin ladabi da yanayin zafi da ƙwayoyin halitta da zafin jiki waɗanda zasu iya haifar da rashin lafiya. Bugu da ƙari, munanan haɗarurruka ga lafiya na iya fitowa a cikin wuraren da babu wadata da ingancin tsaftar jiki da muhalli, ayyukan likitanci ba a tsara su da kyau ba haka kuma babu tsaftataccen ruwa. Tafiya tsakanin ƙasashe na ƙaruwa, yadda ya zama miliyoyin mutane ke tafiya don aiki, zamantakewa, nishaɗi da kuma dalilai na aikin jin ƙaidalilai kowace shekara. Dole ne dukkanin matafiya su shirya don nau'ikan haɗari ga lafiya da za a iya samu cikin yanayin da ba a sani ba a kafin da yayin da kuma bayan tafiya. Ya kamata mutane da ke shirin tafiya su nemi shawara kan haɗarin da za su iya samu a wurin da zasu je kuma su fahimci hanyar da zasu kare lafiyarsu da kuma yadda zasu rage haɗarin kamuwa da cuta. Shirin gaba sune, matakan da suka dace da taka tsantsan na iya kare lafiyar matafiya, kuma suna rage haɗarin haɗari da samun cuta. Kodayake masana'antar likitanci da masana'antar tafiye-tafiye na iya samar da taimako mai yawa da kuma shawara kyau, ya kasance da alhakin matafiya ne neman bayanai da fahimtar haɗarurrukan da ke ƙunshe da kuma ɗaukan matakan kariya da suka dace don kiyaye lafiyarsu yayin tafiya. Haɗari: Yayin tantance haɗarurrukan lafiya na tafiya ƙasashen a duniya, ya kamata matafiya da ma'aikatan kiwon lafiya suyi la'akari da waɗannan manyan abubuwan da za a kawo:
translations.reference: Travel and health Overview: International travel can pose various risks to health, depending on the characteristics of both the traveller and the travel. Travellers may encounter sudden and significant changes in altitude, humidity, microbes, and temperature, which can result in ill-health. In addition, serious health risks may arise in areas where accommodation is of poor quality, hygiene and sanitation are inadequate, medical services are not well developed and clean water is unavailable. International travel is on the rise, as millions of people travel for professional, social, recreational and humanitarian purposes each year. All travellers must prepare for the variety of health risks they can be exposed to in unfamiliar environments before, during and after they travel. People planning to travel should seek advice on the potential hazards in their chosen destinations and understand how best to protect their health and minimize the risk of acquiring disease. Forward planning, appropriate preventive measures and careful precautions can protect the health of travellers, and minimize the risks of accident and of acquiring disease. Although the medical profession and the travel industry can provide extensive help and sound advice, it remains the traveller’s responsibility to seek information, to understand the risks involved and to take the necessary precautions to protect their health while travelling. Risk: When determining the health risks of international travel, travellers and health professionals should consider the following key factors:
translations.hypothesis: Health risks of international travel Overview: International travel can pose a range of health risks, depending on the traveller’s health status and the nature of the journey. Travellers may be exposed to new and challenging environmental, biological and physical risk factors which can cause illness. In addition, negative health effects may arise in the context of inadequate basic hygiene and sanitation, unsafe food, poor medical facilities and lack of clean water. Flows of people across international borders have increased dramatically in recent decades, with millions of people travelling for work, education, leisure and other reasons every year. All travellers should be prepared for possible health risks in the unfamiliar environment before, during and after their journey. People planning to travel should seek information about the risks to which they may be exposed in their destination and learn how to protect their health and reduce the risk of getting sick. Appropriate preventative measures can protect the health of travellers, and reduce the risk of harm and disease. Although the medical and travel industries can provide extensive support and valuable advice, it is ultimately the responsibility of the traveller to seek information, understand the risks involved, and take necessary precautions to protect their health while travelling. Risks: When assessing health risks of international travel, travellers and health care professionals should consider the following factors:

translations.source: yanayin sufuri Wurin zuwa Tsawon lokaci da yanayin tafiya Dalilin yin tafiya ƙa'idojin masauƙi da tsaftace abinci da muhalli halayyar matafiyi Yanayin lafiyar matafiyi Matafiya na iya riskar waɗannan haɗurran ga lafiya dangane da wurin da suke zuwa: cizon dabbobi da na ƙwari, wanda ya ƙunshi sauro da tantana da ƙwari masu shan jini da sauran ƙwari da zasu iya yaɗa cuta kamar zazzaɓin sauro haɗuwa da jini ko wasu ruwa na jiki
translations.reference: mode of transport destination(s) duration and season of travel purpose of travel standards of accommodation, food hygiene and sanitation behaviour of the traveller underlying health of the traveller Travellers may encounter the following health risks depending on their destination: animal and insect bites, including mosquitoes, ticks, fleas, and some flies, which can spread diseases such as malaria exposure to blood or other bodily fluids
translations.hypothesis: Mode of transport Destination Length of trip and travel conditions Reason for travel Accommodation standards and quality of food hygiene and environmental sanitation Traveler's behaviour Health status of the traveler(s) Travelers may be at risk of the following health concerns depending on their destination: vector-borne diseases, including malaria, dengue, yellow fever, chikungunya and Zika virus diseases; water-borne diseases, including cholera, typhoid and hepatitis A; food-borne diseases, including salmonellosis, campylobacteriosis, shigellosis, hepatitis A and norovirus; respiratory infections, including influenza, tuberculosis and COVID-19; HIV; malaria; meningococcal meningitis; and yellow fever.

translations.source: Canjin yanayi kamar tsauni, zafi, yanayin zafi/sanyi cutukan da ake samu a abinci da ruwa ƙarancin ayyukan kiwon lafiya raunuka, gami da wanda ake samu daga haɗarin kan titi ko daga ayyukan nishaɗi lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa, gami da damuwa da kuma firgici Hakanan matafiya zasu iya haɗuwa da cututtuka da dama, kuma da yawa daga cikin waɗannan za a iya daƙile su ta hanyar alurar rigakafi. Duk da haka, akwai wasu cututtuka, ciki har da wasu daga cikin mafiya haɗari, waɗanda ba rigakafinsu. Wuraren da inda masauƙi ya ke da tsafta da aikin kiwon lafiya da ruwa mai kyau na da ƙarancin barazana ga lafiyar matafiya. Inda ba a samar da waɗannan ayyukan ba, ya kamata matafiya su ɗauki tsattsauran matakan kariya don gujewa rashin lafiya. Ya kamata a dauƙi gargaɗi bisa tafiya daga majiyoyin gwamnati da mahimmanci.
translations.reference: environmental changes, such as altitude, humidity, temperature foodborne and waterborne diseases inadequate medical services injuries, including from road traffic accidents or recreational activities psychological health, including stress and culture shock Travellers may also be exposed to a number of infectious diseases, and many of these can be prevented by vaccination. However, there are some infectious diseases, including some of the most dangerous, for which no vaccines exist. Destinations where accommodation, hygiene and sanitation, medical care and water quality are of a high standard pose relatively few serious risks to the health of travellers. Where these services are not provided, travellers should take stringent precautions to avoid illness. Travel warnings from governmental sources should be taken seriously.
translations.hypothesis: Climate-related factors such as altitude, heat, humidity and extreme temperatures Food- and water-borne diseases Lack of health services Injuries, including those resulting from traffic accidents or recreational activities Mental health, including depression and anxiety Travellers may also be at risk of contracting a range of infectious diseases, some of which may be preventable by vaccination. However, there are some diseases, including some of the most serious, for which there is no preventable vaccine. Areas with good sanitation and medical and water supplies generally pose a low health risk to travellers. Where these services are lacking, travellers should take extra care to avoid becoming ill. Heed all travel advisories issued by your government.

translations.source: Yin rigakafi: Kafin tafiya: tuntuɓi cibiyar magungunan matafiya ko likita, mafi dacewa, makonni 4-8 kafin tafiya don karɓar duk wani rigakafi da ake buƙata; Yi karatu kan cututtukan gida masu alaƙa da wurin da zaka je; nemi bayani game da haɗarin zazzabin cizon sauro da rigakafin cizon sauro. Wannan na iya ƙunsar sayan magani na kariya da tattara sangen gado mai kwarar ƙwari; yi binciken lafiyar jiki da na haƙori; samu takardar magani bisa tsawon zama ka kuma tattara duk magungunan da suka dace; sayi inshorar kiwon lafiya da duk abin da ya dace a ƙasar waje A lokacin tafiya: Ku ci abincin da aka dafa sosai kaɗai da abin sha wanda aka sanya a cikin kwalba mai sanyi. A tafasa ruwan sha idan akwai shakku akan tsaftarsa.
translations.reference: Prevention: Before travel: contact a travel medicine centre or a physician, preferably 4–8 weeks before departure to receive any required vaccinations; read up on local diseases related to your destination; request information on malaria risk and prevention of mosquito bites. This may include purchasing appropriate preventive medication and packing a bednet and insect repellent; get a medical and dental check-up; obtain prescriptions for medication according to length of stay and assemble a suitable medical kit; purchase medical insurance with appropriate cover abroad During travel: eat only thoroughly cooked food and drink only bottled or packaged cold drinks. Boil drinking-water if safety is doubtful.
translations.hypothesis: Prevention: Before you travel: contact your local travel clinic or health professional, ideally 4–8 weeks before you travel to receive any necessary vaccinations; read up on the diseases endemic to the region you are visiting; find out about malaria risks and prevention measures.
