translations.source: Kiwon lafiyar mata Taƙaitaccen bayani: kasancewa namiji ko mace abu ne mai muhimmanci ga batun lafiya saboda irin bambance-bambance da ke samu na halitta. Lafiyar mata da ƙananan yara mata na da muhimmanci domin a wasu al'ummatan sukan rasa gata saboda bambanci da ke da alaƙa da al'ada ta rayuwar yau da kullum. Ga misali mata da ƙananan yara mata na fuskantar barazanar kamuwa da HIV/AIDS. wasu daga ciki dalilai masu alaƙa da al'ada ta yau da kullum da ke daƙile mata daga samun ingantaccen kulawa ta lafiya sun hada da: bambancin iko da ke akwai tsakanin maza da mata; Tsarin zamantakewa da ke daƙile ilimi da batun damarmaki na aikin da za a biya mutum; Ba wa ɓangaren batun rawar mata wajen haihuwa muhimmanci; da da kuma fuskantar cin zarafi na sarari ko na fannin saduwa ko na imoshan. Duk da talauci na taka rawa wajen kawo cikas ga samun ingantaccen kiwon lafiya ga maza da mata; mata da ƙananan yara mata sun fi fuskantar ƙalubalen talauci, ga misali ɓangaren cin abinci (rashin wadataccen abinci) da amfani da abin girki masu illa (COPD).
translations.reference: Women's health Overview: Being a man or a woman has a significant impact on health, as a result of both biological and gender-related differences. The health of women and girls is of particular concern because, in many societies, they are disadvantaged by discrimination rooted in sociocultural factors. For example, women and girls face increased vulnerability to HIV/AIDS. Some of the sociocultural factors that prevent women and girls to benefit from quality health services and attaining the best possible level of health include: unequal power relationships between men and women; social norms that decrease education and paid employment opportunities; an exclusive focus on women’s reproductive roles; and potential or actual experience of physical, sexual and emotional violence. While poverty is an important barrier to positive health outcomes for both men and women, poverty tends to yield a higher burden on women and girls’ health due to, for example, feeding practices (malnutrition) and use of unsafe cooking fuels (COPD).
translations.hypothesis: Women's health Overview: Sex and gender are important determinants of health, due to the different ways that women and men experience and interact with their environments. Women’s and girls’ health matters because in many societies they are disadvantaged by gender norms and expectations that limit their possibilities and choices in life. For example, women and girls face greater risks of HIV/AIDS. Other gender-related barriers to women’s and girls’ health include: gender-based power imbalances; social norms that limit women’s and girls’ education and economic opportunities; the prioritization of women’s roles in child-rearing; and women’s and girls’ lower status in society and experience of violence. Although poverty is a barrier to good health for both women and men, women and girls often face greater barriers than men and boys due to gender inequality. For example, women and girls are more likely to be food insecure (lacking access to enough safe and nutritious food) and less likely to receive treatment for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

translations.source: cutar fata (Endemic treponematoses) Taƙaitaccen bayani: cutar fata ta Yaws cutar fata ce mai tsananin gaske da ke da yanayi na kumburi da gyambo (ciwo). Bakteriyar da ake kira Treponema Pallidum ce ke haifar da wannan cutar fata wacce aka sanya ta cikin kashin baktariyar da ke haifar da sifilis da ake samu ta hanyar saduwa. cutar fata ta Yaws ta fi shafar yara 'yan ƙasa da shekaru 15 da ke rayuwa cikin talauci a wuri mai yanayin zafi a yankin Afirka da Asiya da Latin America da tsibirin Fasifik. Mafi yawan waɗanda ke kamuwa da cutar na rayuwa ne a ƙauyuka da ke da nisa da wuraren kiwon lafiya. Talauci da yanayi na rashin abin hannu da rashin tsabta ne ke taimakawa wajen yaɗuwar cutar fata ta Yaws. duk da akwai rahotanni 80000 na kamuwa da cutar fata ta Yaws a duk shekara, masana sun yi amanna cewa za a iya magance cutar da ma kawar da ita saboda da dalilai masu yawa. Da farko dai ana samun cutar ne a cikin bil'Adama ba dabba ba wanda ke nuna sauƙin magance cutar. Za a iya magance cutar cikin sauƙi ta hanyar amfani da magunguna da tuni akwai su kamar yadda aka yi nasarar kawar da cutar a wasu ƙasashe kamar Indiya. Wasu 'yan ƙalilan da ke da cutar na zaune a keɓantattun wurare wanda hakan ke nuna sauƙin daƙile yaɗuwarta idana aka yi amfani da matakai na bibiya da kulawa.
translations.reference: Yaws (Endemic treponematoses) Overview: Yaws is a chronic skin infection characterized by papillomas (noncancerous lumps) and ulcers. It is caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum subspecies pertenue, which belongs to the same group of bacteria that causes venereal syphilis. Yaws primarily affects children aged under 15 years who live in poor communities in warm, humid and tropical forested areas of Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Pacific islands. The majority of affected populations live rural areas, far from health services. Poverty, low socio-economic conditions and poor personal hygiene facilitate the spread of yaws. Although there are over 80 000 cases of yaws each year, experts believe the disease can be controlled and ultimately eradicated for several reasons. First, it only occurs in humans, not animals, making control much easier. It is also easy to treat with readily available drugs and has already been eliminated in some countries, including India. The remaining pockets of yaws infection, although usually in remote places, means further spread is less likely with proper surveillance and control measures.
translations.hypothesis: Endemic treponematoses Overview: Yaws (or treponematosis) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease that is caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum pertenue, a close relative of the bacterium that causes syphilis. Yaws primarily affects children under 15 years of age living in impoverished tropical areas of Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the Western Pacific. Most cases occur in rural villages far from medical facilities. Poverty, poor nutrition and poor hygiene contribute to the spread of yaws. Despite 80 000 cases of yaws being reported annually, experts believe the disease is both preventable and curable for a number of reasons. The disease is primarily found in humans and not animals, indicating an easier eradication process. The disease can be easily treated with existing medicines and has already been successfully eradicated in some countries, including India. The few remaining endemic countries are located in remote areas, which means that the spread of the disease can be easily stopped if proper monitoring and control measures are implemented.

translations.source: Alamomin kamuwa: Akwai matakai biyu na kwamuwa da cutar fata ta Yaws. mataki na farko shi ne matakin da mai larurar ke ɗauke da cutar kuma zai iya yaɗawa ga sauran mutane. a wannan mataki a kan samu ɓullowar ƙurji (wanda bai shafi kansa ba da ke ɓullowa kamar ƙurji) wanda ke fara girma da zarar mutum ya kamu da shi. ƙurjin yana dauke da ƙwayar cutar da kuma kan ɗauki watanni 3-6 ana maganinsa. Idan kuma ba a ɗauki mataki na magani ba, yana cigaba da yaɗuwa ne a kan fatar zuwa sauran sassan jiki. ana iya fara jin raɗaɗi daga cikin ƙashi da musayar lafiyayyen ƙashi da wani. mataki na biyu shi ne matakin da cutar ba za ta iya yaɗuwa ba wanda hakan na faruwa ne kusan shekaru biyar da kamuwa da cutar. ana iya fayyace cutar da ƙandarewar hanci da ƙashi da tafin hannu/dunduniya (kaurara). bayan nazarin alamomin cutar, za a iya tabbatar da cutar ne kawai idan aka haska fatar da wata nau'in nau'irar ganin ƙwaƙwaf ta musamman (darkfield examination). ba cika amfani da gwajin jini ba saboda cutar fata ta yaws na da alaƙa da bakteriyar da ke haifar da cutar sifilis, don haka sakamako ɗaya za a samu na cututtukan biyu.
translations.reference: Symptoms: There are two stages of yaws infection. The early stage is when the patient is infectious and can spread the disease to others. In this stage, a papule (a noncancerous, outward-growing lump) develops at the site of infection. This papule is full of the organisms and may persist for 3–6 months followed by natural healing. Without treatment, this is followed by disseminated skin lesions over the body. Bone pain and bone lesions may also occur. The second stage is noninfectious and typically appears five years after infection. It is characterized by disabling consequences of the nose, bones and palmar/plantar hyperkeratosis (thickening). After a field diagnosis based on these symptoms, the disease can be confirmed by examining a sample from a skin legion under a special type of microscope (darkfield examination). Blood tests are not typically used because yaws is closely related to the bacterium that causes syphilis and the two diseases will show the same result.
translations.hypothesis: Symptoms: There are two stages of yaws infection. The first is the primary stage when the person is most infectious and can spread the infection to other people. In this stage, there is a slow-growing (over months to years) non-cancerous (benign) growth that usually starts on the extremities (arms and legs). The growth is full of bacteria and can take 3–6 months to heal with treatment. If left untreated, it progresses to involve deeper structures and eventually bone. There may be severe pain and loss of a part of the body. The second is the late-stage of the disease, which occurs about 5 years after infection. It can be diagnosed by observing the characteristic skin eruption and the associated thickened, shiny skin (elephantiasis). After clinical examination, the diagnosis can be confirmed by observing the organism in a slit-skin smear examined with a special darkfield microscope. Blood tests are not useful as yaws is caused by the same bacteria that causes syphilis and the results will be the same for both diseases.

translations.source: Magani: A yanzu ba babu wata rigakafi ta cutar fata ta yaws. Ilimantarwa da inganta tsabtar jiki su ne muhimman dabarun da ake amfani da su na kariya. ana iya amfani da nau'o'in antibayotik guda biyu wajen maganin cutar fata ta yaws. an yi ba da shawarar amfani da maganin sha na azithromycin (30 mg/kg, maximum 2 g). za a iya amfani da maganin Benzathine penicillin (ta hanyar allura sau ɗaya) a kan waon 0.6 (ga yara 'yan ƙasa da shekaru 10) da awon 1.2 (ga yara 'yan sama da shekaru 10) ga marasa lafiya da ake zargin gazawar maganin da aka ɗora su a kai bayan azithromycin ko marasa lafiyar da laurarsu ta fi ƙarfin azithromycin. wannan mataki na magani sai warkar kashi 95% na masu cutar, sai dai akwai buƙatar sake duba su bayan mako 4 da karɓar antibiyotik ɗin. wani bincike ya nuna bayanan da suka gabata daga 1950 cewa ƙasashe 90 da yankuna suna fama da cutar fata ta yaws. kuma 14 cikin 90 na ƙasashen ne ke da bayanan na kusa-kusa a kan cutar fata ta yaws idan aka yi la'akari da tsarin bibiyar cutar, duk da cewa waɗannan al'ƙaluma ka iya zama manuniya ce ta wanzuwar wannan cutar, sai dai an rage mata ƙarfi. Ƙasashen Ghana da Papua New Guineada Tsibirin Solomon sun tabbatar da cewa suna samun sama masu cutar 10000 a kowacce shekara. Ƙasashen Ecuado da India sun yi nasarar daƙile yaɗuwar cutar.
translations.reference: Treatment: There is currently no vaccine for yaws. Health education and improved personal hygiene are the most important tactics for prevention. Two antibiotics can be used to treat yaws. A single oral dose of azithromycin (30 mg/kg, maximum 2 g) is the recommended treatment. Benzathine penicillin (single intramuscular dose) at 0.6 million units (children aged under 10 years) and 1.2 million units (people aged over 10 years) can be used for patients with suspected clinical treatment failure after azithromycin, or patients who cannot be treated with azithromycin. This treatment will result in complete clinical healing in 95% of cases but patients should be re-examined 4 weeks after receiving the antibiotics. A review of the historic documents from 1950s shows that over 90 countries and territories were endemic for yaws. Only 14 out of the 90 countries and territories have recent data on yaws based on the routine surveillance system; however, these figures may just be an indication of the presence of the disease and not its full extent. Ghana, Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands report over 10 000 cases per year. Ecuador and India appear to have interrupted transmission.
translations.hypothesis: Treatment: There is no vaccine for yaws. Health education and good hygiene are important measures for prevention. Two antibiotics can be used to treat yaws. Oral azithromycin (30 mg/kg single dose, maximum 2 g) is the antibiotic of choice. Benzathine penicillin (intramuscular injection) can be used in doses of 0.6 g (for children under 10 years) and 1.2 g (for children over 10 years) for patients who do not respond to azithromycin or for those in whom azithromycin is contraindicated. This treatment is curative in 95% of patients, but a re-evaluation 4 weeks after the end of treatment is necessary. A recent analysis of available data from 1950 showed that 90 countries and territories had cases of yaws. Only 14 of the 90 countries had recent data on the number of yaws cases, considered as the number of cases reported through the surveillance system, although these figures are likely to be an underestimation of the true number of cases. Ghana, Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands each reported over 1000 cases annually. Ecuador and India have each eliminated yaws as a public health problem.

translations.source: Zazzaɓin masassara ko shawara Taƙaitaccen bayani: zazzaɓin masassara ko shawara cuta ce da 'yan Adam ke kamuwa da ita ta hanayr ciwon sauri. akwai yuwuwar yaɗuwarsa kuma ana iya magance ta ta hanyar rigakafi. waɗannan sauraye da ke cizo na iya hayayyafa a kusa da muhallan mutane (domestic) da dazuka (wild) da kuma duka muhallan biyu (semi-domestic). masassara ko shawara zazzaɓi ne mai tasiri kuma cuta mai illar gaske da ke da yuwuwar yaɗuwa a duniya wanda ake kallo a matsayin barazana ga kiwon lafiya a duniya. akwai hanyoyi 3 na hanyoyin yaɗuwar cutar: Sylvatic; cutar na yaɗuwa ne ta hanyar ciwon da sauraye ke yi wa birrai wanda daga nan ne suke yaɗa wa sauran birrai da mutane. zazzaɓin masassara ko shawara tsakanin halittu biyu na yaɗuwa ne a lokacin da sauraye suka harbi birrai da mutane. wannan nau'i ne na cuta ake yawan samun ɓarkewarsa a yankin Afirka. Zazzaɓin masassara na iya yaɗuwa a birane idan mutanen da suka harbu tare da yaɗa ta a wuraren da ke da yawan sauraye a kuma muhallin da mutane ke da ƙarancin kariya daga cutar. a wasu lokutan matafiya ne yaɗa wannan zazzaɓi na masassara a ƙasashen da ba su da ita.
translations.reference: Yellow fever Overview: Yellow fever is a viral disease that is transmitted to humans by the bites of infected mosquitoes. It is prone to epidemics and is preventable with a vaccine. These day-biting mosquitoes breed around houses (domestic), in forests or jungles (wild), or in both habitats (semi-domestic). Yellow fever is a high-impact, high-threat disease, with a risk of international spread, representing a potential threat to global health security. There are 3 types of transmission cycles: Sylvatic (or jungle) yellow fever spreads when monkeys are bitten by wild mosquitoes that pass the virus on to other monkeys and humans. Intermediate yellow fever spreads when semi-domestic mosquitoes infect both monkeys and people. This is the most common type of outbreak in Africa. Urban yellow fever can cause large epidemics when infected people introduce the virus into heavily populated areas with high mosquito density and where people have little immunity. Occasionally, infected travellers have exported cases to countries that are free of yellow fever.
translations.hypothesis: Mpox (monkeypox) Overview: Human mpox is a zoonosis – a disease that is transmitted to humans from animals – with a high case fatality ratio. It is a highly contagious disease and can be controlled with vaccination. These animals can live in close proximity to humans (domestic), wildlife (wild) or both (semi-domestic). Mpox is a significant public health risk with global implications and is considered a threat to global health security. There are three main modes of transmission: Sylvatic: the virus is transmitted to humans through contact with infected animals, their bodily fluids, or contaminated materials, with subsequent human-to-human transmission. Human-to-human transmission of mpox occurs primarily through close contact with infected people or contaminated materials. This form of the disease is more common in Africa. Mpox can also spread in urban settings if there are people with close contact with infected people and if there are local rodent populations that can act as a source of infection for people with little or no immunity to the virus. In some cases, the virus has been spread by travellers to countries where the disease is not endemic.

translations.source: kodayake, ƙwayar cutar na yaɗuwa cikin sauƙi ne a ƙasashen da ke da nau'in wannan sauro wanda ke iya yaɗa cutar, ko wani yanayi da kuma yawan dabbobin da ke iya ajiye ƙwayar cutar. Alamomin kamuwa da cutar: zazzaɓin masassara na da alamomin mabambanta. da zarar mutum ya kamu, ƙwayar cutar na ƙyanƙyashewa a jikinsa ne tsakanin kwanaki 3-6. Wasu mutane ba za sa jin alamun kamuwa, amma idan hakan ta faru, mafi yawan alamun da mutum ke ji shi ne zazzaɓi, zugi tare da ciwon baya da ciwon kai da rashin son cin abinci da jin hararwa ko yin amai. A mafi yawancin lokuta akan nemi alamun zazzaɓin a rasa bayan kwanaki 3-4. wasu daga cikin marasa lafiya suna shiga mataki na biyu kuma mafi haɗari bayan awanni 24 daga daina jin alamomin farko. Zazzaɓi mai zafi na dawowa da kuma ke shafar sassan jiki da dama kamar hanta da ƙodoji. A wannan mataki, akwai yuwuwar mutane su fuskanci sauyin launi a wani sashe na jiki (sauyawar launin fata da ƙwayar idanu zuwa launin rawaya wanda hakan ya sa ake kiran cutar da 'yellow fever') da bawali mai launin baƙi da ciwon ciki da hararwa. Ana iya samun zubar jini daga baki da hanci da idanu ko ciki. Rabin waɗannan marasa lafiya sun mutu a cikin kwananki 7-10.cutar zazzaɓin yana da wuyar ganewa,musamman a lokacin farkon matakan.
translations.reference: However, the disease can only spread easily to a new country if there are mosquito species able to transmit it, specific climatic conditions, and the animal reservoir needed to maintain it. Symptoms: Yellow fever can present with a wide range of symptoms and severity. Once contracted, the yellow fever virus incubates in the body for 3–6 days. Many people do not experience symptoms, but when these do occur, the most common are fever, muscle pain with prominent backache, headache, loss of appetite, and nausea or vomiting. In most cases, symptoms disappear after 3–4 days. A small percentage of patients enter a second, more toxic phase within 24 hours of recovering from initial symptoms. High fever returns and several body systems are affected, usually the liver and kidneys. In this phase, people are likely to develop jaundice (yellowing of the skin and eyes, hence the name yellow fever), dark urine, and abdominal pain with vomiting. Bleeding can occur from the mouth, nose, eyes, or stomach. Half of these patients die within 7–10 days.Yellow fever is difficult to diagnose, especially during the early stages.
translations.hypothesis: However, the virus is endemic in countries with the right mosquito vectors, or in areas with high population movement and high vector population. Symptoms: Yellow fever has a wide spectrum of symptoms. Once infected, the virus multiplies in the body between 3–6 days. Some people do not develop any symptoms, but when they do, the most common are fever, muscle ache, backache, headache, nausea and vomiting. The fever usually lasts 3–4 days. Some patients may progress to the second, more serious phase within 24 hours of initial symptom onset. Severe forms of the disease can also cause jaundice (yellowing of the skin and eyes), and bleeding disorders, with blood in the vomitus, faeces, urine or through the gums. Half of these patients die within 7–10 days. Yellow fever is difficult to detect in the early stages.

translations.source: Za'a iya rikitar da lamura masu tsanani tare da matsanancin zazzabin cizon sauro, leptospirosis, hepatitis na kwayar cuta (musamman nau'ikan fulminant), sauran zazzabi na haemorrhagic, kamuwa da wasu flaviviruses (kamar zazzabin haemorrhagic na dengue) da guba. Gwajin polymerase{PCR} a cikin jini da fitsari wani lokaci na gano ƙwayar cutar a farkon matakan cutar. A cikin matakai na gaba, ana buƙatar gwaji don gano ƙwayoyin cutar (IgM). Matakin magance cutar:kamuwa da zazzaɓin masassara na iya haifar da mummunar cuta kuma na iya zama mai kisa a lokuta masu tsanani. tallafin magani na farko a asibitoci yana inganta ƙimar rayuwa. A halin yanzu babu wani takamaiman maganin rigakafin ƙwayar cuta don zazzaɓi, amma takamaiman kulawa don magance rashin isashshen ruwa a jiki, zazzabi, da gazawar hanta da koda yana inganta sakamako. Ana iya magance ƙwayoyin cuta masu alaƙa da maganin rigakafi. Marasa lafiya suna buƙatar zama a gidan sauro da rana don irage haɗarin yadawa ga wasu ta hanyar cizon sauro. Alurar riga kafi ita ce hanya mafi mahimmanci don hana zazzabi. Za a iya hana barkewar cutar ne kawai idan an yiwa yawancin jama'a allurar rigakafi.
translations.reference: More severe cases can be confused with severe malaria, leptospirosis, viral hepatitis (especially fulminant forms), other haemorrhagic fevers, infection with other flaviviruses (such as dengue haemorrhagic fever) and poisoning. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing in blood and urine can sometimes detect the virus in early stages of the disease. In later stages, testing to identify antibodies is needed (IgM). Treatment: Yellow fever infections can cause serious illness and can be fatal in severe cases. Early supportive treatment in hospitals improves survival rates. There is currently no specific anti-viral drug for yellow fever, but specific care to treat dehydration, fever, and liver and kidney failure improves outcomes. Associated bacterial infections can be treated with antibiotics. Patients need to stay under mosquito nets during the day to limit the risk of spreading to others through mosquito bites. Vaccination is the single most important measure for preventing yellow fever. The prevention of outbreaks can only be achieved if the majority of the population is immunized.
translations.hypothesis: Serious complications can occur with severe malaria, leptospirosis, viral hepatitis (especially fulminant forms), other haemorrhagic fevers, infections with other flaviviruses (such as dengue fever) and cholera. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) in blood and urine can sometimes detect the virus early in the course of infection. In later stages, serological tests for antibodies (IgM) are needed to confirm the infection. Treatment: Severe malaria can cause serious complications and can be fatal in severe cases. Early supportive care in a hospital setting improves outcomes. There is currently no specific antiviral drug treatment for dengue, but careful management of dehydration, fever, and liver and kidney failure improves outcomes. There are vaccines for some of the related viruses. Patients should take care to avoid mosquito bites during the day to prevent infecting others with the virus. Vaccination is the most important way to prevent malaria. Only a high level of population immunity can prevent outbreaks.

translations.source: Maganin cutar zazzabin shawara yana da aminci kuma mai araha, kuma kashi ɗaya na alluran rigakafi yana ba da rigakafi na tsawon rayuwa daga cutar. Mutanen da suka warke daga kamuwa da cutar zazzaɓi kuma suna da kariya har tsawon rayuwars. ƙara karantawa game da allurar rigakafin zazzaɓin cizon sauro. Kula da sauro na iya taimakawa wajen hana zazzabin rawaya kuma yana da mahimmanci a cikin yanayin da allurar rigakafi ba ta da yawa ko kuma ba a samun rigakafin nan da nan. Kula da sauro ya haɗa da kawar da wuraren da sauro ke hayayyafa da kashe manya sauro da tsutsa ta hanyar amfani da maganin kashe kwari a wuraren da ke da yawan sauro. Shigar da al'umma ta hanyar ayyuka, kamar tsaftace magudanar ruwa da kuma rufe kwantena na ruwa inda sauro ke iya hayayyafa hanya ce mai mahimmanci kuma mai inganci don magance sauro.
translations.reference: The yellow fever vaccine is safe and affordable, and a single dose provides life-long immunity against the disease. People who recover from yellow fever infection are also protected for life. Read more about the yellow fever vaccine. Mosquito control can also help to prevent yellow fever and is vital in situations where vaccination coverage is low or the vaccine is not immediately available. Mosquito control includes eliminating sites where mosquitoes can breed and killing adult mosquitoes and larvae by using insecticides in areas with high mosquito density. Community involvement through activities, such as cleaning household drains and covering water containers where mosquitoes can breed is an important and effective way to control mosquitoes.
translations.hypothesis: The typhoid vaccine is safe and inexpensive, and a single dose provides lifelong immunity to the disease. People who recover from typhoid fever also have lifelong immunity. Read more about typhoid vaccination Mosquito control can also prevent dengue and is particularly important in areas where the vaccine is not yet widely available or where vaccination is not immediately possible. Mosquito control includes eliminating mosquito breeding sites, killing adult mosquitoes and applying insecticide to areas where mosquitoes land. Community initiatives such as cleaning up trash and covering water storage containers where mosquitoes can breed are also effective and sustainable ways to control mosquitoes.

translations.source: An bar mutanen da ke da buƙatar kulawar likita a baya cikin raɗaɗi, sabon rahoto ya bayyana. Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya (WHO) ta fitar da wani sabon rahoto kan samun damar yin amfani da sinadarin morphine a matsayin magani, wanda ya bayyana yadda rarraba morphine a duniya a matsayin maganin raɗaɗi mai mahimmanci, bai daidaita ba kuma baya biyan bukatun likita.B50. Rahoton, mai taken "cikin raɗaɗi", yana nuna matsalolin samun damar yin amfani da wannan magani mai mahimmanci tare da bayyana hanyoyin samar da shi cikin ta hanyar daidaitattun manufofi. Duk da cewa morphine magani ne mai inganci kuma mai sauƙin farashi don kawar da raɗaɗi mai ƙarfi, wanda aka jera tun 1977 a cikin wallafar WHO ta farko na jerin samfuran Mahimman Magunguna, rarrabuwar kai a cikin ƙasashe yana da ƙarfi. Akwai bambanci ninki 5 zuwa 63 a kiyasin matsakaicin yawan amfani da morphine tsakanin ƙasashe masu samun kuɗin shiga da ƙasashe masu ƙaramin karfi. Yanayin amfani ya bambanta sosai a cikin ƙasashe masu irin wannan arziki; Bai dace da buƙatun kiwon lafiya ba, kamar yadda ƙiyasin adadin kwanakin da mutane ke fama da raɗaɗi ko fama da matsanancin ƙarancin numfashi ga masu fama da rashin lafiyan da ba na tashi ba. Wadannan bayanan sun yi daidai da na Hukumar Lancet ta 2018 wacce ta bayyana rashin samun damar yin amfani da magungunan rage jin zafi a matsayin daya daga cikin rashin adalci mafi muni, a harkar kiwon lafiya ta duniya tare da 10% mafiya arzikin ƙasashe da ke daukar kashi 90% na morphine da aka rarraba. daidai opioids. Barin mutane cikin raɗaɗi a lokacin da ake samun ingantattun magunguna don magance raɗaɗin ciwo, musamman a yanayin kula da lafiya na karshen rayuwa, ya kamata ya zama abin damuwa ga masu tsara manufofi, in ji Dokta Yukiko Nakatani, Mataimakin Daraktan WHO. -Gabaɗaya don Magunguna da Kayayyakin Lafiya. Dole ne mu yi kira da gaggawa a samar da morphine kan lokaci ga waɗanda ke cikin buƙatun likita ta hanyar madaidaitan manufofi, a ko'ina.
translations.reference: People with medical needs are “left behind in pain” reveals new report The World Health Organization (WHO) has published a new report on access to morphine for medical use, which describes how the global distribution of morphine, as a vital pain medicine, is unequal and does not fulfil the medical need. The report, titled “Left behind in pain”, highlights the problems in access to this essential medicine and offers actions to improve safe access through balanced policy. Despite morphine being an effective and relatively low-cost medicine for relieving strong pain, listed since 1977 in the first edition of the WHO Model list of Essential Medicines, the disparity in access across countries is stark. There is a 5- to 63-fold difference in the estimated median consumption of morphine between high-income countries and lower income countries. Consumption pattern varies significantly across countries of similar wealth; it does not correspond to medical need, as indicated by the estimated number of days people are in pain or suffer with severe shortness of breath for people with a terminal illness. This data echoes that of the 2018 Lancet Commission which described the lack of access to pain relief medication as ‘one of the most heinous, hidden inequities in global health’ with the richest 10% of countries possessing 90% of distributed morphine-equivalent opioids. “Leaving people in pain when effective medicines are available for pain management, especially in the context of end-of-life care, should be a cause of serious concern for policy-makers,” says Dr Yukiko Nakatani, WHO Assistant Director-General for Medicines and Health Products. “We must urgently advocate for safe and timely access to morphine for those in medical need through balanced policy, everywhere.”
translations.hypothesis: Patients left to suffer in pain, new report reveals The World Health Organization (WHO) published a new report on access to morphine for pain relief, showing that global availability of morphine as an essential pain medication is inadequate and uneven, and far from meeting the need. The report, titled “In unbearable pain”, highlights the challenges in access to this essential medicine and sets out a roadmap for improving access through appropriate policies. Despite being a safe and effective pain reliever, and listed on the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (EML) since its first edition in 1977, availability of morphine in countries is limited. There is a 5-63 times greater disparity in morphine consumption between high- and low-income countries. Even within countries of similar income levels, consumption varies widely and rarely reflects underlying need, whether it be palliative care needs, or the needs of those with cancer, HIV/AIDS, or those suffering from severe injuries or end-stage chronic illnesses. These findings echo the 2018 Lancet Commission on pain relief, which identified inadequate access to pain medication as one of the world’s greatest health inequities, with just 10% of the world’s wealthiest countries receiving 90% of available morphine. “Leaving people to live with unrelenting pain when safe and effective treatments are available, particularly at the end of life, should be of concern to all policymakers,” said Dr Yukiko Nakatani, WHO Assistant Director-General for Access to Medicines and Health Products. “We must act now to ensure timely access to morphine for those in need through appropriate policies in place, wherever they are.”

translations.source: Dalilan banbance-banbance Damar samun morphine a matsayin magani yana da alaƙa da abubuwa da dama da suka haɗa da shugabanci nagari, ingantaccen sayayya da hanyoyin samar da kayayyaki, wadatar albarkatu da ayyukan haɓaka iya aiki, tare da shamakain da ke da alaƙa da ƙaƙƙarfan dokoki da manufofi, ƙarancin bayar da kulawa, da rashin fahimtar halaye da fahimta. Duba da yanayin ƙasashe daban-daban, abubuwan da ke samar da dama da tsaiko da fifiko wajen mahimmancin ɗaukar mataki sun bambanta; wani binciken masu ruwa da tsaki da aka gabatar a wannan rahoto, mai masu amsa tambayoyi daga mambobin ƙasashen WHO guda 105, ya tabbatar da wannan bambancin. Misali, ana ɗaukar rashin samar da sinadarin morphine da sauran magungunan opioid masu karfi a wuraren kiwon lafiya saboda ƙarancin kuɗaɗe a matsayin wani shamakai a ƙasashe masu ƙaramin karfi da matsakaicin kuɗin shiga idan aka kwatanta da ƙasashe masu tasowa. Fiye da kashi ɗaya bisa uku na waɗanda suka amsa tambayoyi a duk faɗin yankuna sun bayyana cewa dalilan dake kawo cikas sun shafi dokoki da ƙa'idoji, a yayin da suka fahimci muhimmancin tsarin doka da ƙa'ida wajen samar da dama cikin aminci. ƙayyadaddun buƙatu na babu gaira babu dalili na iya kawo cikas ga majiyyaci wajen samun dama saboda suna hana samarwa ko rubutawa da rarrabawa ga ma'aikatan kiwon lafiya. Yana da kyau a lura cewa damuwa game da yuwuwar illolin magungunan opioid abu ne mai tushe, kamar yuwuwar su na haifar da matsalolin dakr da alaƙa da amfani da opioids. Saboda wannan dalili, ɗaukan wani mataki na taka tsantsan game da yuwuwar cutarwar amfani da opioid (misali amfani a cikin ciwon daji na yau da kullun ba tare da ciwon daji ba) yana da mahimmanci ga lafiyar jama'a matuƙar an san amfaninsa daidai yake da haɗarinsa. Kada ire-iren waɗannan damuwa su lalata fa'idojin amfani da magungunan opioid lokacin da lafiya ta buƙaci hakan da lokacin amfani da su ta hanyar ƙwararrun ma'aikata. Damar daukar mataki: Rahoton ya gabatar da wasu jerin ɓangarorin ɗaukar matakai da nufin inganta damar samun morphine.
translations.reference: Reasons for the disparity Access to morphine for medical use is influenced by many interacting factors including enablers related to good governance, reliable/efficient procurement and supply processes, resource availability and capacity-building activities, along with barriers related to overly restrictive legislation and policies, inadequate service provision, and misinformed attitudes and perception. Given different country contexts, enablers, barriers and priorities for action vary; a stakeholder survey presented in this report, with respondents from 105 WHO Member States, confirms this variation. For example, irregular supply of morphine and other strong opioids at health facilities due to limited financing were commonly noted as a barrier in low- and middle-income countries compared to high-income countries. More than a third of respondents across all regions also noted barriers arising from legislative and regulatory factors while recognizing the importance of a legislative and regulatory framework in achieving safe access. Unduly restrictive requirements could hamper patient access because they impede the flow of supply or make prescribing and dispensing difficult for health-care professionals. It is important to note that concerns about the potential harmful effects of opioids are valid, such as their potential to lead to opioid use disorder. For this reason, a certain amount of caution about the potential harms of opioid use (e.g. use in chronic non-cancer pain) is important for public health insofar as its use is well-informed and proportionate to risks. Such concerns should not undermine the benefits of opioid use when clinically indicated and when used safely by trained professionals. Opportunities for actionThe report presents a complementary set of areas for action that aim to improve safe access to morphine.
translations.hypothesis: Reasons for differences Access to morphine as an essential medicine is affected by many factors including good governance, efficient procurement and supply systems, availability of resources and quality capacity building activities, and enabling environments created by related formal rules and policies, and by less formal social norms and understandings. Given the varying circumstances across countries, the enabling factors and barriers to action and the priorities for action differ; a survey of stakeholders conducted for this report, with responses from 105 WHO Member States, confirmed this diversity. For example, the unavailability of morphine and other strong opioids in health facilities is more likely to be related to lack of financial resources than to formal restrictions in low- and middle-income countries as compared to high-income countries. Over a third of respondents across regions indicated that the greatest barriers were related to regulations and legislation, while also recognizing the importance of a supportive legal framework to enable access. Unnecessary restrictions can lead to patients being denied access to necessary medications because they prevent the supply, prescription, and distribution of controlled medicines to patients by health professionals. It is important to note that concerns about the potential harms of opioids are legitimate, including the risk of developing opioid use disorder and the risk of respiratory depression and death associated with opioid use. For this reason, a cautious approach to the prevention of opioid use disorder (e.g. opioid-naive patients with chronic non-cancer pain) is warranted in the public health interest, provided the potential benefits outweigh the risks. These concerns should not, however, prevent appropriate use of the medicines for pain relief in palliative care and other settings where there is a clear need and benefit and where the medicines are used under the supervision of health-care professionals. Policy actions: The report proposes a series of policy actions aimed at improving access to morphine.

translations.source: Waɗannan sun haɗa da aiwatar da ƙananan shirye-shirye na yankuna da na jihohi kan haɓaka damar yin amfani da morphine wajen kiwon lafiya tare da mahimman ayyuka da kayayyaki don kulawa da jin daɗi, wanda aka tsara akan Jerin Kayayyakin WHO na Mahimman Magunguna da Muhimman Ƙunshin Lafiya na Kulawar WHO. Har ila yau, sun haɗa da inganta tsarin mulki, daidaita sayayya da hanyoyin samar da kayayyaki don magance duk wani tasgaro, inganta kayan aiki kamar samar da kuɗaɗe, samar da ƙwarewa a ma'aikatar kiwon lafiya, da wayar da kan jama'a game da fa'idodi da illar amfani da opioid. Nasarar waɗannan ayyukan za ta ta'allaƙa ne kan haɗin gwiwa da haɗin kai tsakanin dukkan masu ruwa da tsaki a matakan ƙasa, yanki da duniya baki ɗaya.
translations.reference: These include implementing small-scale regional or state-wide programmes on improving access to morphine for medical use with a package of essential services and products for palliative care that is formulated according to the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines and the WHO Essential Package of Palliative Care. They also include improving governance, streamlining procurement and supply processes to address any inefficiency, improving resourcing such as stable funding, enhancing competent skill sets of the health workforce, and raising awareness about both the benefits and potential harms of opioid use. The success of these actions will hinge on collaboration and cooperation among all stakeholders at national, regional, and global levels.
translations.hypothesis: These include the implementation of regional and national action plans on increasing access to morphine for pain relief, with key elements and outputs laid out in the WHO List of Essential Medicines and the WHO Model List of Essential in vitro Diagnostics. They also include strengthening governance, regulating procurement and supply systems to avoid waste, improving infrastructure such as financing, developing workforce capacity in health care, and raising public awareness of the benefits and risks of opioid use. The success of these efforts will depend on collaboration and coordination among all relevant stakeholders at national, regional and global levels.

translations.source: Ƙananan tsibirai sun amince kan babban shirin ayyuka kan cututtukan da ba sa yaɗuwa da cututtukan ƙwaƙwalwa. A yau, an ƙaddamar da sanarwar Bridgetown na 2023 akan Cututtukan da ba sa yaɗuwa (NCDs) da Lafiyar Ƙwaƙwalwa, don magance wasu cututtukan masu tsanani a duniya a cikin Ƙananan Tsibirai masu tasowa (SIDS), musamman waɗanda ke cikin haɗari. Sanarwar ita ce mahimmiyar sakamako na taron ministocin SIDS kan cututtukan da ba sa yaɗuwa (NCDs) da lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa, wanda ke gudana daga ranar 14 zuwa 16 ga Yuni, wanda Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya (WHO), da kuma Pan American Health Organisation (PAHO) suka shirya. Gwamnatin Barbados. NCDs na da matuƙar tasiri ga SIDS, wanda hakan ke haifar da kashi 74% na duk mace-mace a duniya saboda dogaro da abincin da ake shigowa da su daga waje, tasirin kasuwanci da kuma rikicewar yanayi. Wani sabon rahoton na WHO ya bayyana cewa 8 daga cikin ƙasashe 15 da ke da fiye da kashi 30 cikin dari na haɗarin mutuwa da wuri daga cututtukan zuciya, ciwon daji, ciwon sukari, ko cututtukan numfashi na yau da kullun sune SID. Ƙasashe 10 da ke da mafiya yawan masu fama da cutar ƙiba a duniya duk SID ne a cikin Pasifik, inda sama da kashi 45% na manya ke rayuwa da cutar ƙiba. Matsalolin lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa ya zama ruwan dare a cikin ƙasashen SIDS, wanda ya shafi kimanin kashi 15.2 na yawan jama'ar Caribbean da kashi 11.2 na yawan jama'ar Pasifik. Mutanen da ke fama da matsalar lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa suna fuskantar haɗarin mutuwa da wuri, rashin samun isasshen kulawa ta lafiyar jiki gami da kuma yunkurin kashe kawunansu. Abin kunya, ƙarancin ƙwararrun ma'aikata da tasirin sauyin yanayi suna ba da gudummawa wajen fuskantar ƙalubale a cikin SIDS wanda ke buƙatar kulawa da gaggawa. Sanarwar Bridgetown ta 2023 ta zayyana ƙwararan matakai don magance matsalolin zamantakewa, muhalli, tattalin arziki da kasuwanci waɗanda ke haifar da NCDs da yanayin lafiyar hankali.
translations.reference: Small islands agree bold plan of action on noncommunicable diseases and mental health Today, the 2023 Bridgetown Declaration on Noncommunicable Diseases (NCDs) and Mental Health was launched, to address some of the world’s deadliest diseases in Small Island Developing States (SIDS), which are especially at risk. The Declaration is a key outcome of the SIDS Ministerial Conference on Noncommunicable Diseases (NCDs) and Mental Health, running from 14 to 16 June, co-hosted by the World Health Organization (WHO), the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) and the Government of Barbados. SIDS are disproportionately impacted by NCDs – which cause 74% of all deaths globally – due to their reliance on imported food, commercial influences and the climate crisis. A new WHO report shows that 8 of the 15 countries with more than a 30% risk of premature death from cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, or chronic respiratory disease are SIDS. The 10 countries with the highest obesity rates globally are all SIDS in the Pacific, where over 45% of adults live with obesity. Mental health conditions are common in SIDS countries, affecting an estimated 15.2% of the population in the Caribbean and 11.2% of the population in the Pacific. People with mental health conditions face a higher risk of premature mortality, including from unaddressed physical health conditions and from suicide. Stigma, specialized staff shortages and the impact of climate change contribute to a challenging situation in SIDS that requires immediate attention. The 2023 Bridgetown Declaration outlines bold steps to address the range of social, environmental, economic and commercial issues that lead to NCDs and mental health conditions.
translations.hypothesis: Small island states commit to big actions on noncommunicable diseases and mental health Today, the Bridgetown Declaration 2023 on Noncommunicable Diseases (NCDs) and Mental Health was launched, to address some of the world’s most pressing health issues in Small Island Developing States (SIDS), many of which are also high-risk. The declaration is a key output of the SIDS Ministerial Conference on NCDs and Mental Health, held June 14-16, 2023, in Bridgetown, Barbados, co-convened by the World Health Organization (WHO), the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) and the Government of Barbados. NCDs are a major health threat to SIDS, accounting for 74% of all deaths globally due to their reliance on imported foods, susceptibility to trade-related factors and climate change. A new WHO report shows that 8 of the 15 countries with the highest percentage of premature deaths from cardiovascular diseases, cancers, diabetes and chronic respiratory diseases are SIDS. The 10 countries with the highest rates of obesity in the world are all SIDS in the Pacific, where over 45% of adults live with obesity. Mental health challenges are also pervasive in SIDS, affecting an estimated 15.2% of the Caribbean population and 11.2% of the Pacific population. People with mental health conditions are at higher risk of suicide and premature mortality, and experience poorer physical health outcomes and lower quality of life. Tragically, a shortage of trained personnel and the impacts of climate change add to the many challenges faced by SIDS requiring urgent attention. The Bridgetown Declaration 2023 outlines concrete actions to address the social, environmental, economic and commercial determinants of NCDs and mental health conditions.

translations.source: Ta hanyar gamammiyar tsari da SID ta jagoranta, sanarwar ta nuna cewa ba za a iya magance NCDs da matsalolin lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa yadda ya kamata ba, ba tare da magance rikicin yanayi ba. Ɗaukan ƙwararan matakai da suka dace a game da yanayi, lafiya da kuma walwalarmu, ya dogara ne kan gyaran tsarin tafiyar da kuɗaɗe a duniya, don samar da biliyoyin hanyoyin zuba hannun jari, da rage wa ƙasashe masu tasowa nauyin biyan basussukan da ake bin su. Firayim Ministan Barbados. Bayar da kuɗi ga ƙasashe masu rauni don daidaitawa da sauyin yanayi abu ne mai muhimmanci, tare da ƙididdige cututtuka marasa yaɗuwa da lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa. Ƙalubalen da Jihohin masu tasowa a Kananan Tsibirai ke fuskanta, suna da alaƙa da juna, da fuskoki daban-daban. Sauyin yanayi, lalacewar muhalli, rashin daidaiton zamantakewa da tattalin arziki, da kuma hanyoyin kasuwanci na kiwon lafiya suna ƙara tsananta nauyin NCDs da yanayin lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa," in ji Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Darakta-Janar na WHO. Duk da ƙarancin albarkatun da suke da shi da kuma matsalar yanki, wadannan al’ummomi sun nuna matukar jajircewa wajen fuskantar matsaloli. Tare, dole ne mu samar da hanyar da ta ginu akan daidaito, juriya, da ɗorewa. Dole ne mu ƙarfafa tsarin kiwon lafiya, haɓaka matakan kariya da ganowa da wuri, da kuma ba da fifiko ga haɗin gwiwar NCD da ayyukan kula da lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa a cikin kiwon lafiya na farko. Darakta-Janar ɗin ya kuma yi alƙawarin cewa WHO za ta yi aiki don tattara kuɗaɗe don bunƙasa yanayin juriya, wuraren kula da lafiya masu ɗorewa a cikin SIDS. WHO za ta kuma ci gaba da bayar da shawarwari don samar da kuɗaɗe na asara da lalacewa don daidaita canjin yanayi da rage saka hannun jari a ƙasashe masu ƙaramin karfi.
translations.reference: Developed through an inclusive process led ‘for’ and ‘by’ SIDS, the declaration highlights that NCDs and mental health conditions cannot be properly addressed without responding to the climate crisis. “Bold action for our climate, good health, and well-being relies on redressing and reorganizing global financing to unlock billions in investment, while making it less punishing for developing countries to pay their debts,” said Her Excellency Mia Amor Mottley, Prime Minister of Barbados. “Funding for climate change adaptation and mitigation in the most vulnerable countries is also key, with noncommunicable diseases and mental health accounted for.” "The challenges faced by Small Island Developing States are interconnected and multifaceted. Climate change, environmental degradation, social and economic inequalities, and the commercial determinants of health exacerbate the burden of NCDs and mental health conditions," said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General. "Despite their limited resources and geographical constraints, these nations have shown remarkable resilience in the face of adversity. Together, we must forge a path that is based on equity, resilience, and sustainability. We must strengthen health systems, enhance prevention and early detection measures, and prioritize the integration of NCD and mental health services into primary health care. "The Director-General also pledged that WHO would work to mobilize financial resources to develop climate resilient, environmentally sustainable health-care facilities in the SIDS. WHO will also continue to advocate for ‘loss and damage’ funding for climate change adaptation and mitigation investments in lower income countries.
translations.hypothesis: Through a whole-of-society approach, led by the SID, the declaration recognizes that NCDs and mental health cannot be effectively addressed without tackling the climate crisis. “Scaled up action on climate, health and well-being rests on a transformed financial architecture, one that unlocks trillions of dollars in investment, and reduces the debt burden on developing countries.” - Hon. Mia Mottley, Prime Minister of Barbados. Financing climate adaptation and mitigation is essential, including for non-communicable diseases and mental health. “The challenges faced by Small Island Developing States are interconnected, with climate change, environmental degradation, social and economic inequities, and health systems all compounding the burden of NCDs and mental health conditions,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General. “Despite their limited resources and unique geographic challenges, these communities have demonstrated remarkable resilience in the face of adversity. Together, we must forge a path forward that is rooted in equity, sustainability, and resilience. We must strengthen health systems, improve prevention and early detection, and prioritize NCD and mental health services in primary health care.” The Director-General also committed WHO’s efforts to mobilize resources to improve climate resilience, and access to sustainable and universal health coverage in SIDS. WHO will also continue to advocate for loss and damage financing for climate adaptation and mitigation, and the replenishment of funds in low- and middle-income countries.

translations.source: A matsayin wani ɓangare na amincewa da sanarwar, SIDS ta sanya hannu don gudanar da ayyuka daban-daban, waɗanda suka shafi fannoni kamar haɗar da al'umma gabaɗaya, haɓaka aiwatarwa, tabbatar da saka hannun jari, daidaitawa tsakanin gwamnatoci da lissafin ci gaba. Taron ya kuma nuna takamaiman alƙawurra na SIDS akan NCDs da lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa, gami da inganta samun damar kula da lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa a wuraren kulawa na farko, sabunta dokokin sarrafa taba don rufe sigari da vaping, da rage yawan cin gishiri da sukari. Waɗannan alƙawuran sun yi daidai da mafi kyawun tsarin WHO masu sauƙin kuɗi, abubuwan da suka dogara da shaida don magance NCDs. A baya-bayan nan, an sabunta jerin mafiya kyawun sayayya a Majalisar Kiwon Lafiya ta Duniya a watan Mayu don haɗe ƙananan rigakafi ta cutar rheumatism, cikakkiyar kulawa da cutar numfashi mai tsanani da tsawo, cututtukan huhu, da kuma cututtukan kansar mahaifa, nono, colorectal, hanta da ciwon daji na yara, da kuma cikakken maganin cutar kansa ga masu ɗauke da cutar HIV. "SIDS a ƙasashen nahiyar Amurka na cigaba da zama masu rauni sosai ga NCDs. Wannan taron na ministoci ya zo a lokaci na musamman, kuma zai zama mabuɗi don ci gaba da tattaunawa, dangane matsalar (mutuwa ta fuju'a) SIDS, da kuma bayyana matsalar (cututtuka marasa yaɗuwa) NCDs, da matsalar (lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa ) a sahun gaba cikin jerin muhimman abubuwan tattaunwa, in ji Dr Jarbas Barbosa, Daraktan ( ƙungiyar lafiya ta Amurka)PAHO, kuma Daraktan (ƙungiyar likitoci ta duniya yankin Amurka) WHO. Domin tabbatar wannan yunƙurin, dole ne mu yi ƙoƙari yanzu. PAHO (ƙungiyar lafiya ta Amurka) a shirye take don tallafawa aiwatar da ayyukan gaggawa a yankinmu, gami da kula da waɗannan yanayi cikin ayyukan kiwon lafiya a ƙaramin mataki, da kuma cin gajiyar abubuwan bunƙasawa, kamar kayan aikin kiwon lafiya na na'ura. Ƙasashe masu fama da (mutuwar fuju'a) SIDS sun yi nasarar yanke shawara ta duniya; a nan ne birnin Spain (Port of Spain) da yankin ( SAMOA )suka shimfida yarjejeniya, wacce ta ba da damar yin sanarwar duniya a Karo na farko, dangane da cututtuka marasa yaduwa, (NCDs) a shekara ta 2018. Taron na ƙarawa juna sani, da sanarwar da ta gabata; za su haska babban taron majalisar Ɗinkin duniya da ke tafe, kan batun kiwon lafiyar duniya a watan Satumba na 2023 da kuma kan cututtuka marasa yaɗuwa (NCDs) a shekara ta 2025.
translations.reference: As part of agreeing the Declaration, SIDS signed up to undertake a suite of actions, covering areas such as engaging all of society, accelerating implementation, securing investments, aligning across governments and accounting for progress. The conference also showcased specific commitments by SIDS on NCDs and mental health, including to improve access to mental health care in primary care facilities, update tobacco control legislation to cover e-cigarettes and vaping, and reduce populations’ salt and sugar intake. These commitments align with WHO’s ‘best buys’ – a set of cost-effective, evidence-based interventions to tackle NCDs. The list of best buys was recently updated at the World Health Assembly in May to include secondary prevention for rheumatic fever, acute and long-term management of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease as well as several interventions for cervical, breast, colorectal, liver and childhood cancer, and the comprehensive treatment of cancer for those living with HIV. “SIDS in the Americas remain overwhelmingly vulnerable to NCDs. This Ministerial Conference comes at a unique time and will be key to amplifying the voice and needs of SIDS, bringing NCDs and mental health to the forefront of our priority list,” said Dr Jarbas Barbosa, PAHO Director, and WHO Regional Director for the Americas. “To build on this momentum, we must act now. PAHO is ready to support accelerated implementation of interventions in our region, including mainstreaming care for these conditions into primary health services and taking advantage of innovations such as digital health tools.” SIDS countries have a track record of driving global decision-making; their Port of Spain and SAMOA pathway agreements paved the way for the first-ever UN political declaration on NCDs in 2018. The conference and the Declaration will inform and shape forthcoming UN General Assembly High-Level Meetings on universal health coverage in September 2023 and on NCDs in 2025.
translations.hypothesis: As part of the declaration’s approval, the SIDS committed to actions across ten areas, including whole-of-society engagement, action implementation, investment promotion, government coordination, and progress tracking. The declaration also highlighted specific commitments made by the SIDS on NCDs and mental health, including improving access to mental health care in primary health care settings, updating tobacco control policies to include e-cigarettes and vaping, and reducing the consumption of salt, sugar and processed foods. These commitments are in line with WHO best buys, evidence-based interventions for NCDs. Just last month, the WHO Global Model List of Essential Medicines was updated to include new recommendations for smallpox, severe acute lower respiratory infections, chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases, and cancers of the cervix, breast, colorectal, liver and childhood cancers, as well as antiretroviral therapy for HIV. “SIDS in the Americas region continue to be disproportionately affected by NCDs. This Ministerial meeting is taking place at a critical time, and will serve as a vital catalyst for further progress on the SIDS-related NCD targets, goals and priorities, including mental health, which have been placed at the top of the global health agenda,” said Dr Jarbas Barbosa, Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) Director and WHO Regional Director for the Americas. “To ensure that this momentum is sustained, we must act now. PAHO stands ready to support urgent actions in our region, including the integration of these conditions into primary health care services, and the leveraging of innovations, such as digital health tools.” The SIDS Ministerial conference resulted in a historic global call to action; here in Port of Spain, the leaders of the Caribbean and Pacific islands made a joint declaration, the “Port of Spain Declaration”, in 2007, which gave rise to the first-ever United Nations high-level meeting on NCDs in 2018. The meeting’s outcome, the Political Declaration of the Third High-level Meeting of the General Assembly on the Prevention and Control of NCDs, will inform the global health agenda and actions on NCDs until 2030.

translations.source: Tattaunawar ƙungiyar ma'aikatan lafiya na duniya, na ma'abota shirin nazarin cututtukan yankuna masu fama da zafin Rana wa'yanda a kayi sake; ya ƙare da kiran ɗaukar mataki a fadin duniya. Jama'a da wakilai sun bar wajen shirin da aka yi na abokan hulɗar nazarin cututtukan yankuna masu fama da zafin rana; tare da kiran mayar da hankali wajen ɗaukar mataki daga darektanta Dr Ibrahima SocÃ Fall. Yayin da taron kasa da kasa, wanda ya samu halartar wasu manyan abokan hulɗa 300, ya samu ƙarƙarewa a Geneva a ranar Talata 13 ga watan Yuni, Dr Fall ya bukaci mahalarta taron da su dauki sakon cewa, idan ba mu kalubalanci kanmu ba, ba za mu iya ingantawa ba ko Cigaba. A cikin wani babban taron da aka gudanar don nazarin ci gaban (ƙungiyar likitoci ta duniya) WHO, a tsare - tsarenta don kula da cututtukan yankuna masu fama da zafin rana a 2021- 2030, da samar da kyakkyawar fahimta game da ayyukan ( cututtuka marasa yaɗuwa )NTD na duniya daga ƙayyadaddun cututtuka da kuma hangen gaba, abokan tarayya, masu ba da gudummawa, abokan fasaha, cibiyoyi da wakilan ƙasa; sun ƙarfafa himmarsu don cimma manufa mai fa'ida: a hasashen duniya Na kubuta daga cututtuka marasa yaɗuwa a yankunan masu fama da zafin rana a shekara ta 2030. Jigon taron ya tattara ne akan Samar da al'umma guda, wajen gudanar da shirin NTD na duniya bai ɗaya. Ta hanyar daukar bayanai masu mahimmanci guda, Wanda ya assasa tsarin mallakar nagartacciyar kasa, wajen auna cigaba ba hanyoyinsa ba, da jajircewa na al'amura , da haɗin gwiwa domin tabbatar da nuna kwarewa, abubuwan da aka tattauna an gudanar dasu a aikace , a bayyane kuma an yaɗata tare da buƙatar daidaito da adalci a harkar kiwon lafiya, domin daƙile matsalar NTDs. Irin wannan tsarin ne kawai, in ji taron, zai iya samar da sauyin da wasu al'ummomin duniya mafi talauci ke buƙata domin cimma muradun ci gaba mai dorewa na Majalisar ɗinkin Duniya a shekarar 2030. A cikin irin wannan taron na farko na duniya tun bayan ƙaddamar da tsarin a watan Janairun 2021, wakilai kuma sun ji ta bakin daraktan WHO - Janar Dr tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. Da yake maraba da mahalarta farkon taron na kwanaki biyu, Dr tedros ya ce, wannan taron ya bayya komai game da WHO, abokan hadin gwiwa da ke haduwa don yin amfani da karfin hadin gwiwarsu don magance kalubalen kiwon lafiyar duniya wanda babu daya daga cikimmu da zai iya magancewa shi kadai. Kalubale iri-iri kamar cututtukan yankuna masu fama zafi rana, da aka yi sake da su, kuma shi ne abin da muka kawo tare.
translations.reference: WHO’s Global Neglected Tropical Diseases Programme Partners’ Meeting ends with stirring call for worldwide action Delegates and representatives left the Global Neglected Tropical Diseases Programme Partners’ Meeting with a stirring call to action from its director Dr Ibrahima Socé Fall. As the multinational meeting, attended by some 300 key partners, came to an end in Geneva on Tuesday 13 June, Dr Fall urged participants to take on board the message that, “if we do not challenge ourselves, we cannot evolve and improve”. In a wide-ranging event held to review progress against the WHO road map for neglected tropical diseases 2021–2030 and generate a better understanding of global NTD operations from both disease-specific and cross-cutting perspectives, partners, donors, technical partners, institutions and country representatives reinforced their commitment to achieving an ambitious target: a world free from neglected tropical diseases by 2030. The meeting’s primary theme centred around the vision of “One community delivering one Global NTD Programme”. Taking their cues from the three key strategic shifts advocated in the road map – greater country ownership, measuring impacts not process, and a commitment to cross-cutting activities and collaboration for greater efficiency – discussions were pragmatic, clear-sighted and suffused also with the need for health equity and justice to tackle NTDs. Only such an approach, the meeting heard, can bring about the change that is needed by some of the world’s poorest communities to achieve the United Nations 2030 Sustainable Development Goals. In the first such global meeting since the launch of the road map in January 2021, delegates heard also from WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. Welcoming participants at the beginning of the two-day symposium, Dr Tedros said, “This gathering illustrates what WHO is all about – partners coming together to leverage their collective strength to address global health challenges that none of us could address alone. “A multifaceted challenge like neglected tropical diseases takes a multifaceted approach, and that is what we bring, together”.
translations.hypothesis: Global health workforce conference delegates call for urgent action to strengthen response to tropical diseases Communities and advocates leave conference with renewed hope for action on tropical diseases, thanks to commitment from Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus In a final act of the three-day conference, which drew to a close in Geneva on Tuesday 13 June, Dr Tedros asked delegates to take a message with them: “If we challenge ourselves, we can improve and move forward.” At the concluding session of the Strategic Roundtable on Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTDs) that WHO convened in December 2022, partners and stakeholders provided their views on the draft WHO road map to advance the fight against NTDs 2023–2030, the new WHO global NTD list, and the NTD road map implementation plan covering countries, partners, donors, technical partners, platforms and networks. They reinforced their commitment to achieving the goal of WHO’s NTD road map: a world free of NTDs by 2030. The tone of the meeting was captured by the title of one of the plenary sessions: “One Health, One Planet - uniting behind a shared agenda for NTDs”. Through the sharing of compelling stories, the establishment of guiding principles on quality country ownership, the measurement of progress beyond averages, and the commitment to shared responsibility and accountability, partners and delegates identified actions needed to improve the quality of services delivered to those affected by NTDs, and to address the underlying social and structural determinants of health inequities that drive the NTD burden. Only such an approach, the meeting heard, can deliver the transformative change that the world’s poorest communities need to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. In this first in-person meeting since the launch of the strategy in January 2021, delegates heard from WHO Director-General, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, who said: “This meeting is a testament to what can be achieved when WHO, partners and donors work together, combining their strengths to tackle some of the world’s most pressing health challenges, which none of us can solve alone. The breadth of the challenge is captured in the theme of the meeting: One Health, One Planet - uniting behind a shared agenda for NTDs.

translations.source: Wakilai da mahalarta taron sun shafe kwanaki biyu, suna bankaɗo manyan giɓina da ƙalubalen cimma manyan burika da kuma ƙalubale na gida. Waɗanda ke fuskantar ƙalubalen ƙasa da suka haɗa da mutanen da abin ya shafesu kaitsaye, dangane da NTDs da waɗanda ke da alhakin gudanar da ayyukan magance NTDa, an nemi su yarda, musamman ta fuskar sadarwa da haɗin gwiwar al'umma. Taron ya kuma lura da mahimmancin haɓaka al'ummomi masu kokari, don haɓaka iyawa da kwarin gwiwa da amincewar ma'aikatan NTD na duniya. A ci gaba da tattaunawa, wakilai sun amince da ka'idoji da matakai masu amfani don aiwatar da ayyuka zuwa ga maƙasudan da ake so a cimma, tare da tsarawa Bai ɗaya, domin ɗaukar mataki na duniya na 2025-2030. Muhimman matakai da yanke shawarwari a taron sun haɗa da shawarwari don ƙarfafawa da aiwatar da haɗin gwiwar amfani da kafafen sadarwa na zamani, don tabbatar da haɗin kai don cigaba da tsare - tsare, wajen lura da rairayewa, da kuma tabbatar da ingantaccen tsarin sarrafa kayan aiki a cikin tsarin kasa. Taron abokan hulɗar ya gudana kuma a ƙarshen babban aikin bita a cikin Sashen Kula da Cututtukan yankuna masu fama da zafin rana na WHO. A cikin watanni hudu da suka gabata, WHO tana jin gudumawa da shaida daga dukkan abokan hulɗarta da masu ruwa da tsaki, domin tabbatar da cewa ita kanta ta kunshi dabi’un rikon amana da gaskiya da daidaito,wanda ta yadda da kuma buƙata. Waɗannan abubuwa masu ƙima sun haɗa da tabbatar da cewa an bunƙasa NTDs a cikin tsare - tsaren cigaban kiwon lafiya na duniya. Mahalarta taron sun yi maraba da abin lura kan muhimman ayyukan da al'ummar NTD za su iya, kuma dole ne su bada gudummuwa ga manya - manyan kalubale, gamayyar harkar Lafiya ta Duniya, harkar lafiya ta Bai ɗaya, ƙaro ƙoƙarin magance barazanar sauyin yanayi a duniya. Wakilan da suka halarta kai tsaye sun sami damar jin daɗin wani baje kolin da aka keɓe don kula da cututtuka na yankuna masu fama da zafin rana a hedikwatar WHO.
translations.reference: Delegates and participants spent the subsequent two days identifying the major gaps and challenges to achieving high-level goals and local, on-the-ground challenges. Those on-the-ground challenges include ensuring that people directly affected by NTDs, and those directly responsible for administering interventions against NTDs, are solicited and acknowledged, particularly in terms of communication and community engagement. The meeting noted also the importance of developing communities of practice, in order to build the capacity and confidence of the global NTD workforce. In further discussions, delegates agreed on principles and practical steps to implement action towards the stated targets and planned together for a Global Action Plan for 2025–2030. Key actions and decisions arising from the meeting included recommendations for strengthening and operationalizing national coordination platforms to ensure coordination for joint planning and for monitoring and evaluation, and to ensure more efficient supply chain management within national systems. The Partners’ Meeting took place also at the end of a major functional review process within WHO’s Department of Control of Neglected Tropical Diseases. Over the course of the past four months, WHO has been hearing contributions and testimony from all its partners and stakeholders, in order to ensure that it itself embodies the values of accountability, transparency and equity that it espouses and demands. Those values also include ensuring that NTDs are repositioned in the global health architecture. Meeting participants welcomed the emphasis on the key roles that the NTD community can and must play in contributing to wider challenges such as Universal Health Coverage, One Health and the increasing threat of global climate change. Delegates attending in person were also able to enjoy an exhibition dedicated to neglected tropical diseases at WHO headquarters.
translations.hypothesis: Delegates and participants spent two days immersed in workshops, technical sessions, and informal discussions, sharing their top priorities, challenges, and national contexts. Those with country-level responsibilities, including national NTD focal points, those responsible for implementing NTD interventions, were asked to identify top priorities, especially in reference to communication, collaboration, and community engagement. The meeting also heard the importance of developing local champions, to improve country ownership and the sustainability of global efforts for NTDs. In an open discussion, participants agreed on key principles and priorities for actions towards the goal of universal health coverage, with a focus on pandemic preparedness, One Health, climate change and universal health coverage. Key actions and decisions resulting from the Summit include the recommendations to strengthen and leverage digital solutions for enhanced collaboration, coordination, monitoring, and accountability in pursuit of universal health coverage. The partner event took place at the end of a three-day technical consultation on the WHO Regional Tropical and subtropical mycetoma Initiative. Over the last four months, WHO has benefited from the input and advice of all partners and stakeholders consulted, in order to ensure that the new strategy is based on the values of equity, responsibility and solidarity, and meets the needs of affected communities. These priorities include the recognition that NTDs are included in global health equity initiatives. Participants in the Summit welcomed the recognition of key roles that the NTD community can play, and must play, in addressing major global challenges, including One Health, universal health coverage, and increasing global efforts to mitigate climate change. Delegates heard first-hand from three patient advocates during a special session dedicated to tropical disease priorities held at WHO headquarters.

translations.reference: Global Neglected Tropical Diseases Programme Partners’ Meeting, 12–13 June 2023 Representatives of the global NTD community will gather in Geneva next week to participate in the Global Neglected Tropical Diseases Programme Partners’ Meeting, which takes place in headquarters’ auditorium on 12-13 June 2023. The objectives of the meeting are to review progress on the WHO road map for neglected tropical diseases 2021–2030 and generate a better understanding of global NTD operations from both disease-specific and cross-cutting perspectives, as well as to engage in wide-ranging discussions around the vision for One WHO delivering on one Global NTD Programme. While previous global meetings of NTD partners were convened by WHO in 2007 and 2017, this third upcoming event is the first since the launch of the road map in January 2021. The WHO road map for neglected tropical diseases 2021–2030 is a comprehensive framework that outlines targets, mechanisms for alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals and other global agendas and calls for strategic shifts in NTD approaches with the aim of ending the epidemic of neglected tropical diseases by 2030. The meeting will focus on: reviewing current progress to achieving the 2030 targets; identifying the major gaps and challenges to reaching those targets; agreeing principles and practical steps for how to implement action towards the targets; galvanizing support and commitment from NTD partners to operationalize the shifts advocated in the road map and to achieve its targets; and
translations.hypothesis: Global NTD partners’ meeting, 12 - 13 June 2023 Delegates from around the world will meet in Geneva next week to discuss progress in the fight against neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), at the NTD partners’ platform meeting, taking place at WHO headquarters on 12-13 June 2023. The aim of the meeting is to take stock of progress against the WHO road map to control NTDs 2021-2030, provide a comprehensive overview of the current NTD landscape from the perspective of different diseases, discuss priorities and chart a path forward for the WHO NTD programme. While the previous global NTD partners’ meetings were held in 2007 and 2017, this third meeting is the first since the launch of the new road map in January 2021. The WHO road map to control NTDs 2021-2030 is a key strategic policy document that outlines cross-cutting themes, strategies and actions in line with the Sustainable Development Goals and other global initiatives, and charts a path forward for NTD control and elimination efforts with the vision of ending the NTD epidemic by 2030. The deliberations will focus on: reviewing progress made towards the 2030 targets; identifying major gaps and challenges encountered in reaching those targets; agreeing on key principles and priorities for actions to achieve the objectives; soliciting commitments and offers of support from NTD partners for actions proposed in the road map; and developing a plan for the implementation of the road map.

translations.reference: WHO announces winners of the 4th Health for All Film Festival 7 winning short films, 4 special mentions from the jury The World Health Organization has announced the official selection of this year’s winning films at its 4th Annual Health for All Film Festival, held at WHO Headquarters, Geneva. The event, attended in person and online by actors, producers and public figures, saw winning films announced for 7 different categories, while 4 films received special mentions from the jury. This is the fourth year of the film festival and competition was no less fierce, with some 93 shortlisted films covering issues ranging from anxiety and depression through to the effects of climate change on health, as well as the health challenges of people with disabilities. The films were judged by a panel of distinguished professionals, artists and activists, including the renown actors, Sharon Stone and Alfonso Herrera, dance choreographer, Sherrie Silver, climate activist, Sophia Kianni and media personality, Adelle Onyango. They were joined by senior United Nations officials and WHO staff. “The Health for All Film Festival brings a human face to WHO’s scientific work,” said WHO Director-General, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. “Listening to the voices of people affected by health issues is a powerful way to raise awareness and improve our understanding of people’s experiences and this can help us advance towards health for all.”
translations.hypothesis: WHO announces the winners of the 4th Global Health Film Festival Seven films win in the short film category, 4 special mentions from the Jury The winners of this year’s film competition were announced at the World Health Summit 4, the quadrennial conference on global health priorities, taking place at the WHO headquarters in Geneva. The event, which was attended by filmmakers, producers, and high-profile figures in person and via video messages, featured the winning films in seven categories, with four films receiving special mentions from the jury. This is the fourth edition of the film festival, and the competition was fierce, with 93 films selected from a pool of over 2000 submissions, covering topics as diverse as mental health, climate change and health, and disability and health. The films were judged by a panel of experts, artists and advocates, including Academy Award-winning actress, Sharon Stone; filmmaker, Alfonso Herrera; choreographer, Sherri Silver; disability rights advocate, Sophia Kianni; and media personality, Adelle Onyango. They were joined by senior officials and staff from the World Medical Association. “WHO is thrilled to host the fourth edition of the Global Health Film Festival,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General. “Listening to the stories of people affected by health issues is a powerful way to raise awareness and increase understanding of the challenges people face, and how we can work to improve health for everyone.”

translations.reference: From the official selection one “GRAND PRIX” is attributed for each of the three main competition categories: Universal Health Coverage, Health emergencies, and Better health and well-being, which align with WHO’s Triple Billion Targets. Sharon Stone, Golden Globe and Emmy Award-winning actress from the United States of America, producer and activist for health and humanitarian causes said: "I am delighted to be part of the Health for All Film Festival. This is about creating better awareness on crucial actions needed for reaching healthier living conditions around the world. The stories selected talk to us about the intrinsic value of good health and its access, and they advocate for universal health coverage. Universal Health Coverage is a very important right, it’s a human right for everyone around the world. "Four special prizes were also given for a Student-produced film, a film on Climate Change and Health, a film on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights and a Very Short Film. The theme of mental health featured heavily in this year’s winning entries, including a powerful and moving short film from Sweden about anxiety and depression. The film, set to a stirring soundtrack, featured a series of actors expressing different stages of anxiety and how it can manifest itself. The overall message was that you are not alone in experiencing negative thoughts and that it is okay to acknowledge such feelings.Another winning film, from Bangladesh, features a young boy who was exposed to lead from a local factory.
translations.hypothesis: From the Oscars to the Emmys, the Golden Globes and Sundance, the nominees and winners from Hollywood and beyond, are reminded that the most important role they can play is to help achieve universal health coverage.” The selected stories exemplify the true value and attainability of universal health coverage, and promote the concept of global health equity. Universal health coverage is a fundamental right, a human right for everyone in the world. Four special awards were also given for student-made films on climate and health, a film on sexual and reproductive health and rights, and two short films. The theme of mental health was also prominent in this year’s winning entries, including a powerful animated short from Sweden about depression and loneliness. The film, which is set to an original song, features a diverse cast of characters who each represent a different stage of depression and how it can manifest. Its overall message is that you are not alone if you experience negative thoughts and that it is okay to seek help. Another winning film, from Bangladesh, depicts a young boy who is being raised by a transgender man.
