translations.source: Samun makamashi na asali yana da alaƙa a tsakanin damar sabuntawa, sabon rahoton ya nuna An ci gaba da samun gibin samun wutar lantarki a duniya: Mutane miliyan 675 ba su da wutar lantarki, mutane biliyan 2.3 sun dogara da abubuwan girki masu ɗumama. Wani sabon rahoton da hukumar kula da ikon ƙasa da ƙasa (IEA), da hukumar sabunta ikon ƙasa da ƙasa (IRENA), da hukumar kididdiga ta majalisar dinkin duniya (UNSD) da bankin duniya, da hukumar lafiya ta duniya (WHO), suka fitar a yau, ya nuna cewa duniya bata kan hanyar cimma burin ci gaba mai dorewa (SDG) 7 don samun iko nan da 2030. A wannan shekara ta nuna rabin lokaci don cimma SDGs nan da 2030. SDG 7 shi ne tabbatar da samun dama Kai tsaye,, abin dogaro, da dorewa da iko na zamani. Makasudin ya hada da isar da damar samun wutar lantarki da dafa abinci mai tsafta, ninka matakan inganta ingantaccen aiki na tarihi, da kara yawan kason abubuwan da za a iya sabuntawa a cikin hadakar samun iko na duniya. Cimma wannan buri zai yi tasiri mai zurfi ga lafiyar mutane da walwala, yana taimakawa wajen kare su daga hatsarori na muhalli da zamantakewa kamar gurɓataccen iska, da faɗaɗa hanyoyin samun kulawa da kiwon lafiya na farko da ayyuka. Bibiyar gyaran 2023 SDG 7: bunƙasar samun iko ya bayyana rahoton kashedin cewa ƙoƙarin da ake yi yanzu bai isa ba don cimma SDG 7 akan lokaci. An sami ɗan ci gaba kan taƙamaiman abubuwa na ajandar SDG 7 - alal misali, ƙaruwar yawan amfani da abubuwan sabuntawa a fannin wutar lantarki - amma ci gaban bai isa ba don cimma manufofin da aka tsara a cikin SDGs. Ana sa ran rikicin samun makamashi na duniya zai haifar da tura abubuwan sabuntawa da ingantaccen iko tare da manufofin gwamnati da yawa da ke nuna karuwar saka hannun jari.
translations.reference: Basic energy access lags amid renewable opportunities, new report shows Global energy access gap persists: 675 million people without electricity, 2.3 billion people reliant on harmful cooking fuels A new report by the International Energy Agency (IEA), the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), the United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD), the World Bank, and the World Health Organization (WHO), released today, finds that the world is not on track to achieve the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7 for energy by 2030. This year marks the halfway point for achieving SDGs by 2030. SDG 7 is to ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy. The goal includes reaching universal access to electricity and clean cooking, doubling historic levels of efficiency improvements, and substantially increasing the share of renewables in the global energy mix. Attaining this goal will have a deep impact on people’s health and well-being, helping to protect them from environmental and social risks such as air pollution, and expanding access to primary health care and services. The 2023 edition of Tracking SDG 7: The Energy Progress Report warns that current efforts are not enough to achieve the SDG 7 on time. There has been some progress on specific elements of the SDG 7 agenda – for example, the increased rate of using renewables in the power sector – but progress is insufficient to reach the targets set forth in the SDGs. The global energy crisis is expected to stimulate the deployment of renewables and improve energy efficiency with several government policies pointing to increasing investment.
translations.hypothesis: Clean energy access is falling between the rhetoric and reality, new report finds Global electricity access deficit: 675 million people without electricity, 2.3 billion rely on polluting stoves A new report, published today by the International Energy Agency (IEA), the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), the United Nations Statistics Commission (UNSD), the World Bank, and the World Health Organization (WHO), shows the world is not on track to meet the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7 for universal access to electricity by 2030. This year marks the halfway point to achieving the SDGs by 2030. SDG 7 aims to ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy. The goal includes targets to expand access to electricity and clean cooking, increase the share of renewable energy in the global energy mix, and double the rate of improvement in energy efficiency. Achieving this goal would have far-reaching impacts on human health and well-being, helping to protect people from environmental and social risks such as air pollution, and expanding access to life-saving health interventions and services. Tracking progress SDG 7: Energy 2023 The report finds that current efforts are insufficient to meet the SDG 7 targets on time. There has been some progress on specific aspects of the SDG 7 agenda – for example, the increase in the share of renewables in electricity generation – but the overall progress has been insufficient to meet the targets set in the SDGs. The global energy crisis is expected to drive investments in new energy sources and increase the ambition of many governments.

translations.source: Ko yaya, ƙididdigar IRENA ta nuna cewa kwararar kudaden jama'a na ƙasa da ƙasa don tallafawa na samar da cikakken makamash, a cikin ƙasashe masu karamin karfi da matsakaita, suna na raguwa tun kafin barkewar cutar ta COVID-19 kuma an taƙaita kudade ga kananan ƙasashe. Don cimma burin SDG ta 7 da kuma tabbatar da cewa mutane sun ci gajiyar ci gaban zamantakewa da tattalin arziƙin na canjin makamashi mai dorewa, ya zama dole a sake fasalin tsarin kuɗin jama'a na duniya da ayyana sabbin damammaki don buɗe hannun jari. Rahoton ya kuma nuna cewa karuwar basussuka da hauhawar farashin na kara tabarbare hasashe na ganin an kai ga samun tsaftataccen makamashin dafa abinci da wutar lantarki. Hasashen da aka yi a halin yanzu ya nuna cewa mutane biliyan 1.9 ba za su rasa girki mai tsafta ba sannan miliyan 660 ba za su samu wutar lantarki ba a shekarar 2030 idan ba mu dauki wani mataki ba kuma a ci gaba da kokarin da ake yi a yanzu. wadannan giɓinan za su yi mummunan tasiri ga lafiyar al'ummar mu masu rauni da kuma hanzarta canjin yanayi. A cewar WHO, mutane miliyan 3.2 ne ke mutuwa a kowace shekara sakamakon rashin lafiya da amfani da gurbataccen mai da fasahohin kirki ke haifarwa, wanda ke kara yawan kamuwa da gurɓacewar iska na gida. Mahimmin sakamakon rahoton A cikin 2010, kashi 84% na al'ummar duniya sun sami wutar lantarki a wancan lokacin. wannan ya karu zuwa 91% a cikin 2021, ma'ana fiye da mutane biliyan sun sami damar shiga cikin wannan lokacin. Ko yaya, saurin haɓakar damar shiga ya ragu a cikin 2019 - 2021 idan aka kwatanta da shekarun da suka gabata.
translations.reference: However, IRENA estimates show that international public financial flows in support of clean energy in low- and middle-income countries have been decreasing since before the COVID-19 pandemic and funding is limited to a small number of countries. To meet SDG 7 targets and to ensure that people fully benefit from the socio-economic gains of the shift to sustainable energy, it is necessary to structurally reform international public finance and define new opportunities to unlock investments. The report also finds that mounting debt and rising energy prices are worsening the outlook for reaching universal access to clean cooking and electricity. Current projections estimate that 1.9 billion people will be without clean cooking and 660 million without electricity access in 2030 if we do not take further action and continue with current efforts. These gaps will negatively impact the health of our most vulnerable populations and accelerate climate change. According to WHO, 3.2 million people die each year from illness caused by the use of polluting fuels and technologies, which increase exposure to toxic levels of household air pollution. Key findings of the report In 2010, 84% of the world’s population had access to electricity. This increased to 91% in 2021, meaning more than a billion people gained access over that period. However, the growth pace of access slowed in 2019–2021 compared to previous years.
translations.hypothesis: Nevertheless, IRENA’s figures show that international public financial flows to support the energy transition in low- and middle-income countries have declined since before the COVID-19 pandemic and that the funds are insufficient for the poorest nations. To achieve the goals of SDG 7 and ensure that people can take advantage of the social and economic benefits of a clean energy transition, the international financial system must be reformed and new funding sources mobilized. The report also points out that rising interest rates and a strong US dollar are making it more difficult to achieve the goals for clean cooking and electricity access. Current projections show that 1.9 billion people will still be unable to access clean cooking and 660 million people will be without electricity in 2030 if we continue at current rates of progress. These gaps will have a devastating effect on the health of our most vulnerable populations and worsen the impacts of climate change. According to WHO, 3.2 million people die annually from health risks attributable to air pollution indoors, exacerbated by the use of polluting cooking technologies and fuels. Key findings In 2010, 84% of the world population had access to electricity. This increased to 91% in 2021, meaning over a billion people gained access during this time. However, the pace of increase slowed in 2019-2021 compared to the previous years.

translations.source: YunƘurin samar da wutar lantarki a yankunan karkara ya taimaka wajen wannan ci gaba, amma akwai babban giɓi a cikin birane. A cikin shekarar 2021, mutane miliyan 567 a yankin Sahara ba su da wutar lantarki, wanda ya kai sama da kashi 80% na al'ummar duniya ba tare da samun wutar lantarki ba. Rashin isa ga yankin ya ƙasance kusan daidai da na shekarar 2010. Duniya ta ƙasance a kan hanya don samun damar dafa abinci mai tsafta nan da 2030. Kimanin mutane biliyan 2.3 har yanzu suna amfani da gurbataccen mai da fasahohin dafa abinci, galibi a yankin Sahara da Asiya. Amfani da biomas na gargajiya yana nufin gidaje suna kwashe sama da sa'o'i 40 a mako suna tattara itace da dafa abinci, wanda ke hana mata neman aikin yi ko shiga cikin ƙungiyoyin yanke shawara na gida da yara zuwa makaranta. Bisa kididdigar da WHO ta yi a shekarar 2019, mutane miliyan 3.2 ne ke mutuwa da wuri a kowace shekara sakamakon gurɓacewar iska da aka haifar ta hanyar amfani da gurbataccen mai da fasahohin dafa abinci. Amfani da wutar lantarki mai sabuntawa a cikin amfani da duniya ya karu daga 26.3% a cikin 2019 zuwa 28.2% a cikin 2020, haɓaka mafi girma na shekara guda tun farkon sa ido kan ci gaban SDGs. Ƙoƙarin haɓaka rabo mai sabuntawa a cikin dumama da sufuri, wanda ke wakiltar sama da kashi uku cikin huɗu na amfani da makamashi na duniya, ya ci gaba da ƙasancewa a kan manufa don cimma manufofin yanayi na 1.5o C. Ƙarfin makamashi - ma'aunin makamashi na yawan makamashin da tattalin arzikin duniya ke amfani da shi kowace dala na GDP" ya inganta daga 2010 "2020 da 1.8% a kowace shekara.
translations.reference: Rural electrification efforts contributed to this progress, but a large gap within urban areas remains. In 2021, 567 million people in sub-Saharan Africa did not have access to electricity, accounting for more than 80% of the global population without access. The access deficit in the region stayed almost the same as in 2010. The world remains off track to achieve universal access to clean cooking by 2030. Up to 2.3 billion people still use polluting fuels and technologies for cooking, largely in sub-Saharan Africa and Asia. The use of traditional biomass also means households spend up to 40 hours a week gathering firewood and cooking, which prohibits women from pursuing employment or participating in local decision-making bodies and children from going to school. According to the 2019 WHO estimates, 3.2 million premature deaths each year were attributable to household air pollution created by using polluting fuels and technologies for cooking. Renewable electricity use in global consumption has grown from 26.3% in 2019 to 28.2% in 2020, the largest single-year increase since the start of tracking progress for the SDGs. Efforts to increase renewables’ share in heating and transport, which represent more than three quarters of global energy consumption, remain off target to achieve 1.5oC climate objectives. Energy intensity – the measure of how much energy the global economy uses per dollar of GDP – improved from 2010–2020 by 1.8% annually.
translations.hypothesis: The electrification of rural areas has aided this progress, but there remain large gaps in urban areas. In 2021, 567 million people in sub-Saharan Africa were without electricity, representing more than 80% of the global population without access. The access gap has remained virtually unchanged since 2010. The world is on track to achieve universal access to clean cooking by 2030. About 2.3 billion people still resort to polluting stoves and fuels, mostly in sub-Saharan Africa and Asia. The use of traditional biomass for cooking means that households spend 40 hours a week collecting fuelwood and cooking, keeping women in particular from paid employment or participation in local politics and children from going to school. According to WHO figures from 2019, 3.2 million people die prematurely each year from household air pollution, resulting from the use of polluting stoves and fuels. The share of renewables in global energy consumption increased from 26.3% in 2019 to 28.2% in 2020, the largest annual increase since the start of the SDG baseline. Efforts to decarbonize heating and transport, which account for three-quarters of global energy use, need to be accelerated to align with the 1.5 °C climate target. Energy intensity – a measure of how much energy the global economy uses per unit of GDP – has improved by 1.8% per year between 2010 and 2020.

translations.source: Wannan ya fi na kashi 1.2% inganta daga shekarun da suka gabata. Koyaya, ƙimar haɓakar ƙarfin makamashi ya ragu a cikin 'yan shekarun nan kuma ya ragu zuwa 0.6% a cikin 2020. Wannan ya sanya ta zama mafi munin shekara don haɓaka ƙarfin makamashi tun bayan rikicin kuɗin duniya, kodayake galibi saboda ƙuntatawa masu alaƙa da cutar, wanda na iya nuna koma baya na ɗan lokaci kawai. Ci gaban shekara-shekara ta 2030 dole ne yanzu matsakaita 3.4% don cimma burin SDG ta 7.3. Adadin kudaden jama'a na ƙasa da ƙasa don tallafawa tsaftataccen makamashi a cikin Ƙasashe masu tasowa ya tsaya a dalar Amurka biliyan 10.8 a cikin 2021, 35% Ƙasa da na 2010 “matsakaici na 2019 kuma kusan kashi 40% na kololuwar 2017 na dala biliyan 26.4. A cikin 2021, ƙasashe 19 sun sami kashi 80% na alkawuran. Za a gabatar da rahoton ga manyan masu yanke shawara a wani taron ƙaddamarwa na musamman a ranar 11 ga Yuli 2023 a Babban Taron Siyasa (HLPF) kan Ci Gaba mai ɗorewa, gabanin SDG na biyu Taron koli a watan Satumba na 2023 a New York. Marubutan sun tursasa al'ummomin ƙasa da ƙasa da masu tsara manufofi da su kiyaye nasarorin da aka samu wajen cimma burin SDG ta 7, don samar da sauye-sauyen tsarin, da kuma mai da hankali kan dabarun yaƙi da ƙasashe masu rauni da ke buƙatar tallafi mafi girma. Sharhi: Rikicin makamashi da mamayar Rasha ta yi wa Ukraine na ci gaba da yin tasiri sosai ga mutane a duk duniya. Haɓaka farashin makamashi ya yi fama da mafi rauni, musamman waɗanda ke cikin ƙasashe masu tasowar tattalin arziki. Yayin da tsaftataccen makamashi ke tafiya da sauri fiye da yadda mutane da yawa ke tunani, har yanzu akwai babban aiki da ake buƙata don isar da ɗorewa, mai aminci da kuma mai araha ga sabis na makamashi na zamani ga biliyoyin mutanen da ke rayuwa ba tare da shi ba. Nasarar canjin makamashi ta dogara ne akan ingantattun manufofi da sabbin fasahohi haɗe tare da tattara manyan jari.
translations.reference: This is higher than the 1.2% improvement from the previous decades. However, the rate of energy intensity improvement has slowed in recent years and dropped to 0.6% in 2020. This makes it the worst year for energy intensity improvement since the global financial crisis, albeit largely due to pandemic-related restrictions, which may indicate only a temporary setback. Annual improvements through 2030 must now average 3.4% to meet the SDG target 7.3. International public financial flows in support of clean energy in developing countries stand at US$ 10.8 billion in 2021, 35% less than the 2010–2019 average and only about 40% of the 2017 peak of US$ 26.4 billion. In 2021, 19 countries received 80% of the commitments.The report will be presented to top decision-makers at a special launch event on 11 July 2023 at the High-Level Political Forum (HLPF) on Sustainable Development, ahead of the second SDG Summit in September 2023 in New York. The authors urge the international community and policymakers to safeguard the gains made toward achieving SDG 7, to advance structural reforms, and to maintain a strategic focus on the vulnerable countries needing the most support. Quotes: “The energy crisis sparked by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine continues to have a profound impact on people all around the world. High energy prices have hit the most vulnerable hard, particularly those in developing economies. While the clean energy transition is moving faster than many think, there is still a great deal of work needed to deliver sustainable, secure and affordable access to modern energy services for the billions of people who live without it. Successful energy transitions rely on effective policies and technological innovation combined with large-scale mobilisation of investment capital.
translations.hypothesis: This is a larger increase than the 1.2% annual increase during the previous decade. However, the energy growth rate has declined in recent years and was 0.6% in 2020. This made it the slowest year for energy growth since the global financial crisis, although much of this was due to Covid-related restrictions, which may only have caused a temporary setback. Annual progress to 2030 must now average 3.4% to reach the SDG 7.3 target. Official international public finance for clean energy in developing countries totalled $10.8 billion in 2021, 35% less than in 2010 and 40% below the 2017 high of $26.4 billion. In 2021, 19 countries received 80% of commitments. The report will be presented to top decision-makers at the special launch event on 11 July 2023, at the United Nations High-Level Political Forum (HLPF) on Sustainable Development, just before the SDG Summit in September 2023 in New York. The authors urge international community and policymakers to protect the gains made towards achieving SDG 7, to accelerate the pace of change, and to focus on the countries and communities most affected and in need of the greatest support. Note: The energy crisis and the war in Ukraine continue to impact people around the world. Rising energy prices have hit the most vulnerable, especially in developing countries. While clean energy is growing faster than many realize, there is still a huge need for more investment to bring universal access to clean, reliable and affordable energy to the nearly 700 million people who still do not have it. The success of the energy transition rests on three pillars: effective policies, innovative technologies combined with smart investments.

translations.source: Dole ne ƙasashen duniya su yi amfani da dukkan wadannan kayayyakin aikin don cimma burin ci gaba mai dorewa nan da karshen wannan shekaru goma. Fatih Birol, Babban Daraktan Hukumar Makamashi ta Duniya. Sabuwar makamashi mai tsada ya sake nuna juriya na ban mamaki, amma mafi talauci a duniya har yanzu ba su iya amfana daga gare ta. Don gano SDG ta 7 ba tare da ɓata manufofin sauyin yanayi ba, dole ne mu kawo sauyi na tsarin yadda haɗin gwiwar duniya ke aiki. Yana da mahimmanci cewa cibiyoyin hada-hadar kuɗi da yawa suna jagorantar tafiyar da harkokin kuɗi cikin adalci a duk faɗin duniya don tallafawa tura abubuwan sabuntawa da haɓaka abubuwan more rayuwa na zahiri. Francesco La Kamara, Darakta-Janar, Hukumar Sabunta Makamashi ta Duniya. Duk da ci gaban da aka samu kan maƙasudan makamashi masu ɗorewa a tsakiyar ajandar 2030, Manufar ta 7 tana da wahala a cimma fiye da yadda yake a cikin 2015 kuma matakan haɓaka ya zama dole idan muna son tabbatar da samun damar samun araha, abin dogaro, ɗorewa da makamashi na zamani ga kowa da kowa. zuwa 2030. Samun wutar lantarki da dafa abinci mai tsafta har yanzu suna nuna babban bambance-bambancen yanki kuma yakamata a mai da hankali kan aikin don tabbatar da cewa ba a bar kowa a baya ba. Saka hannun jari na buƙatar ya isa ƙasashe masu ƙaramin ƙarfi da kuma hamadar sahara domin tabbatar da samun ci gaba cikin adalci wajen cimma burin na 7. Stefan Schweinfest, Sashen ƙididdiga na Majalisar Ɗinkin Duniya. Duk da koma bayan da aka samu a harkar samar da wutar lantarki a duniya, adadin mutanen da ba su da wutar lantarki kusan ya ragu a cikin shekaru goma da suka gabata, daga biliyan 1.1 a shekarar 2010 zuwa miliyan 675 a shekarar 2021. Duk da haka, dole ne a ƙara yin ƙoƙari da matakai na gaggawa don tabbatar da cewa ba a bar masu fama da talauci da wahala a baya ba. Don samun isa ga duniya nan da shekarar 2030, dole ne al'ummar ci gaba su haɓaka hannun jarin makamashi mai tsafta da tallafin manufofi. Guangzhe Chen, mataimakin shugaban ƙasa kan samar da ababen more rayuwa, bankin duniya
translations.reference: The international community must leverage all these tools to meet the Sustainable Development Goals by the end of this decade.” Fatih Birol, Executive Director, International Energy Agency “Cost-competitive renewable energy has yet again demonstrated remarkable resilience, but the poorest in the world are still largely unable to fully benefit from it. To realise SDG7 without compromising climate goals, we must bring about systemic change in the way international cooperation works. It is crucial that multilateral financial institutions direct financial flows more equitably around the world to support renewables deployment and related physical infrastructure development.” Francesco La Camera, Director-General, International Renewable Energy Agency “Despite advances towards sustainable energy targets at the mid-point of Agenda 2030, Goal 7 seems harder to reach than it was in 2015 and scaled-up action is necessary if we are to ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all by 2030. Access to electricity and clean cooking still display great regional disparities and should be the focus of action to ensure that no one is left behind. Investment needs to reach the least-developed countries and sub-Saharan Africa to ensure more equitable progress toward Goal 7.” Stefan Schweinfest, United Nations Statistics Division “Despite a recent slowdown in the global pace of electrification, the number of people without electricity almost halved over the past decade, from 1.1 billion in 2010 down to 675 million in 2021. Nonetheless, additional efforts and measures must urgently be put in place to ensure that the poorest and hardest-to-reach people are not left behind. To reach universal access by 2030, the development community must scale up clean energy investments and policy support.” Guangzhe Chen, Vice President for Infrastructure, World Bank
translations.hypothesis: Countries must utilize all available tools to achieve the goals of Sustainable Development Goal 7 by 2030.” Fatih Birol, Executive Director, International Energy Agency “Clean energy has gotten more expensive, but the world’s poorest are still not able to afford it. To achieve SDG 7 without compromising climate change objectives, we must change the way international cooperation works. It is crucial that multilateral financial institutions lead the way in financing a just transition globally to support the transfer of clean technologies and the development of physical infrastructure. ” Francesco La Camera, Director-General, International Renewable Energy Agency “Despite the progress made on sustainable energy between 2015 and 2030, SDG 7 is off track and the pace of progress needs to accelerate if we are to ensure universal access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all by 2030. Access to electricity and clean cooking remain unevenly distributed geographically and these priorities must be addressed to ensure that no one is left behind. Investment needs to reach the poorest and most fragile states to ensure an equitable progress towards the achievement of SDG 7.” Stefan Schweinfest, United Nations Statistics Division “Despite the significant progress in global electrification, the number of people without access to electricity has almost halved in the last decade, from 1.1 billion in 2010 to 675 million in 2021. However, more efforts and urgent actions are needed to ensure that the poorest and most vulnerable are not left behind. To achieve universal access by 2030, the community must accelerate the pace of innovation and investment in clean energy technologies and supportive policies. ” Guangzhe Chen, Vice President for Equitable Development, World Bank

translations.source: Dole ne mu kare al’umma masu ya sowa ta haryar yin aiki a yanzu. Zuba hannun jari a cikin mafita mai tsabta da sabuntawa don tallafawa samun damar makamashi ta duniya shi ne yadda za mu iya samar da canji na gaske. Tsaftace fasahohin dafa abinci a gidaje da ingantaccen wutar lantarki a wuraren kiwon lafiya na iya taka muhimmiyar rawa wajen kare lafiyar al’ummarmu masu rauni. Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Darakta Janar na Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya WHO. Ga me da rahoton Hukumomin kulawa na SDG 7 ne suka wallafa wannan rahoto, Hukumar Kula da Makamashi ta Duniya ta (IEA) da Hukumar Kula da Makamashi ta Duniya (IRENA), Sashen Kididdiga na Majalisar Dinkin Duniya (UNSD), Bankin Duniya, da Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya (WHO) kuma yana da nufin samarwa al'ummomin kasa da kasa wata dama ta duniya don yin rijistar cigaba da samun makamashi da ingancin makamashi da sabunta makamashi da hadin gwiwar ƙasa da ƙasa don ciyar da SDG 7 gaba. Shirin Taimakawa Sashen Kula da Makamashi na Bankin Duniya (ESMAP) ne ya bayar da tallafin rahoton.
translations.reference: “We must protect the next generation by acting now. Investing in clean and renewable solutions to support universal energy access is how we can make real change. Clean cooking technologies in homes and reliable electricity in health-care facilities can play a crucial role in protecting the health of our most vulnerable populations.” Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General, World Health Organization About the report This report is published by the SDG 7 custodian agencies, the International Energy Agency (IEA), the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), the United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD), the World Bank, and the World Health Organization (WHO) and aims to provide the international community with a global dashboard to register progress on energy access, energy efficiency, renewable energy and international cooperation to advance SDG 7. translations.source: Hukumar Tarayyar Turai da WHO sun kaddamar da wani muhimmin shiri na kiwon lafiya na dijital don karfafa tsaron lafiyar duniya. Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya (WHO) da Hukumar Tarayyar Turai sun ba da sanarwar ƙaddamar da wani muhimmin haɗin gwiwa na kiwon lafiya na dijital. A watan Yuni 2023, WHO za ta ɗauki tsarin Tarayyar Turai (EU) na takardun shaida na dijital na COVID-19 don kafa tsarin duniya wanda zai taimaka wa sauƙaƙe zirga-zirgar duniya tare da kare 'yan ƙasa a duk faɗin duniya daga ci gaba da barazanar lafiya na gaba, game da annoba. Wannan shi ne tubalin farko na cibiyar sadarwa ta WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network (GDHCN) wacce za ta samar da nau'uka samfuran dijital da yawa don isar da ingantacciyar lafiya ga kowa. "Gina kan hanyar sadarwar satifiket ɗin dijital ta EU mai nasara sosai, WHO na da niyyar bai wa duk ƙasashe, membobin WHO damar samun buɗaɗɗen kayan aikin kiwon lafiya na dijital, wanda ya dogara da ƙa'idojin daidaito, ƙirƙira, bayyana gaskiya da kariyar bayanai da kuma keɓancewa. Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Darakta Janar na WHO. Dangane da dabarun kiwon lafiya na duniya na EU da dabarun WHO na duniya kan lafiyar dijital, yunƙurin ya biyo bayan yarjejeniyar 30 ga Nuwamba 2022 tsakanin Kwamishinan Kyriakides da Dr Tedros don haɓaka dabarun haɗin Guiwa kan lamuran kiwon lafiya na duniya. Dangane da dabarun kiwon lafiya na duniya na EU da dabarun WHO na duniya kan lafiyar dijital, yunƙurin ya biyo bayan yarjejeniyar 30 ga Nuwamba 2022 tsakanin Kwamishinan Kyriakides da Dr Tedros don haɓaka dabarun haɗin gwiwa kan lamuran kiwon lafiya na duniya. Wannan yana ƙara ƙarfafa tsare-tsaren ƙungiyoyi da yawa tare da WHO a ainihinsa, wanda ƙaƙƙarfan EU ke ƙarfafa shi. Wannan haɗin gwiwar wani muhimmin mataki ne ga shirin aiwatar da dijital na dabarun lafiya na duniya na EU. Ta amfani da mafi kyawun ayyuka na Turai muna ba da gudummawa ga ƙa'idodin kiwon lafiya na dijital da haɗin kai a duniya ''don fa'idar waɗanda suka fi buƙata. Hakanan misali ne mai ƙarfi na yadda daidaitawa tsakanin EU da WHO na iya isar da ingantacciyar lafiya ga kowa, a cikin EU da duk duniya.
translations.reference: The European Commission and WHO launch landmark digital health initiative to strengthen global health security The World Health Organization (WHO) and European Commission have announced today the launch of a landmark digital health partnership. In June 2023, WHO will take up the European Union (EU) system of digital COVID-19 certification to establish a global system that will help facilitate global mobility and protect citizens across the world from on-going and future health threats, including pandemics. This is the first building block of the WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network (GDHCN) that will develop a wide range of digital products to deliver better health for all. “Building on the EU’s highly successful digital certification network, WHO aims to offer all WHO Member States access to an open-source digital health tool, which is based on the principles of equity, innovation, transparency and data protection and privacy,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General. “New digital health products in development aim to help people everywhere receive quality health services quickly and more effectively”. Based on the EU Global Health Strategy and WHO Global strategy on digital health, the initiative follows the 30 November 2022 agreement between Commissioner Kyriakides and Dr Tedros to enhance strategic cooperation on global health issues. This further bolsters a robust multilateral system with WHO at its core, powered by a strong EU.“This partnership is an important step for the digital action plan of the EU Global Health Strategy. By using European best practices we contribute to digital health standards and interoperability globally—to the benefit of those most in need. It is also a powerful example of how alignment between the EU and the WHO can deliver better health for all, in the EU and across the world.
translations.hypothesis: EU and WHO launch major digital health initiative to bolster global health security The World Health Organization (WHO) and the European Union (EU) announced a major new digital health partnership. In June 2023, WHO will take over the EU’s COVID-19 digital certificate framework to facilitate international travel and protect citizens from health threats posed by pandemics. This is the first deliverable of the WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network (GDHCN) which will provide a secure and interoperable platform for the issuance of various digital health certificates and credentials to advance universal health coverage. “Building on the success of the EU Digital COVID Certificate, WHO aims to provide all WHO Member States with access to cutting-edge digital health tools based on the principles of equity, innovation, transparency, data protection and interoperability.” Said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General. The initiative follows a Memorandum of Understanding signed on 30 November 2022 between Commissioner Kyriakides and Dr Tedros to strengthen cooperation on global health issues. The initiative follows a Memorandum of Understanding signed on 30 November 2022 between Commissioner Kyriakides and Dr Tedros to strengthen cooperation on global health issues. This is further strengthened by the many initiatives undertaken with WHO under the aegis of the European Union. “This partnership is an important step in the implementation of the EU Global Health Strategy. By building on Europe’s best practices we are contributing to global digital health and solidarity in support of those most in need. It is a concrete example of how closer alignment between the EU and WHO can deliver better health for all, both within the EU and around the world.”

translations.source: A matsayin hukumar gudanarwa da daidaitawa kan ayyukan kiwon lafiya na kasa da kasa, babu wani abokin tarayya mafi kyau fiye da WHO don ci gaba da aikin da muka fara a EU da kuma ci gaba da samar da hanyoyin magance lafiyar dijital ta duniya, "in ji Stella Kyriakides, Kwamishinan Lafiya da Tsaron Abinci. Wannan haɗin gwiwar zai haɗa da haɗin gwiwa ta kut-da-kut a cikin haɓakawa, gudanarwa da aiwatar da tsarin GDHCN na WHO, tare da cin gajiyar ƙwararrun Hukumar Turai a fagen. Mataki na farko shi ne tabbatar da cewa takaddun shaida na dijital na EU na yanzu sun ci gaba da aiki yadda ya kamata." Tare da ƙasashe da yankuna 80 da ke da alaƙa da EU Digital CVID-19 Certificate, EU ta saita daidaitattun duniya. Takardun shaida na EU ba kawai ya zama muhimmin kayan aiki a yaƙinmu da cutar ba, har ma ya sauƙaƙe balaguron balaguron ƙasa da yawon buɗe ido. Na yi farin ciki da cewa WHO za ta gina ƙa'idodin kiyaye sirri da fasaha mai mahimmanci na takardar shaidar EU don ƙirƙirar kayan aiki na duniya game da annoba ta gaba, in ji Thierry Breton, Kwamishinan Kasuwar Cikin Gida. Tsarin WHO na duniya yana ginuwa a kan gadon tsarin na EU Ɗaya daga cikin mahimman abubuwa a cikin aikin Tarayyar Turai game da cutar ta COVID-19 shi ne takardun shaida na COVID-19 na zamani. Don sauƙaƙe motsi kyauta a cikin iyakokinta, EU ta hanzarta kafa takardun shaida na COVID-19 masu aiki (mai suna 'EU Digital COVID-19 Certificate' ko 'EU DCC'). Dangane da fasahohin bude-bude da ka'idoji ya ba da izinin haɗin kai na ƙasashen da ba na EU ba waɗanda ke ba da takaddun shaida daidai da ƙayyadaddun EU DCC, zama mafita mafi amfani da ita a duniya.
translations.reference: As the directing and coordinating authority on international health work, there is no better partner than the WHO to advance the work we started at the EU and further develop global digital health solutions,” said Stella Kyriakides, Commissioner for Health and Food Safety. This partnership will include close collaboration in the development, management and implementation of the WHO GDHCN system, benefitting from the European Commission’s ample technical expertise in the field. A first step is to ensure that the current EU digital certificates continue to function effectively.“ With 80 countries and territories connected to the EU Digital COVID-19 Certificate, the EU has set a global standard. The EU certificate has not only been an important tool in our fight against the pandemic, but has also facilitated international travel and tourism. I am pleased that the WHO will build on the privacy-preserving principles and cutting-edge technology of the EU certificate to create a global tool against future pandemics,” added Thierry Breton, Commissioner for Internal Market. A global WHO system building on EU legacy One of the key elements in the European Union’s work against the COVID-19 pandemic has been digital COVID-19 certificates. To facilitate free movement within its borders, the EU swiftly established interoperable COVID-19 certificates (entitled ‘EU Digital COVID-19 Certificate’ or ‘EU DCC’). Based on open-source technologies and standards it allowed also for the connection of non-EU countries that issue certificates according to EU DCC specifications, becoming the most widely used solution around the world.
translations.hypothesis: As the health cluster lead for global emergencies, WHO is the natural partner to continue the work we have already begun with the EU and ensure a coordinated global approach to digital health solutions,” said Stella Kyriakides, Commissioner for Health and Food Safety. This partnership will include joint work on the development, governance, and implementation of the WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network (GDHCN). The first step will be to ensure that the current EU Digital COVID Certificate system continues to function properly. With 80 countries and territories connected to the EU Digital COVID Certificate, the EU has set a global standard. “The EU Digital COVID Certificate has not only been a vital tool in our fight against the pandemic, but has also facilitated the recovery of cross-border travel and tourism. I am pleased that WHO will build on the privacy-preserving and security-by-design features of the EU Digital COVID Certificate to create a global tool for future pandemics,” said Thierry Breton, Commissioner for the Internal Market. WHO's global standard builds on EU experience One of the key elements of the EU's COVID-19 response was the development of the EU Digital COVID Certificate. To facilitate free movement within its borders, the EU quickly developed a functional COVID-19 certificate system (known as the 'EU Digital COVID Certificate' or 'EU DCC'). Based on open-source technology and standards, it allowed the interoperability of non-EU countries’ vaccination certificates with the EU DCC, making it the most widely accepted global solution.

translations.source: Tun daga farkon barkewar cutar, WHO ta yi hulɗa tare da duk yankuna na WHO don ayyana gama - garin ƙa'idodin a irin waɗannan takardun. Don taimakawa ƙarfafa shirye-shiryen kiwon lafiya na duniya ta fuskar ci gaban barazanar kiwon lafiya, WHO tana kafa cibiyar sadarwar ba da takardar shaida ta dijital ta duniya wacce ke gina tushen tushen tsarin EU DCC, ka'idoji da fasahohi masu buɗewa. Tare da wannan haɗin gwiwar, WHO za ta sauƙaƙe wannan tsari a duniya a ƙarƙashin tsarinta tare da manufar ba da damar duniya ta ci gajiyar haɗuwa da takaddun shaida na dijital. Wannan ya haɗa da daidaitaccen saiti da tabbatar da sa hannun na zamani don hana zamba. Ta yin hakan, WHO ba za ta sami damar yin amfani da kowane bayanan sirri ba, wanda zai ci gaba da zama keɓaɓɓen yanki na gwamnatoci. Tushe na farko na tsarin WHO na duniya zai fara aiki a watan Yuni 2023 kuma yana da niyyar haɓaka ci gaba a cikin watanni masu zuwa. Haɗin kai na dijital na dogon lokaci don isar da ingantacciyar lafiya ga kowa Don sauƙaƙe haɓakar EU DCC ta WHO da kuma ba da gudummawa ga ayyukanta da ci gaba, WHO da Hukumar Turai sun amince da haɗin gwiwa a cikin lafiyar dijital. Wannan haɗin gwiwar za ta yi aiki don haɓaka tsarin WHO ta hanyar fasaha tare da tsarin da aka tsara don rufe ƙarin shari'o'in amfani, wanda zai iya haɗawa, misali, digitization na Takaddun shaida na Alurar riga kafi ko Prophylaxis. Fadada irin waɗannan hanyoyin dijital na dijital zai zama mahimmanci don isar da ingantacciyar lafiya ga 'yan ƙasa a duk faɗin duniya.
translations.reference: From the onset of the pandemic, WHO engaged with all WHO Regions to define overall guidelines for such certificates. To help strengthen global health preparedness in the face of growing health threats, WHO is establishing a global digital health certification network which builds upon the solid foundations of the EU DCC framework, principles and open technologies. With this collaboration, WHO will facilitate this process globally under its own structure with the aim to allow the world to benefit from convergence of digital certificates. This includes standard-setting and validation of digital signatures to prevent fraud. In doing so, WHO will not have access to any underlying personal data, which would continue to be the exclusive domain of governments. The first building block of the global WHO system becomes operational in June 2023 and aims to be progressively developed in the coming months. A long-term digital partnership to deliver better health for all To facilitate the uptake of the EU DCC by WHO and contribute to its operation and further development, WHO and the European Commission have agreed to partner in digital health. This partnership will work to technically develop the WHO system with a staged approach to cover additional use cases, which may include, for example, the digitisation of the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis. Expanding such digital solutions will be essential to deliver better health for citizens across the globe.
translations.hypothesis: Since the beginning of the pandemic, WHO has worked with all WHO regions to establish regional standards for such documents. To support strengthening of national health systems in the face of ongoing and emerging health threats, WHO is developing a global digital health certificate network based on the EU Digital COVID Certificate’s open-source system, standards and technologies. Through this partnership, WHO will facilitate global equitable access to this system under its governance and with the aim of maximizing global participation and interoperability of digital health certificates. This includes the secure setup and maintenance of digital signatures to prevent forgery. In doing so, WHO will not have access to any personal data, which will remain the sole responsibility of the national governments. The first release of WHO's global standard will be available in June 2023 and is expected to be updated several times over the coming months. Sustainable digital cooperation for universal health coverage To facilitate the development of the WHO EU DCC and support its implementation and sustainability, WHO and the European Commission signed a partnership agreement on digital health. This partnership will work to develop WHO technical standards and guidelines for a wide range of use cases, including, for example, the digitization of vaccination records or prophylaxis. Expanding such digital solutions will be essential to achieving universal health coverage.

Wannan haɗin gwiwar ya dogara ne akan dabi'u da ka'idoji na gaskiya da budewa, haɗa kai, lissafin kuɗi, kariya da bayanan sirri, tsaro, haɓakawa a matakin duniya, da daidaito. The WHO and the European Commission will work together to encourage maximum global uptake and participation. Particular attention will be paid to equitable opportunities for the participation by those most in need: low and middle-income countries.

This partnership relies on the guiding principles of honesty, transparency, collaboration, accountability, protection of personal data, security, global sustainability, equity and non-discrimination. translations.source: Majalisar Kiwon Lafiya ta Duniya ta saba'in da shida - Sabuntawar yau da kullun: 30 ga Mayu 2023 Taron shekara-shekara na WHO ya ƙare da yarjejeniya kan kudade, da kuma batutuwan kiwon lafiya da yawa Dabarar ta mayar da hankali ne kan duk wani wuri da ake ba da kiwon lafiya, a cikin tsarin kiwon lafiya; ya dogara ne a kan ka'idar kulawa mai tsabta da aminci a matsayin muhimmin sashe na haƙƙin lafiya, wanda ke tafiyar da daidaito, wanda ya kamata ya tabbatar da lissafi da ɗorewa. mafi kyawun sayayya don magance cututtuka marasa yaɗuwa; bincike; nakasa; rigakafin nutsewa; gaggawa, kulawa mai mahimmanci da aiki; abinci micronutrients; lafiyar 'yan asali; rigakafin kamuwa da cuta; lafiyar mata da yara; oxygen na likita; kiwon lafiya na farko; lafiyar 'yan gudun hijira da bakin haure gyarawa; magungunan gargajiya, da kuma aikin WHO na amsa da yawa na gaggawa yayin aiki tare da Membobin Kasashe don kasancewa cikin shiri don fuskantar sababbi. Tun da farko a wannan rana, wakilai a cikin Kwamitin A sun amince su lura da taswirar hanyar da za a bi don Kiwon Lafiyar Duniya da Aminci (tare da wani ɗan canji a suna daga Kiwon Lafiyar Duniya don Amincewar Zaman Lafiya ci gaba wajen karfafa taswirar hanya. A zaman majalissar, a matsayin matakin amincewa na karshe na majalisar, wakilai sun amince da kudurori da hukunce-hukuncen kwamitocin biyu, tare da amincewa da rahotonsu. Wannan ya haɗa da amincewa da kasafin kuɗi na 2024-25, da haɓaka 20% na gudunmawar da aka tantance. Shuwagabannin kwamitoci da wakilai daga yankuna biyu sun yi jawabi domin sanin aiki da ci gaban wannan Majalisar.
translations.reference: Seventy-sixth World Health Assembly – Daily update: 30 May 2023 WHO’s annual assembly ends with agreement on funding, and array of health topics WHO’s 76th health assembly closed today, having addressed a vast array of issues, including behavioural sciences; best buys for non-communicable diseases; diagnostics; disabilities; drowning prevention; emergency, critical and operative care; food micronutrients; indigenous health; infection prevention and control; maternal and child health; medical oxygen; primary health care; refugee and migrant health; rehabilitation; traditional medicine, and WHO’s work in responding to dozens of emergencies while working with Member States to be better prepared to face new ones. Earlier in the day, delegates in Committee A agreed to note the roadmap towards the Global Health and Peace Initiative (along with a slight change in name from “Global Health for Peace Initiative”), and requested that the Director-General report on progress in strengthening the roadmap. In plenary, as the final approval step of the assembly, delegates adopted the resolutions and decisions of the two committees, and adopted their reports. This included approval of the budget for 2024-25, and a 20% increase in assessed contributions. The committee chairs and representatives from two regions spoke to recognize the work and progress of this Assembly.
translations.hypothesis: Seventy-sixth World Health Assembly – Daily update: 30 May 2023 WHO’s annual Assembly concludes with agreement on financing, and a host of health priorities The strategy focuses on all-hazard preparedness, within the context of universal health coverage; it is based on the principle of “One Health” and the right to health, which is equitable, accountable and sustainable. best buys in non-communicable disease prevention; research; disability prevention; drowning prevention; emergency, critical and operative care; food fortification; indigenous health; infection prevention control; maternal, newborn and child health; medical oxygen; palliative care; refugee and migrant health; traditional medicine, and WHO’s work on multi-country action plans in response to emergencies while continuing to work with Member States to be better prepared for the next big one. Earlier in the day, delegates in Committee A agreed a draft resolution on A global strategy on health and safety (with a slightly modified title from the original “Global strategy on health for peace”) that makes progress on the road to a safer world. In the final hours of the Assembly, in a plenary session, Member States adopted the resolutions and decisions from the Committees, with the reports being endorsed. This included the approval of the Programme budget 2024–2025, with a commitment to a 20% increase of assessed contributions. The Committee Chairs and Regional Directors took the floor to thank delegates for their work and commitment during this Assembly.

translations.source: A yayin jawabansa na rufe taron, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Wanda shi ne babban daraktan hukumar ta WHO, ya bayyana cewa Ƙaruwar gudunmawar da aka tantance da kuma zagayen saka hannun jari na da tarihi da kuma wani gagarumin ci gaba. Ya yi magana a kan shekara mai zuwa, tare da muhimman zama da manyan tarurrukan da zasu shafi kiwon lafiya na duniya; tarin fuka da shirye-shiryen annoba da mayar da martani a babban taron Majalisar Dinkin Duniya na bana. Ya karfafa akan ci gaba da tattaunawa kan batun yarjejeniyar barkewar cutar da kuma gyare-gyaren da za a inganta dokokin kiwon Lafiya ta Duniya zuwa matakin da ba a taɓa ganin irinsa ba. ba dama na tsararraki don koyo daga kura-kuran cutar ta COVID-19 da kuma tabbatar da cewa ba a maimaita su ba. Wakilan kuma sun sami damar jin ta bakin tsohon ma'aikacin WHO Gwen Carnelley, wanda ya cika shekaru 100 a wannan shekara, wanda ya fara aiki tare da WHO a cikin 1949, shekara guda bayan wanda aka kafa shekaru 75 da suka gabata. Bidiyon rufe taron kiwon lafiya na duniya karo na saba'in da shida (76). An gabatar da Gwen Carnelley da ƙarfe 54:37 kuma yayi magana jim kaɗan bayan haka. Daga gobe ne za a fara taron hukumar zartaswa karo na 153, inda za a tattauna sakamakon majalisar, da dai sauransu.
translations.reference: In his closing remarks, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO’s Director-General, noted that “the increase in assessed contributions and the investment round are historic and a huge milestone.” He spoke about the year ahead, with high-level meetings on universal health coverage, tuberculosis and pandemic preparedness and response at this year’s UN General Assembly. He pointed to the continuing negotiations on the pandemic accord and amendments to the International Health Regulations as unprecedented—“generational”—opportunities to learn from the mistakes of the COVID-19 pandemic and ensure they are not repeated. Delegates also had the chance to hear from former WHO staff Gwen Carnelley, who turned 100 this year, who began working with WHO in 1949, just a year after WHO was founded 75 years ago. Video of Closing of the 76th World Health Assembly. Gwen Carnelley is introduced at 54:37 and speaks shortly afterwards. Starting tomorrow, the 153rd meeting of Executive Board begins, where the outcomes of the Assembly will be discussed, among other things.
translations.hypothesis: In his closing remarks, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General, said the increased ambition and breadth of the investment agenda was a historical development. He looked forward to a year of important meetings and events on global health, including the upcoming UN High-Level Meeting on Tuberculosis and AIDS, and the Global Health Summit. He urged further discussion on the pandemic agreement process and reforms to the International Health Regulations to an unprecedented level. Delegates also heard from former WHO staff member Gwen Carnelly, who turned 100 years old this year, and who worked for WHO in 1949, the year after the Organization was founded 75 years ago. translations.reference: Seventy-sixth World Health Assembly – Daily update: 29 May 2023 Landmark resolution for strengthening Indigenous Peoples’ health globally The World Health Assembly today approved an unprecedented resolution on the health of Indigenous Peoples, which requests the Director-General to develop a global action plan for the health of indigenous peoples and to present it to the Seventy-ninth World Health Assembly in 2026. Indigenous Peoples, although representing diverse population groups and communities, in general have considerably lower life expectancy than non-indigenous populations. They also have a higher prevalence of many diseases and adverse health conditions, including diabetes, maternal and infant mortality and malnutrition. The Assembly requested the action plan be developed in consultation with Indigenous Peoples; that WHO provide support to Member States, upon request, for improving indigenous health; and that the improvement of Indigenous Peoples’ health be included in the development of the Fourteenth WHO General Programme of Work. In the same resolution, the Health Assembly urged Member States to, among other tasks, develop knowledge about the health situation of Indigenous Peoples, with their free, prior and informed consent; develop, fund and implement national health plans, strategies or other measures for Indigenous Peoples;

Takardun da ke da alaƙa: A76/a/conf./1 - Lafiyar ƴan asalin ƙasar Ƙuduri na farko don hanzarta aiwatar da rigakafi na batun nutsewar. Wakilan a taron kiwon lafiya na duniya na saba'in da shida sun amince da wani ƙuduri na hanzarta ɗaukar matakin rigakafin nutsewar duniya. Kudirin ya bukaci kasashe mambobin kungiyar da su tantance halin da suke ciki na nutsewa da kuma bunkasa da aiwatar da shirye-shiryen rigakafin nutsewa da yawa. Hatsarin Nutsun Ruwa yakan haddasa mutuwar mutum dubu Dari biyu da talatin da shida 236000 a kowace shekara. Ita ce lamba ta ɗaya a duniya gun sanadin mutuwar yara masu nasaba da rauni. A sama da shekara goma da suka wuce, mutane miliyan biyu da rabi ne suka mutu sakamakon nutsewa, kuma sama da kashi casai'n 90% na waɗanda suka mutun sun mutu ne a kasashe masu ƙaramin karfi da matsakaicin kuɗin shiga. Bisa gayyatar da Majalisar Dinkin Duniya ta yi wa hukumar WHO, za ta tsara ayyuka a cikin tsarin Majalisar Dinkin Duniya kan yadda za ta aiwatar da rigakafin nutsewa tare da sauƙaƙa bikin ranar rigakafin nutsewa ruwa ta duniya; a ranar 25 ga Yulin kowace shekara. Hukumar WHO za ta ƙara ƙulla wata kawance ta duniya a kan rigakafin nutsewa wanda za ta haɗa da ƙungiyoyin tsaro na MDD, da abokan kawo ci gaba na ƙasa da ƙasa, da kuma ƙungiyoyi masu zaman kansu. Domin samun ƙarin gamsashiyar fahimtar nauyi na gaske akan tbatun nutsewa, ƙudurin ya ƙara buƙatar WHO ta shirya rahoton matsayin duniya kan rigakafin nutsewa.

Related document: A76/A/CONF./1 - Health of Indigenous Peoples First-ever resolution to accelerate action on drowning preventionThe delegates at the Seventy-sixth World Health Assembly agreed a resolution to accelerate action on global drowning prevention. The resolution requests Member States to assess their national drowning situation and to develop and implement multisectoral drowning prevention programmes. Drowning causes 236 000 deaths every year. It is a leading global cause of injury-related child deaths. Over the past decade, 2.5 million people died from drowning, and over 90% of those occurred in low- and middle-income countries. At the invitation of the United Nations (UN) General Assembly, WHO will coordinate actions within the UN system on drowning prevention and facilitate the observance of World Drowning Prevention Day on 25 July each year. WHO will also set up a Global Alliance for Drowning Prevention with organizations of the UN system, international development partners and nongovernmental organizations. To better understand the true burden and impact of drowning, the resolution further requests WHO to prepare a global status report on drowning prevention.

Related documents: A76/A/Conf.1 - Indigenous health First resolution on drowning prevention World Health Assembly delegates have approved a resolution to accelerate action on global drowning prevention. The resolution urges Member States to assess their drowning burden and to develop and implement comprehensive national water safety plans. Drowning claims 236,000 lives each year. It is the sixth leading cause of death worldwide for children aged 1-5 years. More than 2.5 million people have died in drowning incidents over the past decade, and more than 90% of these deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries. At the invitation of the United Nations Secretary-General, WHO will take the lead in coordinating activities within the UN system on drowning prevention and will facilitate the annual global commemoration of World Drowning Prevention Day on 25 July. WHO will forge a new global coalition on drowning prevention that includes UN agencies, international development partners, and civil society. To better understand the true scale of the drowning burden, the resolution also requests WHO to prepare a global report on the status of drowning prevention.

translations.reference: New resolution to accelerate efforts on food micronutrient fortification The delegates approved a resolution on accelerating efforts to prevent micronutrient deficiencies through safe and effective food fortification. Deficiencies in vitamin and mineral status, particularly of folate, iron, vitamin A, and zinc, affect 50% of all preschool aged children and 67% of all women of reproductive age worldwide. Micronutrient deficiencies can have serious consequences, including spina bifida and other neural tube defects.Large scale food fortification is part of the solution. By adding essential vitamins and minerals to staple foods and condiments, such as wheat and maize flours, rice, cooking oil and salt in accordance with national consumption patterns and deficiencies, countries can correct and further prevent a demonstrated micronutrient deficiency. The resolution urges Member States to develop policies on food fortification with micronutrients and/or supplementation, and to consider ways of strengthening financing and monitoring mechanisms. The resolution was agreed under the umbrella of the United Nations Decade of Action on Nutrition (2016-2025) report. Related document: EB152/CONF./5 Accelerating efforts for preventing micronutrient deficiencies and their consequences, including spina bifida and other neural tube defects, through safe and effective food fortification Related links
translations.hypothesis: New resolution to improve efforts on acute malnutrition Representatives agreed a resolution aimed at rapidly achieving an end to acute malnutrition through effective implementation of high-quality nutrition interventions. Deficiencies in vitamins and minerals, in particular folate, iron, vitamin A and zinc, affect up to 50% of all children and 67% of all women of reproductive age worldwide. Severe acute malnutrition can lead to life-threatening conditions, including kwashiorkor and marasmus. Fortification of staple foods is one such solution. By fortifying essential foods and condiments such as maize flour, rice, vegetable oil and salt according to national protocols for the prevention of micronutrient deficiencies, countries can effectively and sustainably improve the nutritional status of their populations. The resolution urges Member States to consider introducing policies on mandatory national food fortification with micronutrients, including folic acid, and to consider the most appropriate mechanisms for financial support and regulatory controls. The resolution is approved under the umbrella of the United Nations Decade of Action on Nutrition (2016–2025). Related documents EB152/CONF./5 Improving efforts to prevent and reduce acute malnutrition, including fortification and other interventions with high impact on reducing micronutrient deficiencies

translations.source: Ƙarin karatu da fahimta game da ƙudurin Ayyukan WHO domin inganta abinci Kasashe (mambobi) sun amince kan ayyukan faɗa da yaƙar magunguna marasa inganci A ranar 27 ga Mayu, Majalisar Kiwon Lafiya ta Duniya ta saba'in da shida ta yarda kan wani ƙuduri na aiwatar da nazari mai zaman kansa na Mechanism (MSM) don abubuwan da suka faru, marasa inganci da magungunan jabu, wanda ke ƙarfafa kiran da Babban Darakta Janar na Janairu 2023 ya yi na a kara sa ido aiki a wannan yanki mai mahimmanci. Za a ƙaddamar da bitar a taron kwamitin gudanarwa na MSM na gaba daga baya a cikin 2023. Majalisar ta kafa MSM a shekara ta 2012 don kawar da magunguna marasa inganci da jabun samfuran likitanci ta mahangar lafiyar jama'a kuma ta hanyar gaskiya da haɗa kai. Manufar MSM ita ce ta kare lafiyar jama'a da haɓaka damar samun arha Mai aminci, inganci da samfuran ingatattun magungunan likitoci. Da yake lura da abubuwan da suka faru na baya-bayan nan, na gurɓatattun magunguna da aka samu a kasuwanni daban-daban, da kuma mace-macen da za a iya hana su, ƙasashe (mambobin) sun jaddada goyon bayan da ake bukata don inganta karfinsu na daƙile hakan, da kuma ganowa da kuma ba da amsa ga marasa inganci da gurbataccen kayayyakin kiwon lafiya; ta hanyar samun fasahohin da suka dace, gami da wuraren gwajin ɗakin gwaje-gwaje, tare da inganta sa-ido kan kasuwanni na yau da kullum da talla, da siyar da samfuran likitanci a kan layi. Kasashen (membobi) sun yi kira da a riƙa aiwatar da fasahohin bin diddigi don sarrafawa da yin kasuwa da sa ido, sannan akwai kuma buƙatar samar da haɗin gwiwa ta yau da kullun Kama daga abokan huldar gida da na duniya kamar hukumomin tilasta bin doka da kwastam. An ƙarfafa (membobin) ƙasashen su daidaita da ƙa'idojin da za su inganta doka da sanya takunkumin hana yin mu'amalan da ba su kamata ba a samfuran likitanci marasa inganci.
translations.reference: Read more about the resolution WHO's work on food fortification Member States approve actions to counter substandard and falsified medicines On 27 May, the Seventy-sixth World Health Assembly approved a resolution to conduct an independent review of the Member State Mechanism (MSM) for incidents, substandard and falsified medicines, reinforcing the Director-General’s January 2023 call for increased vigilance and action in this important area. The review will be initiated at the next MSM steering committee meeting later in 2023. The Assembly established the MSM in 2012 to tackle substandard and falsified medical products from a public health perspective and in a transparent and inclusive way. The goal of the MSM is to protect public health and promote access to affordable, safe, efficacious and quality medical products. Noting recent events of contaminated medicines found on various markets and related preventable deaths, Member States emphasized the support needed to improve their capacity to prevent, detect and respond to substandard and falsified medical products through access to appropriate technologies, including laboratory testing facilities, along with improved oversight on informal markets and advertising, and the online sale of medical products. Member States called for embracing and implementing track and trace technologies for market control and surveillance, as well as the need for formal collaboration by relevant local and global partners such as law enforcement and customs administrations. Member States were encouraged to align with conventions aimed at improvement of legislation and imposition of prohibitive sanctions for wrongful dealing in substandard and falsified medical products.
translations.hypothesis: Learn more about the WHO Global Strategy for Food Safety Member States agree to actions to fight substandard and falsified medicines On 27 May, the Seventy-sixth World Health Assembly adopted a resolution on “Strengthening the WHO global action on substandard and falsified medicines,” which endorsed the call by the Director-General in January 2023 for enhanced action in this critical area. The survey will be launched at the next meeting of the MSM steering committee, later in 2023. The Member States established the MSMC in 2012 to reinforce the public health approach to the control of substandard and falsified medicines through coordination and collaboration. The MSMC aims to protect public health and increase access to affordable, safe, effective and quality medical products. Concerned by recent incidents of substandard or falsified medicines found on the market, and the potential harm to patients, Member States stressed the need for continued support to strengthen their capacity to prevent, detect and respond to incidents of substandard or falsified medical products; by putting in place appropriate technical requirements, including for laboratory testing facilities, and by improving post-marketing surveillance and pharmacovigilance, including of products sold online. Member States highlighted the need for regulatory tools for market control and surveillance, and the need for closer collaboration with national and international partners, such as law enforcement agencies and customs authorities. Member States were encouraged to align their regulatory frameworks with international norms and standards to enhance control and reduce the risks posed by substandard and falsified medical products.

translations.source: Majalisar Kiwon Lafiya ta Duniya ta saba'in da shida - Sabuntawa kullum: 27 ga Mayu 2023 Dabarar farko ta duniya game da rigakafin kamuwa da cuta da kuma kula da Majalisar Kiwon Lafiya ta Duniya ta amince a yau kan dabarun farko na duniya kan rigakafin kamuwa da cuta (IPC), wanda ya gina kusan shekaru ashirin na kokarin da WHO da abokan tarayya suka jagoranta. Dabarar farko ta duniya game da rigakafin kamuwa da cuta da kuma kula da Majalisar Kiwon Lafiya ta Duniya ta amince a yau kan dabarun farko na duniya kan rigakafin kamuwa da cuta (IPC), wanda ya gina kusan shekaru ashirin na kokarin da WHO da abokan tarayya suka jagoranta. HAIS suna daga cikin abubuwan da suka fi faruwa a cikin yanayin isar da sabis na kiwon lafiya. Cutar sankarau ta COVID-19 da manyan cututtukan da suka barke a baya-bayan nan kamar cutar Ebola, Ciwon numfashi na Gabas ta Tsakiya da Cutar Cutar Sudan sun fallasa gibin da ke akwai a cikin shirye-shiryen IPC a duk ƙasashe. Dabarar ta tsara hangen nesa: Nan da 2030, duk wanda ke samun dama ko ba da kulawar lafiya ba shi da lafiya daga cututtukan da ke da alaƙa. Makasudai guda uku sune: don hana kamuwa da cuta a cikin kiwon lafiya; yi aiki don tabbatar da shirye-shiryen IPC suna aiki kuma an aiwatar da su; da daidaita ayyukan IPC tare da sauran fannoni da sassa. Dabarar ta mayar da hankali ne kan duk wani wuri da ake ba da kiwon lafiya, a cikin tsarin kiwon lafiya; Ya dogara ne akan ka'idar kulawa mai tsabta da aminci a matsayin muhimmin sashi na haƙƙin lafiya, wanda ke tafiyar da daidaito, wanda ya kamata ya tabbatar da lissafi da dorewa. Dabarun IPC na duniya za a cika su, kuma a yi amfani da su tare da haɗin gwiwa tare da, tsarin aiki na duniya mai alaƙa da tsarin sa ido, wanda za a haɓaka a cikin dubu biyu da ashi da uku 2023 - 2024. Takardun da ke da alaƙa EB152/9 - Daftarin dabarun duniya kan rigakafin kamuwa da cuta da sarrafawa, rahoton taƙaitaccen bayani na Babban Darakta-Janar.
translations.reference: Seventy-sixth World Health Assembly – Daily update: 27 May 2023 First global strategy on infection prevention and controlThe World Health Assembly agreed today on the first-ever global strategy on infection prevention and control (IPC), which builds on almost two decades of efforts led by WHO and partners. The strategy provides Member States with strategic directions to substantially reduce the ongoing risk of health care-associated infections (HAIs), including those that exhibit antimicrobial resistance. HAIs are among the most frequent adverse events occurring in the context of health service delivery. The COVID-19 pandemic and recent major disease outbreaks such as Ebola virus disease, the Middle East respiratory syndrome and the Sudan virus disease have clearly exposed the existing gaps in IPC programmes in all countries. The strategy sets a clear vision: by 2030, everyone accessing or providing health care is safe from associated infections. Its three key objectives are: to prevent infection in health care; act to ensure IPC programmes are in place and implemented; and coordinate IPC activities with other areas and sectors. The strategy is focused on any setting where health care is delivered, across the health system; it is based on the principle of clean and safe care as a fundamental component of the right to health, which is equity driven, and which should ensure accountability and sustainability. The global IPC strategy will be complemented by, and used in conjunction with, an associated global action plan and monitoring framework, that will be developed in 2023–2024. Related document EB152/9 - Draft global strategy on infection prevention and control, Executive summary Report by the Director-General
translations.hypothesis: Seventy-sixth World Health Assembly – Daily update: 27 May 2023 The world’s first IPC strategy endorsed by the World Health Assembly Today, the World Health Assembly endorsed the first-ever global strategy on infection prevention and control (IPC), which builds on more than two decades of work led by WHO and its partners. The global strategy on IPC was endorsed by the World Health Assembly today, marking the culmination of more than two decades of work led by WHO and its partners. HAIs are among the most common adverse events in health care delivery settings. The COVID-19 pandemic and other recent major infectious disease outbreaks, such as Ebola, the Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus and the Sudan virus disease, have revealed critical gaps in IPC capacities in every country. The strategy sets out a vision for 2030: “A world where every person has access to safe health care and is protected from avoidable infections”. There are three main objectives: to prevent infections in health care; to work to ensure IPC programmes are functioning and implemented; and to align IPC activities with other fields and sectors. The strategy focuses on all health care settings within the health system; It is based on the principle of “care as the right”, with safe care being a key component of the right to health, which is universal, equitable, accountable and sustainable. The global IPC strategy will be operationalized through a global action plan with associated monitoring framework, which will be developed in 2023–2024. Related documents EB152/9 - Draft global strategy on infection prevention and control, Report by the Director-General

translations.reference: WHO's work on infection prevention and control Historic resolution paves the way for strengthening rehabilitation in health systemsToday the World Health Assembly agreed a landmark resolution on strengthening rehabilitation in health systems. Rehabilitation services play a key role in ensuring the enjoyment of human rights including the highest attainable standard of physical and mental health. It also promotes sexual and reproductive health, and recognizes the right to work and the right to education. This landmark resolution aims to address the challenges in rehabilitation such as the need to: increase awareness of rehabilitation when setting health priorities and research agendas, allocating resources, promoting cooperation and enabling technology transfer; ensure countries are better equipped to respond to the sudden increase in rehabilitation needs including assistive technology due to health emergencies; ensure persons in marginalized and vulnerable situations have access to affordable, quality and appropriate rehabilitation services including assistive technology; avoid high out-of-pocket costs for people to access rehabilitation services and assistive technology that can cause financial hardships; and address the current insufficient level of rehabilitation workforce to serve the needs of the population. The resolution lists a range of actions to be taken by the WHO Secretariat such as:
translations.hypothesis: WHO’s work on dementia prevention, diagnosis and care, underpinned by a global action plan, provides a clear path for improving health systems. The World Health Assembly today endorsed a new resolution on dementia, underlining the importance of improving dementia care and support worldwide. Caregiving plays a vital role in ensuring dignity, as well as physical and mental well-being. It also supports sexual and reproductive health, and recognizes the right to work and the right to education. This milestone resolution aims to address the challenges ahead by calling for: increased awareness about dementia and the need to develop dementia-friendly communities, plans and policies, allocate resources, build capacity, and enable access to person-centred integrated dementia care and support; ensuring that countries have access to the latest assistive products and technologies through sustainable and affordable universal access to quality assistive products; ensuring that persons with dementia have equitable access to health and other services; providing integrated care and support services in both health and social care settings; and addressing the shortage of dementia carers and the need for more support for dementia carers. The following actions to be taken by WHO are proposed:
