Sanarwa ga editoci: A zagaye na hudu na binciken bugun jini na na hukumar lafiya ta duniyaWHO na duniya, an gayyaci kasashe, yankuna da yankuna 222 don amsa daidaitaccen binciken yanar gizo tsakanin Nuwamba 2022 da Janairu 2023. Binciken na hudu ya biyo bayan binciken hukumar lafiya ta duniya WHO na baya na 2020 da 2021: Zagaye na 1 (Mayu-Satumba 2020), Zagaye na 2 (Janairu-Maris 2021), da Zagaye na 3 (Nuwamba-Disamba 2021) wanda ya nuna girman annobar ta shafi ci gaba da muhimman ayyukan kiwon lafiya da kuma yadda kasashe ke daukar matakai. Yayin da binciken bugun jini yake da iyakoki kamar bayar da rahoto na ɓangaranci da wakilci, ƙarfin wannan ƙoƙarin shine yana da cikakke kuma yana ba da bayanai cikin sauri. Yakamata a fahimci kalmar "ƙasa" ta ƙunshi dukkan kasashe, yankuna da wurare. An kammala nazarin abubuwan da ke faruwa bisa la'akari da martani daga ƙasashe 84, yankuna, ko wurare da suka amsa aƙalla sashin bincike ɗaya a cikin duk zagayen binciken bugun jini guda huɗu.
translations.reference: These include deployment of telemedicine approaches, promotion of home-based care or self-care interventions, approaches for strengthening health workers availability, capacities and support mechanisms, innovations in procuring and delivering medicines and supplies, more routine community communications, and partnerships with private sector providers. Three quarters of countries reported additional funding allocation towards longer term system recovery, resilience and preparedness. Countries expressed need for WHO support to address remaining challenges in the COVID-19 context and beyond, most frequently related to health workforce strengthening, building the monitoring capacities of health services, designing primary health care -- oriented models of care, governance, policy and planning and financial planning and funding. Note to editors: In the fourth round of WHO’s global pulse survey, 222 countries, territories and areas were invited to respond to a standardized web-based survey between November 2022 and January 2023. The fourth survey followed up on WHO’s previous 2020 and 2021 pulse surveys: Round 1 (May-September 2020), Round 2 (January-March 2021), and Round 3 (November-December 2021) which showed the extent to which the pandemic was affecting the continuity of essential health services and how countries are taking action. While pulse surveys have limitations such as reporting bias and representativeness, the strength of this effort is that it is comprehensive and delivers information rapidly. The term “country” should be understood to include all countries, territories and areas. Trend analyses was completed based on responses from 84 countries, territories, or areas that responded to at least one survey section in all four pulse survey rounds.
translations.hypothesis: These include the launch of telemedicine networks, the development of home care or self-care services, efforts to strengthen the capacity, quality and accessibility of care, innovations in the supply and delivery of medications and products, the increased use of digital communication, and partnerships with private providers. Three-quarters of countries reported increased funding for long-term care, recovery and rehabilitation services. Note to editors: The fourth round of WHO’s global survey on hypertension was extended to 222 countries, territories and areas, which were invited to complete a standardized online questionnaire between November 2022 and January 2023. The fourth survey follows immediately on from the WHO surveys of 2020 and 2021: Round 1 (May-September 2020), Round 2 (January-March 2021), Round 3 (November-December 2021) which captured the impact of the pandemic on essential health services and how countries were responding. While the survey has limitations, such as recall bias and representativeness, the strength of this effort lies in its comprehensiveness and timeliness. “Country” should be understood to include all countries, territories and areas. The analysis presented here draws on experiences reported by 84 countries, territories or areas that completed at least one module of the fourth survey on hypertension.

Farashin PCC. Zamaninmu ya sami ci gaba a fannin kimiyya da fasaha fiye da sauran al'ummomin da suka gabata tare kuma sun shaidi sauye-sauye da dama na ilimi, fasaha, likitanci da zamantakewa wanda juyin juya halin hana daukar ciki ya jagoranta sannan kuma ya biyo bayan ci gaban kiwon lafiyar haihuwa, sabbin hanyoyin kiwon lafiya gami da hakkoki da daidaiton jinsi. Kodayake, manyan ƙalubale a fagen SRHR suna ci gaba, kuma, a zahiri, ana sake tambayar wasu ci gaba a yau. Muna yaba wa ma'aikatan HRP-, abokan tarayya da masu goyan baya kan nasarorin da aka samu har zuwa yau kuma mun ga babban ci gaba da aka cimma a cikin rabin karni na samar da shaidun da ke goyan bayan cikakkiyar dama ga lafiyar jima'i da haihuwa da hakki. Muna so mu fayyace manyan nau'ikan nasarori guda uku: Da fari dai, babban bincike na HRP ya yi tasiri mai ma'ana kan manufofin kiwon lafiyar jama'a, ka'idoji, da ayyuka a duk duniya don magance buƙatun ci gaba na al'umma daban-daban. Na biyu, HRP, musamman ta hanyar HRP Alliance, ya ƙarfafa cibiyoyin bincike a cikin gida da kuma na duniya, kuma, ya ba wa masu bincike da yawa damar samun ƙwarewar bincike wanda ke tabbatar da cewa bincike mai inganci na SRHR zai iya ci gaba, kuma ya haɓaka, a nan gaba. Na uku, a cikin duniyar da ke fama da tashin hankali, rikice-rikice da ƙaruwar adawa ga daidaiton jinsi, HRP ta sauƙaƙe kiyaye haƙƙin mata da 'yan mata da kuma al'ummomi masu rauni. HRP ya kasance babban kayan aiki a cikin tsarin Majalisar Dinkin Duniya don bincike game da haifuwar ɗan adam kuma ci gaba da kasancewa jagora musamman a lafiyar jima'i da haihuwa ta duniya.
translations.reference: Statement of celebration for HRP’s 50th anniversary: Sweden and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland To capture the spirit of Policy and Coordination Committee (PCC) members celebrating HRP’s 50th anniversary and its numerous achievements, Sweden and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland read the following note of appreciation and congratulations at the 36th meeting of the HRP PCC. Our generation has seen more progress in science and technology than all preceding generations together and witnessed several intellectual, technological, medical and social transformation spearheaded by the contraceptive revolution and followed by advances in reproductive health, health innovations as well as rights and gender equality. However, considerable challenges in the field of SRHR continue, and, arguably, some advances are in question again today. We applaud HRP-staff, partners and supporters on the numerous achievements to date and recognise the enormous strides accomplished during half a century in producing the evidence that supports full and equal access to sexual and reproductive health and rights. We would like to outline three major categories of achievements: Firstly, the high-quality research by HRP has had tangible impact on public health policy, standards, and practice worldwide addressing the evolving needs of diverse populations. Secondly, HRP, notably through the HRP Alliance, has strengthened research institutions locally and globally, and, enabled numerous researchers to acquire the research skills that ensure that high-quality SRHR research can continue, and indeed increase, into the future. Thirdly, in a world beset by crisis, conflict and increasing resistance to gender equality, HRP has facilitated the upholding of the basic rights of women and girls and vulnerable populations. HRP remains the main instrument within the United Nations system for research in human reproduction and continues to be an exceptional leader in global sexual and reproductive health.
translations.hypothesis: Statement to mark the 50th anniversary of HRP: Sweden and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland Taking the floor at the 36th HRP General Assembly, Sweden and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland delivered this joint statement on behalf of the Political Coordinating Committee (PCC) celebrating 50 years of HRP and its achievements. The PCC commended HRP for: The evolution of our times has witnessed scientific and technological advancements unparalleled in the history of humankind and has experienced profound changes in the intellectual, technical, medical and social landscapes, including the sexual and reproductive health landscape, driven by scientific breakthroughs and resulting in new health priorities, innovations and human rights and gender equality. However, major challenges in the field of SRHR remain, and some progress is under threat. We appreciate the dedication of HRP staff, partners, and donors, and we look forward to seeing what the next 50 years bring. We have witnessed significant progress in the last half-century in the generation of evidence supporting sexual and reproductive health and rights. We would like to highlight three key areas of achievement. Firstly, HRP’s pioneering research has influenced health policy, guidelines and services globally in response to the needs of diverse communities. Secondly, HRP, and especially the HRP Alliance, has strengthened local and international research capacities, and provided opportunities for many researchers to gain experience in rigorous SRHR research, ensuring that high-quality SRHR research can continue to evolve and improve. Thirdly, in a world of increasing conflict, instability and backlash against gender equality, HRP has helped to safeguard the rights of women, girls and other marginalized communities. HRP has been a vital resource within the UN system for research on human reproduction and continues to be a world leader in sexual and reproductive health research.

translations.source: Hukumar lafiya ta duniya WHO ta ƙaddamar da wani sabon shiri don inganta shirye-shiryen annoba Don taimaka wa ƙasashe su shirya don faruwar annoba a gaba,hukumar lafiya ta duniya WHO ta ƙaddamar da wani sabon shiri a yau wanda ke ba da jagora kan haɗaɗɗun tsare-tsare don ba da amsa ga duk wani cututtukan numfashi kamar mura ko coronaviruses. Sabon Tsari da Juriya don Ƙaddamar da wani tsari, ko PRET, ta haɗa sabbin kayan aiki da hanyoyin ilmantarwa da ayyukan gama kai da aka kafa yayin bala'in COVID-19 da sauran abubuwan gaggawa na lafiyar jama'a na baya-bayan nan. Ta hanyar shirin hukumar lafiya ta duniya, WHO za ta yi amfani da tsarin watsa shirye-shirye don jagorantar kasashe a cikin shirye-shiryen annoba, ganin cewa da dama sun zama ruwan dare tsakanin kungiyoyin masu cutar. PRET tana amsa kiran jagorar fasaha da goyan baya don haɓaka da ƙarfafa shirye-shirye a haɗe da amsa, kamar yadda aka tsara a cikin kudurori na Majalisar Lafiya ta Duniya. Cutar ta COVID-19 da sauran matsalolin gaggawa na kiwon lafiya sun nuna cewa akwai bukatar kasashe su kasance cikin shiri don magance barazanar kamuwa da cuta, tare da tsare-tsaren shirye-shiryen da aka kera a hannu da ingantacciyar daidaituwa da hadin gwiwa da sauran bangarorin kamar aikin gona. Tsarin shirye-shirye, rigakafi, da mayar da martani ba dole ba ne su kasance lardin da ke bangaren lafiya kaɗai bai,” in ji Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Darakta Janar na hukumar lafiya ta duniya WHO. Kamar yadda matsalolin gaggawa na kiwon lafiya ke yin tasiri a sassa da dama, haka nan dole ne a shirin mu da kokarin mayar da martani ga ɓangarori, darussa da cututtuka. Yana da mahimmanci kuma, cewa haɗin kai da daidaito tsakanin al'umma su ne cibiyar ƙoƙarinmu, musamman ga waɗanda ba a sani ba kuma galibi suna cikin haɗari. PRET juyin halitta ne a tsarin WHO game da shirye-shiryen kamuwa da cutar ta hanyar aikace-aikacen yanayin watsa ruwan tabarau, maimakon mayar da hankali kan takamaiman cututtuka.
translations.reference: WHO launches new initiative to improve pandemic preparedness To help countries better prepare for future pandemics, WHO launched a new initiative today that provides guidance on integrated planning for responding to any respiratory pathogen such as influenza or coronaviruses. The new Preparedness and Resilience for Emerging Threats Initiative, or PRET, incorporates the latest tools and approaches for shared learning and collective action established during the COVID-19 pandemic and other recent public health emergencies. Through the initiative, WHO will use a mode of transmission approach to guide countries in pandemic planning, given that many capacities and capabilities are common among groups of pathogens. PRET answers the call for technical guidance and support for promoting and strengthening integrated preparedness and response, as outlined in World Health Assembly resolutions. The COVID-19 pandemic and other health emergencies have shown that countries need to be operationally ready to respond to infectious disease threats, with tailored preparedness plans in hand and better coordination and collaboration with other sectors such as agriculture. “Preparedness, prevention, and response activities must not be the province of the health sector alone,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General. “Just as health emergencies have impacts across many sectors, so must our preparedness and response efforts span sectors, disciplines and pathogens. It is critical, too, that community engagement and equity are the centre of our efforts, especially for those populations that are marginalized and most at risk.” PRET is an evolution in WHO’s approach to pandemic preparedness through the application of a mode of transmission lens, rather than a focus on specific diseases.
translations.hypothesis: WHO launches new initiative to improve pandemic preparedness To help countries better prepare for future epidemics, WHO today launched a new initiative that provides guidance on integrated approaches to preparedness and response for all respiratory pathogens, including influenza and coronaviruses. The Pandemic Prevention and Response Toolkit, or PRET, includes a new toolbox of resources and a series of training and awareness activities that have been developed during the COVID-19 pandemic and other recent public health emergencies. Through the WHO Infodemic Management Programme, WHO uses infodemic management strategies to guide countries in preparing for epidemics, as many infodemics cut across organizations and disease groups. The PRET answers the need for technical leadership and support to build and strengthen preparedness and response activities, as described in the relevant World Health Assembly resolutions. COVID-19 and other health emergencies have demonstrated the need for countries to be better prepared for the risk of infectious disease threats, with policies and plans developed in consultation with and coordination across other sectors, such as agriculture. “Preparedness, prevention and response are not the sole responsibility of the health sector alone; they are societal responsibilities and must be integrated into the plans and actions of all relevant sectors,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General. “As health emergencies impact sectors across society, so too must our preparedness and response efforts be integrated, inclusive and multisectoral. It is imperative that collaboration and solidarity across communities are at the heart of our efforts, especially for those most vulnerable and often left behind.” The PRET is a new WHO approach to pandemic preparedness planning that moves away from single pathogen-focused planning and instead focuses on the common elements of pandemic planning across a wide range of potential pathogens.

translations.source: WHO za ta ci gaba da haɓakawa da yada jagora kan takamaiman cututtuka kamar yadda ake buƙata. Kaddamar da shirin yana gudana ne a rana ta ƙarshe ta tarurruka tare da mutane sama da 120 da ke wakiltar ƙasashe membobin, abokan tarayya, da sakatariyar WHO, don ayyana hanyar ci gaba don PRET, gami da haɓaka taswirar aiwatarwa ta duniya don shirye-shiryen rigakafin cututtukan ƙwayar cuta na numfashi. Tsarin farko na PRET Initiative yana mai da hankali kan ƙwayoyin cuta na numfashi, gami da mura, coronaviruses, da ƙwayar cuta ta syncytial na numfashi. Ganin yadda annobar cutar ta COVID-19 take cigaba da kuma yuwuwar barazanar kamuwa da mura ta jiragen ruwa, wannan tsarin zai baiwa kasashe damar yin nazari sosai, gwadawa, da sabunta yunƙurin shirye-shiryen cutar sankarau don tabbatar da cewa suna da iya aiki da iya aiki a wurin. Ana ci gaba da aiki don gano rukuni na gaba na ƙwayoyin cuta, irin su arboviruses, da za a magance a ƙarƙashin wannan shirin. Wannan zai bi manyan abubuwan da aka gano ta hanyar shawarwari goma don ƙarfafa gine-ginen duniya don shirye-shiryen gaggawa na lafiya, amsawa, da juriya (HEPR). Ƙaddamar da PRET ta haifar da sabon zamani don shirye-shiryen cutar sankara kuma tana wakiltar juyin halitta na ainihin ayyukan hukumar lafiya ta duniya WHO don tallafawa duk Membobin Kasashe don ƙarfafa shirye-shiryen gaggawa na kiwon lafiya, rigakafi, da damar amsawa da iyawa. Har ila yau, shirin na iya yin aiki don aiwatar da manufofi da tanade-tanade na Yarjejeniyar Cutar Kwalara, wadda a halin yanzu ƙasashe membobin hukumar lafiya ta duniya WHO ke tattaunawa. Bayan bayanai da tattaunawa tsakanin mahalarta taron, hukumar lafiya ta duniya WHO ta gayyaci masu ruwa da tsaki zuwa wannan kiran na duniya don aiwatar da shirye-shiryen rigakafin cutar sankarau. Kira zuwa ga Aiki
translations.reference: WHO will continue to develop and disseminate guidance on specific diseases as needed. The launch of the initiative is taking place on the last day of meetings with over 120 individuals representing Member States, partners, and the WHO secretariat, to define the path forward for PRET, including the development of a global implementation roadmap for respiratory pathogen pandemic preparedness. The PRET Initiative’s first module focuses on respiratory pathogens, including influenza, coronaviruses, and respiratory syncytial virus. Given the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and the possible threat of avian influenza, this module will enable countries to critically review, test, and update their respiratory pandemic planning efforts to ensure they have the functional capacities and capabilities in place. A process is underway to identify the next group of pathogens, such as arboviruses, to be addressed under this initiative. This will follow priorities identified through the ten proposals to strengthen the global architecture for health emergency preparedness, response, and resilience (HEPR). The PRET Initiative ushers in a new era for pandemic preparedness and represents an evolution of WHO’s core activities to support all Member States in strengthening health emergency preparedness, prevention, and response capacities and capabilities. The initiative can also serve to operationalize the objectives and provisions of the Pandemic Accord, which is currently being negotiated by WHO Member States. Following inputs and discussions among meeting participants, WHO invites stakeholders to this global call to action to advance respiratory pathogen pandemic preparedness. Call to Action
translations.hypothesis: WHO will continue to develop and disseminate guidance on specific pathogens as needed. The launch event was held on the final day of the conference with over 120 participants representing WHO Member States, partners, and Secretariat, to mark the progress of PRET, including the development of a global implementation roadmap for prevention of respiratory pathogens. The first phase of the PRET initiative focuses on respiratory pathogens, including influenza viruses, coronaviruses, and respiratory syncytial virus. Given the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and the recurring threat of influenza, this programme enables countries to take a proactive, systematic approach to pandemic preparedness planning and to ensure that their pandemic response systems are fit for purpose. Work is ongoing to identify the next group of priority pathogens, including arboviruses, to be covered by this programme. This will follow on from the priorities identified by the ten-year plan on strengthening global capacity for health emergency preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR). The launch of PRET marks a new era for pandemic preparedness programmes and represents a significant evolution of WHO’s core mission to support all Member States in strengthening their health emergency preparedness, prevention, and response capabilities. It can also serve as a vehicle for implementing the Pandemic Prevention Treaty, the negotiation of which is currently underway among WHO Member States. After the presentations and discussions between the attending delegates, WHO extended an open invitation to all stakeholders to join this global call to action for prevention of respiratory infections. Call to action

translations.source: Hukumar lafiya ta duniya WHO, Membobin Kasashe, da abokan haɗin gwiwa suna aiki tare don ganowa da aiwatar da ayyuka masu fifiko don ƙarfafa shirye-shiryen ƙasa, yanki, da duniya don cututtukan cututtuka da kuma barazanar kamuwa da cuta. Mun fahimci rawar al'ummomi da dukkan sassa, da buƙatar daidaitawa da dorewar ci gaba don kawo ƙarshen firgici da sakaci wanda ya zama ruwan dare a cikin shirye-shiryen annoba da martani. Mun tuna da darussa daga bala'i da annoba da suka gabata, musamman wadanda cututtukan numfashi ke haifar da su. Wadannan cututtukan suna kuma za su ci gaba da haifar da babbar barazana ta duniya tare da yuwuwar haifar da mummunar cututtuka da mace-mace, mamaye tsarin kiwon lafiya, dagula tattalin arzikin duniya, da kuma ta'azzara rashin daidaito, wanda ke wanzuwa a cikin damar yin amfani da kayan aikin biyu don hana kamuwa da cuta kiwon lafiya ga dukan mutane. Wannan Kira ne zuwa Aiki don haɓaka shirye-shiryen annoba da barazanar da ke fitowa a duniya. Shiri mai inganci ya dogara ne akan ingantaccen tsari da aiki tare. Alƙawarin gamayya kan ayyuka masu zuwa za su kai ga ci gaban da aka samu nan da Disamba 2025 kamar yadda za a bayyana a cikin tsarin sa ido na (Shiri da Juriya don Barazana masu tasowa (PRET): Sabunta shirye-shiryen da ke tabbatar da ayyukan fifiko kuma waɗanda suka yi la'akari da koyo daga abubuwan da suka faru a baya. Gane haɗarin da ƙwayoyin cuta na numfashi ke haifarwa, tsarawa don da annobar cutar numfashi dangane da jigogin da aka gano a cikin Module PRET #1: Abu ne mai muhimmanci zama cikin shirin fuskantar annobar cututtuka masu alaƙa da numfashi.
translations.reference: WHO, Member States, and partners are working together to identify and implement priority actions to strengthen national, regional, and global preparedness for pandemics and emerging infectious disease threats. We recognize the role of communities and all sectors, and the need for harmonized and sustained momentum to end the cycle of panic and neglect that is all too common in pandemic preparedness and response. We recall lessons from previous epidemics and pandemics, especially those caused by respiratory pathogens. These pathogens have and will continue to pose a significant global threat with the potential to cause tremendous morbidity and mortality, overwhelm health systems, de-stabilize the global economy, and exacerbate inequities, which exist in the access to both the tools to prevent pandemics and health care for all people. This is a Call to Action to accelerate preparedness for pandemics and emerging threats globally. Effective preparedness relies on robust planning and coordinated action. A collective commitment on the following actions will see progress achieved by December 2025 as will be described in the (Preparedness and Resilience for Emerging Threats (PRET) monitoring framework: Update preparedness plans that affirm priority actions and that have considered learnings from past events. Recognizing the risk posed by respiratory pathogens, planning for a respiratory pathogen pandemic based on the themes identified in the PRET Module #1: Planning for Respiratory Pathogen Pandemics is a priority
translations.hypothesis: WHO, Member States and partners are working together to identify and implement priority actions to strengthen country, regional and global capacities for preparedness and response to infectious diseases and emerging threats. We recognize the role of communities and all sectors, and the need for shared and sustained efforts to overcome the pandemic fatigue and inertia that have characterized the response to the pandemic. We are reminded of the lessons from past disasters and epidemics, in particular those caused by respiratory pathogens. These diseases continue to pose a significant global threat with the potential to cause severe morbidity and mortality, burden health systems, disrupt economies and exacerbate inequities that already exist in access to life-saving tools and health for all. This is a call to action to improve pandemic and emerging threat preparedness around the world. Effective preparedness planning relies on robust planning and coordination. The commitments made at the Summit will contribute to progress to be achieved by December 2025 as presented in the Preparedness and Resilience for Emerging Threats (PRET) roadmap: A blueprint for action, which ensures a coordinated and prioritised approach to preparedness planning and incorporates lessons learnt from past events. Recognizing the respiratory pathogen risk, planning for respiratory pandemic threats based on the SARA framework presented in Module 1 of the PRET roadmap: It is critical to be prepared for pandemic threats posed by respiratory pathogens.

translations.source: Kara haɗin kai tsakanin masu ruwa da tsaki a cikin shirye-shiryen annoba ta hanyar kyakkyawan tsari da haɗin kai. wannan ya haɗa da samar da tsari na daidaito, da gudanar da ayyuka tare da musayar bayanai game da sahihan hanyoyi da ƙalulabe da damarmaki. Ware kuɗi na musamman, ɗaukar nauyi da shirya bibiyar tasirin annobar da kuma ɗaukar mataki ta la'akari da giɓin da aka samu a yayin wata annoba a baya. matakin da aka ɗauka kan Kwabid-19 'yar manuniya ce game irin nasarar da za a samu daga shugabanci da al'umma da tallafi. daidaito cikin wannan aiki na da muhimmanci domin shiryawa annobar. akwai buƙatar al'umma bakiɗaya ta ɗau matakin da zai tabbatar da nasarar ain da aka sa a gaba. ya kamata aiwatarwar ta ƙarfafi guiwar al'umma wajen gina tabbataccen tsari na yau da kullum da cin moriyar ƙarin dama ta ɗaura ɗamarar ko-ta-kwana. An yi wannan kira ne a lokacin zaburarwa da ɗaura ɗamarar tunƙarar duk wata barazana (PRET): Taron Tattaunawa kan Makomar Annobar Cutar Numfashi ta Duniya da aka yi a ranar 24 ga Afirilu a Geneva, Switzerland.
translations.reference: Increase connectivity among stakeholders in pandemic preparedness planning through systematic coordination and cooperation. This includes building equitable systems; conducting joint exercises; and sharing information on good practices, challenges, and opportunities. Dedicate sustained investments, financing and monitoring of pandemic preparedness with a particular focus on addressing the gaps identified during past pandemics and epidemics. The COVID-19 pandemic response has demonstrated what can be achieved with political commitment, community engagement and funding. At the heart of this work is to ensure equity to be ready for the next pandemic together. Whole-of-society action is needed to make the progress outlined in this Call to Action. Implementation should therefore strengthen the resilience of communities; maintain, sustain, and build on routine systems; and leverage broader capacities for emergency preparedness and response. This Call to Action was released at the Preparedness and Resilience for Emerging Threats (PRET): Global Meeting for Future Respiratory Pathogen Pandemics held on 24-26 April 2023 in Geneva, Switzerland.
translations.hypothesis: Promote collaboration between all relevant sectors in pandemic preparedness planning and coordination. This includes the development of common standards, the coordination of activities and the exchange of information on best practices, methodologies and resources. Allocate specific, timely funding and design monitoring and evaluation to learn from the pandemic and build on the gains made during the pandemic. The response to COVID-19 is a clear example of what can be achieved through strong political leadership, international coordination and solidarity. Equity in this process is vital to effective pandemic preparedness. The whole of society needs to take action to ensure an equitable and resilient recovery. This call to action is being issued during the fifth edition of Pandemic Prevention and Response Day (PPRD) which will take place on 24 April in Geneva, Switzerland.

translations.source: Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya ta yi kira da a ƙara yawan yadda ake amfani da abubuawan da za su taimaka wajen yaƙi da zazzaɓin cizon sauro a yayin Ranar Yaƙi da Zazzaɓin Cizon Sauro ta Duniya, Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya (WHO) ta yi kira da a ƙara ƙoƙari wajen amfani da sabbi da matakan da ake da su da wajen ceto rayuka daga zazzaɓin cizon sauro. Yara kusan miliyan 1.5 da ke fuskantar barazanar kamuwa ko rasa rai sabili da cutar maleriya daga ƙasashen Ghana, Kenya da Malawi, sun samu kashin farko na allurar rigakafin cutar maleriya RTS,S/AS01 (RTS,S). Godiya ga shirin na Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya. kashin farko na rigakafin maleriya wanda aka ƙaddamar a 2019 na cigaba da samar da hanyoyin kariya al'umma da kuma ceton rayuka. idan aka faɗaɗa shirin, Hukumar Lafiya ta duniya na ganin za a iya kai wa ga ceto rayukan dubun nan yara a kowacce shekara. a cewar darakta janar na Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya (WHO), muna da kayan kai ɗauki da za mu iya rage tasirin cutar maleriya da suka haɗa da: abin magance ƙwayoyin yaɗa cutar da magugunan rigakafi da na gwaje-gwaje da na maganin cutar. waɗannan sun ƙunshi ingantattun rigakafin cutar maleriya da za su kai ga ceton dubun nan yara a kowacce shekara. akwai yuwuwar kawo ƙarshen cutar maleriya a ƙasashe da dama, idan aka ƙara himma wajen cigaba da kai ɗauki ga waɗanda suka fi fuskantar baranaza. An yi wa ranar cutar maleriya ta duniya ta 2023 take da lokacin kawo ƙarshen maleriya bakiɗaya: zuba jari, fikira da ɗaukar mataki. Taken, wata hanya ce da Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya ke son yin kira wajen amfani da kayan aiki da sahihan hanyoyi domin hana kamuwa da ba da magungunan magance maleriya musamman a tsakanin talakawa.
translations.reference: WHO urges increased implementation of recommended tools to combat malaria Marking World Malaria Day, the World Health Organization (WHO) is issuing a call for increased implementation of new and existing interventions to save lives from malaria. Nearly 1.5 million children at high risk of illness and death from malaria in Ghana, Kenya and Malawi have now received their first dose of the first malaria vaccine, RTS,S/AS01 (RTS,S), thanks to an ongoing pilot programme coordinated by WHO. The malaria vaccine pilots, launched in 2019, are increasing equity in access to malaria prevention for the most vulnerable and are saving lives. If implemented broadly, WHO estimates that malaria vaccines could save the lives of tens of thousands of children each year. “We have the tools to drive down malaria, a package of interventions that includes vector control, preventive medicines, testing, and treatment,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of WHO. “These are joined by a safe and effective malaria vaccine, which could save the lives of tens of thousands children every year. With sustained investment and scaled-up efforts to reach those most at risk, malaria elimination in many countries is in reach. "World Malaria Day 2023 is being marked under the theme “Time to deliver zero malaria: invest, innovate, implement”. Within this theme, WHO is urging more effective implementation of available tools and strategies to prevent, diagnose and treat malaria, particularly among marginalized populations.
translations.hypothesis: WHO calls for innovative tools to bolster malaria response on World Malaria Day The World Health Organization (WHO) calls for a surge in innovation and implementation of life-saving tools to combat malaria. Children in Ghana, Kenya and Malawi, who are among the 1.5 million at-risk children who have now received the first dose of the RTS,S/AS01 (RTS,S) malaria vaccine, thanks to the WHO-supported Malaria Vaccine Implementation Programme. The first malaria vaccine, which was rolled out in 2019, continues to provide a safe and effective additional tool to reduce malaria cases and save lives. If implemented broadly, WHO estimates that the vaccine could prevent hundreds of thousands of child deaths each year. “We have a range of tools to reduce the malaria burden, including insecticide-treated nets, medicines, vaccines and diagnostics,” said Dr Michael Adekunle Charles, WHO Director of the Global Malaria Programme. “These include a powerful new vaccine that is expected to save hundreds of thousands of young lives each year. We can see the end of malaria in many countries, provided there is continued funding and commitment to the most vulnerable populations.” The theme for World Malaria Day 2023 is “Powering progress: Investment, innovation and impact.” The theme is a reminder of the need for WHO to use its convening power to rally stakeholders around a shared vision for malaria elimination and control, and to promote equitable access to malaria prevention and treatment tools, in particular for the most vulnerable populations.

translations.reference: According to the latest World malaria report, published in December 2022, there were an estimated 247 million new cases of malaria in 2021. The WHO African Region continues to shoulder the heaviest burden of the disease – accounting for an estimated 95% of all malaria cases (234 million) and 96% of all deaths (593 000) in 2021. Nearly 80% of malaria deaths in the African Region were among children under the age of five. New strategies and tools Countries have made some progress in expanding access to malaria services for most-at-risk populations. Despite some progress, many people at high risk of malaria still lack access to services that can prevent, detect and treat the disease. Challenges in expanding access to malaria services have been compounded, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, by the COVID-19 pandemic, converging humanitarian crises, restricted funding, weak surveillance systems, and declines in the effectiveness of core malaria-fighting tools. To address these threats and support countries in building more resilient malaria programmes, WHO recently published new strategies and frameworks, including: a new strategy to contain antimalarial drug resistance in Africa; a new initiative to stop the spread of Anopheles stephensi in urban environments;
translations.hypothesis: According to the latest global malaria report published in December 2022, there were an additional 247 million malaria cases in 2021. The WHO Region of Africa continues to carry the highest burden, with 95% of cases (234 million) and 96% of deaths (593 000) occurring in 2021. 80% of these deaths in the African Region are among children under 5 years of age, making malaria one of the deadliest diseases for young children globally. Innovative approaches and tools Some countries have successfully expanded coverage to populations at greatest risk of malaria. Despite this success, many communities remain vulnerable to malaria due to lack of access to prevention, detection and treatment services. Malaria funding has been severely impacted in recent years particularly in the sub-Saharan Africa region due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the global economic downturn, and consequential funding shortfalls, inattention and insufficient resources to fight malaria. Recently, WHO published new guidelines and recommendations on key interventions for malaria control, including: new recommendations on the use of malaria vaccines in Africa; environmental management;

Nau'in rigakafin maleriya na biyu, R21/Matrix-M (R21), zai iya taimakawa wajen wadatuwarsa ga masaya tare da rage yawan yara masu fama da zazzaɓi da ransa rai saboda cutar ta maleriya. abu ne mai muhimmanci ga Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya cigaba da binciken kwakwaf kan nau'in rigakafin maleriya na R21 har sai ta samu rahoton ƙarin tabbaci game da ingancin bayanai kan gwajin R21 karo na uku da ake yi da zarar an kammala. ana sa ran kai rigakafin maleriya na RTSS zuwa wasu ƙasashen Afirka a farkon shekarar 2024.
translations.reference: a new framework, developed jointly by WHO and UN-Habitat, to guide city leaders in urban malaria control. a new toolkit to help countries assess their malaria surveillance systems and identify areas for investment WHO has also increased the transparency, flexibility and access to its malaria recommendations. The consolidated WHO Guidelines for malaria are now available through two digital platforms: MAGICapp and the “Malaria Toolkit” app. WHO encourages countries to tailor the recommendations to local disease settings for maximum impact. Prospects for new interventions Continued investment in the development and deployment of new malaria vaccines and next-generation tools will be key to achieving the 2030 global malaria targets. A second malaria vaccine, the R21/Matrix-M (R21) vaccine, if approved, could help close the sizable gap between supply and demand and further reduce child illness and death from malaria. It is a priority for WHO to continue the thorough and efficient expert review of the R21 malaria vaccine once additional key safety and efficacy data from the ongoing R21 phase 3 trial are available and provided to WHO. Phased introductions of the RTS,S malaria vaccine in additional countries in Africa are expected to begin in early 2024.
translations.hypothesis: A new partnership between WHO and the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) will help countries to procure and implement malaria control programmes in urban settings. New tools to help countries measure malaria burden and target investments WHO is expanding access to its malaria policy recommendations. WHO’s policy recommendations are available through two apps: the MAGICapp and the Malaria Toolkit. Countries can now respond to WHO’s policy recommendations to increase access to WHO recommended malaria interventions. Innovative delivery approaches Accelerating the development and deployment of new malaria vaccines and advanced technologies is key to achieving the goal of malaria eradication by 2030. The second malaria vaccine, R21/Matrix-M (R21), can help bolster prevention efforts and reduce the burden of malaria-related illness and death in children. It is important that WHO continues to review evidence on the R21 malaria vaccine until a full report on the third and final phase of R21 clinical trials becomes available. The RTS,S malaria vaccine is expected to become available to countries in early 2024.

translations.reference: In the vector control space, there are 28 new products in the R&D pipeline. Tools under evaluation include, for example, new types of insecticide-treated nets, targeted baits that attract mosquitoes, spatial repellents, lethal house lures (eaves tubes) and genetic engineering of mosquitoes. Researchers are prioritizing the development of non-ACT treatments in the field of antimalarial medicines due to the emergence and spread of partial artemisinin resistance. The development of next-generation medicines, such as "triple ACTs," which use a combination of artemisinin and two partner drugs, is underway to reduce the risk of drug resistance. translations.hypothesis: There are new products in the insecticide resistance management toolbox. These include new insecticides, new formulations of existing insecticides, insecticide-treated mosquito nets, spatial repellents and larvicides/pupicides. There is a continued need for new antimalarial drug targets and compounds that are not ACT-based due to the limitations of artemisinin. The development of new medicines that are expected to be rolled out in the coming years, such as triple ACTs (containing artemisinin and two other medicines), is expected to reduce the risk of treatment failure. translations.source: Shirin Kamfanin Musayar Fasaha ta mRNA ya shiga mataki na biyu a cigaban da yake samu. za a ƙaddamar da Kamfanin Fasaha na mRNA a Afrigen, a Afrika ta Kudu. abokan haɗin guiwar za su haɗu ne a garin Cape Town domin tattauna mataki na gaba na cigaba da musayar ilimi game da rigakafin mRNA. sama da mutane 200 masu ba da gudumuwa daga faɗin duniya da ke aiki da Kamfanin Musayar Fasaha ta mRNA ne za su haɗu a wannan sati a Cape Town domin ganawa kai tsaye da juna. darakta-janar na Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya (WHO), Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus da Ministan Lafiya, Dr. Joe Phaahla, da Ministan Kasuwanci da Masana'antu, Mr. Ebrahim Patel na Afirka ta Kudu tare da manyan jami'ai daga ƙasashen da ke ba da tallafi; duk sun haɗu a wurin taron domin sake duba irin cigaban da aka samu tun bayan da Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya da Kanfanin Haɗa Magungunan suka ƙaddamar da ita a 2021. Na yi farin cikin kasancewa a nan Cape Town tare da abokan haɗin guiwa na samar da shiri mai ɗorewa na Kamfanin Musayar Fasaha ta mRNA domin tallafawa ƙasashe masu ƙaramin ƙarfi wajen samun rigafi da sauran magunguna inganta lafiya kamar kowa; a cewar darakta-janar na Hukumar Lafiya ta Duniya, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. Ina alfahari da duk waɗanda suka ba da gudunmuwa a wannan aiki wajen samun nasara cikin abin da bai wuce shekara biyu ba wanda hakan ke tabbatar da cewa idan aka yi aiki bakiɗaya, za mu samu nasara tare. taron ya haɗa da masu haɗin guiwa daga kamfanin kimiyya daga ƙasashe 15 da ke cikin shirin, da ƙwararru da masana'antu da wakilan al'umma da masu zuba hannun jari. Ana sa ran a yayin wannan taro na kwanaki biyar, mahalarta taron za su yi musayar hanyoyin samar da cigaba ɗorawar shirin kamar batu na haƙƙin mallaka da dokokin gudanarwa da fasahar mRNA da muhimman hanyoyin LMICs da suka shafi wasu cututtuka kamar cuta mai karya garkuwar jiki da kuma tarin fuka. Annobar Kwabid-19 ta yi matuƙar fallasa mummunan rashin daidaito na neman lafiya, musamman game da rigakafi.
translations.reference: mRNA Technology Transfer Programme moves to the next phase of its development Inauguration of the mRNA technology Hub facility at Afrigen, South Africa. Partners gather in Cape Town to discuss the next phase of the mRNA vaccine development and knowledge sharing. Over 200 international participants working with the mRNA Technology Transfer Programme met in Cape Town this week for their first face-to-face meeting. Joined by World Health Organization (WHO) Director General, Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus and Dr. Joe Phaahla, Minister of Health and Minister of Trade and Industry, Mr. Ebrahim Patel of South Africa together with high-level officials from funding countries, this unique meeting reviewed the progress since WHO and Medicines Patent Pool (MPP) launched it in June 2021. “I am delighted to be here in Cape Town with our partners to support a sustainable model for mRNA technology transfer to give low- and middle-income countries equitable access to vaccines and other lifesaving health products,” said WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. “I am immensely proud of the achievement of all those involved in this project; in less than two years we have shown that when we work collaboratively, we succeed collectively.” The meeting participants include biomanufacturing partners from 15 countries in the Programme, leading experts, industry, civil society representatives, and funders. During the five-day meeting, participants will share progress and discuss critical enablers for the sustainability of the Programme such as intellectual property issues and regulatory aspects, as well as the science of mRNA technologies and key applications relevant to LMICs in other disease areas such as HIV and tuberculosis. The COVID-19 pandemic has underscored that gross inequity exists in access to health products, especially vaccines.
translations.hypothesis: The mRNA vaccine technology transfer programme has reached a major milestone. The Afrigen mRNA vaccine facility in Cape Town, South Africa, has successfully completed technology transfer from BioNTech. Partners met in Cape Town to discuss the next steps in advancing mRNA vaccine technology and access. More than 200 contributors from around the world who are working on mRNA vaccine technology will come together this week in Cape Town for an in-person meeting. The meeting was also attended by WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus; the South African Minister of Health, Dr Joe Phaahla; the South African Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition, Mr Ebrahim Patel; and senior officials from countries supporting the initiative; all of whom noted the significant progress made since the launch of the mRNA vaccine technology transfer initiative by WHO and partners in 2021. “I am delighted to be here in Cape Town with our partners in the mRNA vaccine technology transfer programme to support low- and middle-income countries to have equitable access to vaccines and other health products,” said WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. “I am proud of everyone who contributed to this effort, which proved that, working together, we can go far and achieve much in just two years.” The Summit brings together partners from 15 countries where the initiative is running, along with experts, industry, philanthropy and other stakeholders. Over the course of the five-day meeting, participants will discuss and chart ways to improve access to mRNA vaccine technology, including intellectual property and regulatory issues, and the application of mRNA technology to other high-priority diseases in LMICs, such as HIV and TB. The COVID-19 pandemic also revealed the deep inequities in access to health, most acutely for vaccines.

translations.source: Tun bayan ayyana Kwabid-19 a matsayin lamarin da ya shafi lafiya da ke buƙata kulawar gaggawa a duniya a watan Maris ɗin 2023, kawo 69.7 cikin ɗari na al'umma ne a faɗin duniya suka kai ga samun aƙalla ƙunshi ɗaya na rigakafin Kwabid-19. Abin lura shi ne kaso 30% na wancan adadi sun fito ne daga ƙasashe masu ƙaramin ƙarfi (LICs). Manufar wannan shiri shi ne ba da gudunmawa ta baiɗaya wajen samun rigakafin nRNA ta hanyar ninƙa samar da rigakafin a tsakankanin LMICs da ƙarfafa haɗin guiwa a tsakanin yanki da sauran yankuna da bunƙasawa da ƙarfafa wa masu aiki na ƙasa ta hanyar ba su horo da tallafi. Abin burgewa game da Tsarin Musayar Fasaha shi ne tsarin sanya kowa cikin samun damar musayar fasaha ga mutane daban-daban wajen iya samar da rigakafin domin isa ga masu buƙata cikin sauri. A cewar dakta Phaahla, ministan Lafiya na Afirka ta Kudu; abin da muke gani a yau abu ne na tarihi, shiri ne da manufarsa karfafa wa LMICs da ke faɗin Duniya ta hanyar haɗin guiwa. Na yi matuƙar farin cikin ganin cigaban da aka samu a ƙankanin lokaci tare da yin maraba da tallafi da aka samu daga ƙasashe da dama kamar Afirka ta Kudu da ke da Kanfanin Kimiyyar Halittu da kuma ƙoƙarinta na ganin ta koya tare da musayar ilimi a kowa. a cewar ministan Ilimi Mai Zurfi da Kimiyya, Blade Nzimande, mafarkinmu game da Shirin Musayar Fasaha ta mRNA shi ne ta zarce batun Kwabid-19 kaɗai. Muna ƙoƙarin samar da yanayi ne da zai ba mu dama a nan gaba mu iya fuskantar kowacce annoba ta hanyar samar da rigakafinta daga fasahar mRNA. Wannan hangen nesa ne da aka yi kan cututtukan da suka zama gama-gari ga al'ummarmu kamar maleriya da tarin fuka da cuta mai karya garkuwar jiki (HIV da AIDS). Haka kuma wannan taro ya fito da muhimmancin shirin da aka ƙaddamar na Fasahar mRNA da aka yi a Afrigen da ke Cape Town a idon Dakta Tedros da Dakta Matshidiso Moeti wanda darakta ne na Yankin Afirka a Majalisar Ɗinkin Duniya da Charles Gore, babban darkta na MPP da kuma ministoci waɗanda suka sa hannu wajen yanka ribon na bikin kaddamarwar.
translations.reference: As of March 2023, more than three years after WHO declared COVID-19 a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), 69.7% of the global population had received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. Notably, this proportion still remains below 30% in low-income countries (LICs) . This Programme aims to contribute to equitable access to mRNA vaccines by increasing the distribution of sustainable manufacturing capacity across LMICs, enhancing regional and inter-regional collaborations, and developing and empowering a local workforce through tailored and inclusive training and expert support. What is unique in the mRNA Technology Transfer model is the multilateral process that allows sharing of technologies to multiple recipients so that through local and regional production those in need can be reached rapidly. Dr Phaahla, Minister of Health South Africa, said: “What we see here today, is a moment in history, a Programme that is aimed at empowering LMICs through a global collaborative network. I am thrilled to see the progress made in such a relatively short time and welcome the support from so many different countries - countries like South Africa that have a strong vibrant biomanufacturing capacity and that are willing to work together, learn from and share with each other.” Minister Blade Nzimande of Higher Education and Science, said: “Ours is the vision of the mRNA Technology Transfer Hub beyond just COVID-19. The capabilities we are building are looking to empower us to deal with other future pandemics whose vaccines could use the same mRNA technology platform. It is a vision that has set its eyes on diseases that are prevalent in our environments such as Malaria, Tuberculosis and HIV and AIDS.” This occasion also marks an important milestone for the Programme with the inauguration of the mRNA technology Hub facility at Afrigen in Cape Town in the presence of Dr. Tedros and Dr. Matshidiso Moeti WHO Regional Director for Africa, Charles Gore Executive Director of MPP and the Honorable Ministers who took part in a ribbon cutting ceremony at Afrigen.
translations.hypothesis: Since the declaration of COVID-19 as a PHEIC in March 2020, global cumulative COVID-19 vaccination coverage has reached 69.7%. Of note, 30% of this number was achieved in LICs. The purpose of this programme is to facilitate equitable access to mRNA vaccine technology by supporting regional vaccine manufacturing, empowering regional collaboration and strengthening national capacities through knowledge sharing and technical assistance. The benefit of the Technology Transfer Initiative is the empowerment of individuals to develop vaccines and diagnostics for their own communities. “What we are seeing today is historic, a program designed to strengthen LMICs around the world through collaboration. I am thrilled by the progress made in such a short time and the support received from nations such as South Africa, which has a robust bioscience industry, and its willingness to share its expertise and knowledge. Our dream for the mRNA vaccine technology platform is much bigger than COVID-19,” said Minister of Higher Education, Science and Innovation, Blade Nzimande. “We are trying to create a situation where we can, in the future, more easily and quickly respond to any epidemic by developing a vaccine based on mRNA technology.” This vision extends to diseases that are endemic in our communities, such as malaria, tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS. The success of this meeting also underscored the importance of the mRNA vaccine technology transfer initiative undertaken by Afrigen in Cape Town, South Africa, and supported by Dr Tedros, Dr Matshidiso Moeti, WHO Regional Director for Africa, Charles Gore, CEO of MPP, and the ministers who signed the non-binding letter of intent at the launch event.

translations.source: Babban Darkta na Afrigen, farfesa Petro Terblanche cewa ya yi, ɗaukacin ma'aikatan Afrigen sun yi farin ciki na cimma wannan gagarumin mataki na kammala tsarin shirin Fasahar mRNA. wannan wuri yana ɗauke da kayayyakin samar da rigakafin mRNA na Kwabid-19 samfurin AfriVac 2121 wanda ake matakin dab da kammala haɗa shi. Sama da watanni 18 Afrigen ke samun cigaba ta hanyar tallafi daga masu haɗin guiwa da mashawarta na wannan shiri. Ƙoƙarinmu na ƙaruwa domin kai wa ga ƙolokuwar mataki na inganci na rigakafin mRNA wanda ginshiƙi ga LMICs mai ɗorewa wajen samar da rigakafin mRNA. Afrigen ta samu nasarar samar da ɗakin gwajin rigakafin Kwabid-19 kuma a yanzu tare da samar da ingantattun ƙananan cibiyoyin samar da rigakafin da za a yi amfani da su a mataki na I da na II na gwaji domin kai wa ga ingancin GMP. Ban da wannan, Afrigen za ta cigaba da ba da horaswa da musayar fasaha ga 'yan abokan haɗin guiwarsu. Msu ba da tallafi sun taka muhimmiyar rawa wajen taimaka wa shirin da tallafin da ya kai Dala 117 zuwa yanzu kuma Faransa ce ta farko wajen fara ba da tallafin ga shirin musayar na mRNA. A wajen taron akwai wakilan Ƙungiyar Tarayyar Turai da suka haɗa da Belgium da Germany da Norway da Canada da Kungiyar Tarayyar Afirka da Afirka ta Kudu da Gidauniyar ELMA. Darakta-janar ta Al'amuran Yau da Kullum ta ƙasa Kanada a Kudanci da Gabashin Afirka, Caroline Delany ta ce; Kanada na ba da tabbacin cigaba da tallafawa shirin Musayar Fasaha ta mRNA, kuma a yau muna farin cikin sanar da ƙarin gudunmowa ta miliyan 15 na kuɗin ƙasar. Da haka jumular gudunmowar da Canada ta ba wa shirin ya kai Dalar Canada miliyan 45.
translations.reference: Professor Petro Terblanche, Executive Director of Afrigen said: “The entire Afrigen team are thrilled to reach this important milestone with the completion of the mRNA technology platform. This platform is housed within the end-to-end mRNA vaccine development and production facility where the mRNA Hub Covid 19 vaccine candidate AfriVac 2121 is currently in scale-up phase. Over the last 18 months, Afrigen has undergone an incredible transformation with the support of a network of partners and mentors enabled by this Programme. We have grown our capability and capacity to meet the highest quality standards of mRNA vaccine development, serving the objective to build sustainable capacity in LMICs to produce mRNA vaccines”. Afrigen has successfully established a COVID-19 vaccine manufacturing process at a laboratory scale and is currently scaling up that process to a level suitable for manufacturing vaccine batches to be used in Phase I/ II clinical trials to GMP standards. In a parallel process, Afrigen will continue to carry out training and technology transfer to the network partners. The funders play a crucial role in supporting the Programme with total funding to date at US$ 117 million and France being the first to fund the mRNA technology transfer work. Present at the meeting were representatives from the European Commission, Belgium, Germany, as well as Norway, Canada, African Union, South Africa, and the ELMA Foundation. Caroline Delany, GlobalAffairs Canada’s Director General for Southern and Eastern Africa said: “Canada reaffirms its continued support of the mRNA Technology Transfer Programme and we are delighted to announce a further contribution of 15 million Canadian dollars at the meeting today. This brings Canada’s total contribution to the Programme up to 45 million Canadian dollars.
translations.hypothesis: Darko Atafeno, CEO of Afrigen, said all employees at Afrigen are excited about reaching this milestone in the development of our mRNA vaccine programme. This platform now contains the manufacturing process for an existing COVID-19 vaccine, the prototype for an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine, AfriVac 2121, which is in late preclinical development. Afrigen has received support from partners and donors over the past 18 months to advance this programme. Our efforts are aimed at achieving economies of scale to make mRNA vaccine technology more accessible and affordable for LMICs to sustainably produce mRNA vaccines. Afrigen has successfully developed a COVID-19 vaccine candidate and now has a GMP-qualified manufacturing facility suitable for use in Phase I and II clinical trials. Additionally, Afrigen will provide technical training and knowledge transfer to its partners. The support they have provided has been invaluable, with funding totalling US$ 117 million to date, and France is the first country to provide funding for the mRNA technology transfer programme. The event was attended by representatives from the European Union, Belgium, Germany, Norway, Canada, the African Union, South Africa, and the ELMA Foundation. “Canada is committed to supporting the mRNA technology transfer initiative, and I am pleased to announce today a contribution of C$15 million towards this effort,” said Caroline Mulroney, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, Canada. “This brings Canada’s total contribution to C$45 million.

translations.source: Waɗannan kuɗaɗe ana amfani da su ne wajen kula da cibiyar a ƙasar Afirka Kudu da kuma sauran masu haɗin guiwa a faɗin duniya. a cewar mataimakin babban darkta na Ƙungiyar Tarayyar Turai, Mr. Martin Seychell, mun yarda da muhimmancin nuna ƙoƙarinmu a matakin gida zuwa sauran yankuna. EC ta riga ta bayar da gudunmawar miliyan 40 domin samar da Cibiyar Musayar Fasaha ta mRNA kuma ta sanya hannun ba da wani tallafin tare da EIB na miliyan 155 domin taimaka wa yunƙurin faɗaɗa ƙarfin samar da rigakafin. translations.reference: Key leadership appointments made to drive WHO strategic direction and initiatives The World Health Organization (WHO) has appointed five new senior figures to its headquarters leadership team in Geneva. The new appointments follow the reappointment of Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus to his second five-year term as Director-General. The overall leadership team has been consolidated to align with the Organization’s priorities for the next five years and will work closely with the Director-General to drive forward these priorities and WHO’s ambitious transformation agenda. To accelerate progress on implementation of WHO’s 13th General Programme of Work (GPW13), and achievement of its “triple billion” targets and the health-related Sustainable Development Goals, WHO’s work for the coming five years is focused on five priorities: making a paradigm shift towards promoting health and preventing disease by addressing its root causes; radically reorienting health systems towards primary health care; strengthening the systems for health emergency preparedness and response; harnessing the power of science, innovation, data and technologies to advance health; and strengthening WHO as the leading authority on global health and to achieve impact in countries.
translations.hypothesis: 143 positions filled to drive WHO's work WHO has appointed five new senior staff to its headquarters in Geneva. To ensure the effective implementation of its Thirteenth General Programme of Work (GPW13) and mobilize the necessary financial resources to achieve the health-related aims of the Sustainable Development Goals, WHO will focus on five key priorities: 1. Reorienting health systems to prioritize primary health care as a resilient foundation for universal health coverage and protection in health emergencies. 2. Strengthening preparedness for and resilience to health emergencies. 3. Harnessing the power of science, innovation, data and digital technologies to accelerate progress on health and strengthen WHO’s role as the health cluster lead in global emergencies.

He leads WHO’s response to disease outbreaks, humanitarian crises and other public health emergencies. Dr Ryan is a founding member of the Global Outbreak Alert and Response Network (GOARN), which has aided the response to hundreds of disease outbreaks around the world.

translations.source: Dakta Ryan yana da digirin farko a fannin likitanci da kuma digiri na biyu a fannin lafiyar jama'a. Mista Raul Thomas zai ci gaba da zama Mataimakin Darakta Janar na Ayyukan Kasuwanci. Mista Thomas yana da cikakken alhakin ayyukan kasuwanci na Hukumar WHO, gami da kasafin kuɗi, yawan ma'aikata, gudanarwa, binciken gujewa haɗari, lissafi da bin doka, da gudanarwa gabaɗaya. Shi ne ke da alhakin aiwatar da yawancin tsare-tsare a ƙarƙashin ajandar canji na Ƙungiya da ƙirƙirar wurin aiki mai mutuntawa da kuma haɗin kan aiki. A tsawon shekaru 20 da ya yi yana aiki tare da Hukumar WHO, Mista Thomas ya yi aiki a yankunan Afirka, Amurka, Gabashin Bahar Rum da Yammacin Pacific, da kuma Hukumar Bincike kan cutar daji(IARC). Mista Thomas yana da digiri na biyu a fannin sarrafa ƙungiyoyi da digiri na farko a fannin gudanar da kasuwanci.

translations.source: Rahoton taron Ƙungiyar Ba da Shawarwari na Fasaha ta Hukumar WHO kan Tsarin rigakafin cutar COVID-19 (TAG-CO-VAC) wanda aka gudanar a ranakun 16-17 ga watan Maris 2023 A cikin watan Yunin 2022, TAG-CO-VAC ta buga wata sanarwa ta wucin gadi wacce ke nuna cewa allurar rigakafin ƙwayoyin cutar sun ci gaba da ba da babban matakan kariya daga mummunan cutar da duk SARS-CoV-2 Variants of Concern (VOCs) ke haifarwa, gami da Omicron. Duk da haka, idan aka yi la'akari da sinadarin daidaita garkuwar jiki, an gano cewar akwai rashin tabbas akan cewar allurar Rigakafin TAG-CO-VAC zai cigaba da tasiri bayan wani ɗan lokaci. A don haka masu bayar da shawarwari akan TAG-CO-VAC ta shawarci masu ƙera alluran rigakafi da hukumomin da ke kula da su, da a su yi la’akari da sabunta sinadaran da ke tattare da maganin rigakafi ta hanyar haɗawa da sinadarin Omicron, a matsayin sa na sinadari mafi ƙarfi wajen yaƙar duk wasu nau'ukan cutar SARS-CoV-2 a matsayin maganin samar da kuzari. Masu ƙera alluran rigakafi da yawa sun haɓaka rigakafin COVID-19 tare da sabunta abubuwan antigenic; wannan ya haɗa da alluran rigakafin mRNA da yawa waɗanda ke ƙunshe da nau'ukan Omicron na farko, ban da ƙwayar cuta mai ƙididdigewa (watau ƙwayar cuta + BA.1 ko BA.4/5), waɗanda hukumomin gudanarwa suka bayar da izini don amfanin gaggawa dasu. A ranakun 16-17 ga watan Maris ɗin 2023, kwamitin TAG-CO-VAC ya sake zama a Muscat, wato babban birnin ƙasar Oman. Maƙasudin taron ya kasu kashi biyu: Domin sake nazarin shaida kan ayyukan sabbin rigakafin cutar COVID-19 waɗanda suka haɗa nau'ukan sinadarin Omicron a matsayin sinadarin ƙarin kuzari Domin kafa jadawalin lokaci don shawarwarin haɗa magungunan rigakafin COVID-19 a cikin shekarar 2023. Shaidar nazarin da kwamitin TAG-CO-VAC ta sake dubawa don tantance ayyukan sabbin rigakafin cutar COVID-19 waɗanda suka haɗa nau'ukan Omicron sun haɗa da:
translations.reference: Report of the meeting of the WHO Technical Advisory Group on COVID-19 Vaccine Composition (TAG-CO-VAC) held on 16-17 March 2023 In June 2022, the TAG-CO-VAC published an interim statement highlighting that index virus-based vaccines continued to confer high levels of protection against severe disease caused by all SARS-CoV-2 Variants of Concern (VOCs), including Omicron. However, given the antigenic distance and uncertainties of further viral evolution, the TAG-CO-VAC recognized that it was likely that the effectiveness of vaccines based on the index virus would reduce over time. The TAG-CO-VAC therefore advised vaccine manufacturers and regulatory authorities to consider an update of vaccine antigen composition by including Omicron, as the most antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 variant thus far, for administration as a booster dose. Multiple vaccine manufacturers have developed COVID-19 vaccines with an updated antigenic composition; this includes several bivalent mRNA-based vaccines containing earlier Omicron descendent lineages, in addition to the index virus (i.e., index virus + BA.1 or BA.4/5), which have been authorized for emergency use by regulatory authorities. On 16-17 March 2023, the TAG-CO-VAC reconvened in Muscat, Oman. The purpose of the meeting was two-fold: to review the evidence on the performance of updated COVID-19 vaccines that incorporate descendent lineages of Omicron as a booster dose; and to establish timelines for COVID-19 vaccine composition recommendations in 2023. The evidence reviewed by the TAG-CO-VAC to assess the performance of updated COVID-19 vaccines that incorporated descendent lineages of Omicron included:
translations.hypothesis: Statement on the fifteenth meeting of the WHO Technical Advisory Group on COVID-19 Vaccine Composition (TAG-CO-VAC) held on 16 and 17 March 2023 In June 2022, the TAG-CO-VAC published a statement indicating that currently approved vaccines continue to provide substantial protection against severe disease caused by SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern (VOCs), including Omicron. However, based on the kinetics of immune responses, there is some uncertainty about the duration of protection conferred by TAG-CO-VAC recommended vaccines. Therefore, the TAG-CO-VAC advises vaccine manufacturers and regulatory agencies to consider updating vaccine antigens to include an Omicron-descendant lineage as the monovalent vaccine antigen. Several vaccine manufacturers have developed COVID-19 vaccines with updated antigen composition; these include several mRNA vaccines that contain an Omicron BA.1- or BA.4/5- descendent lineage, and which have been approved for emergency use listing by WHO. The fifteenth meeting of the TAG-CO-VAC was held on 16 and 17 March 2023 in Muscat, Oman. The objectives of the meeting were twofold: to review the evidence on the performance of new COVID-19 vaccines that include Omicron-descendant lineages as the vaccine antigen; and to provide advice on the timing of updates to COVID-19 vaccine antigen composition in 2023. Evidence reviewed The published and unpublished evidence reviewed by the TAG-CO-VAC to inform its advice on the performance of new COVID-19 vaccines that include Omicron descendent lineages includes:

translations.source: (1) An wallafa nazarin cututtukan lura da ƙididdiga na cikakkiyar tasirin maganin rigakafi na BA.1- ko BA.4/5 mai ɗauke da bivalent mRNA alluran rigakafin da aka yi amfani da su a matsayin masu ƙara kuzari akan alamun bayyanar cututtuka da cuta mai tsanani; (2) Bayanan da aka samu akan ɗakin gwaje-gwaje kan girma da faɗin martanin rigakafin na gaba da yaɗuwa da cututtuka mabanbanta masu alaƙa da cutar SARS-CoV-2 waɗanda BA.1- ko BA.4/5- na ɗauke da allurar mRNA, idan aka kwatanta da ƙwayar cuta ta index idan aka kwatanta su da maganin rigakafin da ake amfani da su a matsayin masu ƙara kuzari (3) Nazarin ɗakin gwaje-gwaje da bayanan lura da martanin ƙwaƙwalwar ajiyar rigakafi don kimanta tasirin maimaitawar antigen akan rigakafi da kuma irin kariya da take samarwa. Ana iya samun ƙarin cikakkun bayanai kan shaidar da kwamitin TAG-CO-VAC tayi nazari akai a cikin wasu kundi na nan daba. Dangane da bitar bayanan da aka kwatanta daga farko, kwamitin TAG-CO-VAC ya yanke shawarar: Ƙara yawan allurai na tushen ƙwayoyin cuta suna ci gaba da ba da manyan matakan kariya daga mummunan cutar da rasa rayuka waɗanda duk cututtuka mabanbanta na nau'ukan cutar SARS-CoV-2 suka haifar, gami da nau'ukan sinadarin Omicron na tsawon lokaci. Kariya daga cututtuka masu tsanani da kamuwa da cutar ke haifarwa ta hanyar alluran rigakafin ƙwayoyin cuta da BA.1- ko BA.4/5 mai ɗauke da bivalent mRNA na raguwa akan lokaci. Duk da haka, ana samun kariya daga cututtuka mai tsanani fiye da kariyar da ake samu daga cututtuka masu saurin yaɗuwa. Idan aka kwatanta da alluran rigakafi na tushen ƙwayoyin cuta, masu haɓaka allurai na BA.1- ko BA.4/5-mai ɗauke da bivalent mRNA alluran rigakafi na iya haɓaka tasirin alluran rigakafi a kan bayyanar cututtuka, yayin da ƙaramin adadin binciken da ke tantance sakamako mai tsanani yana nuna ƙididdiga iri ɗaya na rigakafin. Sinadaran BA.1- da BA.4/5-masu ɗauke da bivalent mRNA na alluran rigakafin suna haifar da mafi girman martanin rigakafi ga cututtuka mabambanta nau'ukan SARS-CoV-2 a lokacin da aka yi amfani da su wajen ƙarin kuzari, idan aka kwatanta da ƙwayar cutar tushen alluran rigakafi.
translations.reference: (1) published observational epidemiological studies of estimates of absolute and relative vaccine effectiveness of BA.1- or BA.4/5-containing bivalent mRNA vaccines used as a booster dose against symptomatic and severe disease; (2) laboratory-based data on the magnitude and breadth of cross-reactive immune responses against previous and circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants induced by BA.1- or BA.4/5- containing mRNA vaccines, as compared to index virus-based vaccines, used as a booster dose; and (3) laboratory-based studies and observational data on immune memory responses to evaluate the impact of repeated antigen exposure on vaccine-induced immunity and protection. Further details on the evidence reviewed by the TAG-CO-VAC can be found in the accompanying annex. Based on the review of the data described above, the TAG-CO-VAC concludes: Booster doses of index virus-based vaccines continue to confer high levels of protection against severe disease and death caused by all SARS-CoV-2 variants, including contemporary Omicron descendent lineages. Protection from severe disease and symptomatic infection induced by index virus-based vaccines and BA.1- or BA.4/5-containing bivalent mRNA vaccines declines over time. However, protection from severe disease is maintained longer than protection from symptomatic infection. As compared to index virus-based vaccines, booster doses of BA.1- or BA.4/5-containing bivalent mRNA vaccines may modestly increase vaccine effectiveness against symptomatic disease, while the small number of studies assessing severe outcomes show similar estimates of vaccine effectiveness. Both BA.1- and BA.4/5-containing bivalent mRNA vaccines enhance the magnitude and elicit greater breadth of cross-reactive immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 variants when used as a booster dose, as compared to the index virus-based vaccines.
translations.hypothesis: (1) published observational studies and a systematic review of the available evidence on the clinical and epidemiological effectiveness of bivalent (BA.1- or BA.4/5- containing) mRNA vaccines used as index vaccines in primary immunization series; (2) published data on the performance of monovalent BA.1- or BA.4/5- containing mRNA vaccines against symptomatic disease and severe disease across a range of SARS-CoV-2 variants, compared to index virus-based vaccines used in the primary series; (3) in vitro data on cross-reactivity and neutralizing antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 variants, to assess the impact of repeated exposure to index antigen on immune responses and the breadth of protection. Further details on the evidence reviewed by the TAG-CO-VAC can be found in the accompanying data annex. Based on the publicly available data reviewed, the TAG-CO-VAC advises: Monovalent vaccines continue to provide substantial protection against severe disease and death caused by SARS-CoV-2, including all Omicron sub-lineages, over time. Protection against severe disease and hospitalization conferred by bivalent (BA.1- or BA.4/5- containing) mRNA vaccines wanes over time. However, protection against severe disease is maintained to a greater extent than protection against symptomatic disease. Compared to index virus-based vaccines, monovalent BA.1- or BA.4/5- containing mRNA vaccines may improve vaccine effectiveness against symptomatic disease, while fewer studies evaluate severe outcomes and the available evidence is consistent for a similar VE against severe disease. Bivalent (BA.1- or BA.4/5- containing) mRNA vaccines induce higher neutralizing antibody responses to circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants, compared to monovalent index virus vaccines.

translations.source: BA.4/5 mai ƙunshe da alluran rigakafin mRNA na bivalent sun haifar da mafi girma daidaiton titres antibody a kan kwanan nan na nau'ukan Omicron (BQ.1, XBB.1) idan aka kwatanta da BA.1-ɗauke da bivalent mRNA alluran rigakafi, lokacin da aka yi amfani da matsayin mai ƙara kuzari.
translations.reference: BA.4/5-containing bivalent mRNA vaccines induced higher neutralizing antibody titres against recent descendent lineages of Omicron (BQ.1, XBB.1) as compared to BA.1-containing bivalent mRNA vaccines, when used as a booster dose.
translations.hypothesis: Bivalent (BA.4/5) mRNA vaccines elicited higher neutralizing antibody titres against recent Omicron sub-lineages (BQ.1, XBB.1) as compared to bivalent (BA.1) mRNA vaccines, when used in a monovalent format.
